entries.title: Build a portfolio that can survive the journey
entries.text: portfolio-actions Build a portfolio that can survive the journey Portfolio A sound long-term idea still needs enough liquidity and manageable concentration to survive difficult periods. JPMorgan’s drawdown chart covers full calendar years from 1980 to 2025. It reports an average intra-year decline of 14.2%, while 35 of the 46 years finished with positive price returns. The 2026 bar is year to date and is outside that full-year count. These are price returns, not returns including reinvested dividends. The lesson is about the route taken, not a guarantee of recovery. A good year can contain a frightening decline. A diversified index’s historical pattern does not imply that every individual share recovers, that every downturn is short, or that leverage is safe. Forced selling can make an interim loss permanent for the investor who must exit. Diversification should address sources of risk rather than product count. Inflation or interest-rate shocks can hurt stocks and long bonds together. AI-linked equities and AI-linked private lending can share a cash-flow driver. An offshore bond and a CHF loan introduce two currency exposures, and their movements should not be assumed to offset. For a reader deciding what to do, separate money by purpose before selecting products. Near-term spending requires dependable liquidity in the spending currency. Long-term growth capital can tolerate a different path. Income assets should be assessed for cash quality, while duration positions need a clear holding horizon and loss tolerance. Use rebalancing to maintain the chosen risk profile rather than allowing winners to determine it unintentionally. Review correlated exposures across direct holdings and funds. For borrowing, use the actual facility rules and stress asset prices, loan FX and financing rates together; the reports do not supply proprietary recognition rules or client-specific margin limits. The strategy implication is conditional: preserve the capacity to stay invested when the investment case remains sound, while retaining the flexibility to change course when evidence changes. This follows from the mechanics and historical evidence; it is not a recommendation to buy a particular security or copy an institution’s portfolio. A plan should fit the uncomfortable middle of the journey, not only the outcome you hope to reach at the end. Historical averages and previous recoveries are not a minimum future return or a deadline for the next recovery. Review cash needs, underlying concentration, duration, credit compensation, currency mismatch and funding resilience together. Record what evidence would change the investment case. jpm-markets jpm-alternatives mas-macro jpm-gtm-p16 Interpretation and practical monitoring

Previously published sourced notes and upcoming-event notices are retained with their original dates. Narrative coverage is partial; no new item verified is not evidence of no news. Reuters price observations at 20:07 SGT, published at 20:34 SGT, precede the separate later quote snapshots on the company cards. Micron and Broadcom investor-relations pages were unavailable during the research check; Meta coverage was partial and some Reuters syndication pages were inaccessible. entries.text: 12-name watchlist · 4 November 2026, 08:00 SGT · full research report Watchlist dashboard Calls and full reports Download original edition JSON Market Intel public watchlist · full saved research edition 12-name watchlist · 4 November 2026, 08:00 SGT 12 names · Watch only · not live Research cutoff: 2026-11-04T08:00:00+08:00 Sources checked: 2026-11-04T00:07:58+00:00 Edition prepared: 2026-11-04T00:07:58+00:00 Ten watchlist names rose and two fell at the completed 3 November US regular-session close. AMD led at +3.65%; Apple fell 1.90%. New in this review window: AMD reported Q3 results and Q4 guidance, while Meta filed final pricing for a $15 billion senior-note offering. Amazon filed a backward-looking 13F. Apple’s developer-preview item is explicitly earlier catch-up, not overnight breaking news. Review window: 4 November 2026, 04:00–08:00 SGT (3 November 20:00–4 November 00:00 UTC), with a 15-minute overlap. The previous 04:00 SGT edition and all older artifacts remain available unchanged. This edition replaces the prior in-progress session snapshots with the verified completed 3 November close and recomputed six-horizon returns. New research is separated from earlier catch-up; quiet names do not receive filler. News coverage is partial, not a complete newswire census. This is a dated personal research report, not a live portfolio, transaction record or signal to copy trades. No buy call or executed holding is implied. A thesis does not establish a purchase. No private notes or restricted research screenshots are included. AAPL MSFT NVDA GOOGL AMZN META BRK.B AMD AVGO MU TSLA TSM Read the dates and return basis All main prices are USD completed regular-session observations for 3 November 2026, at 16:00 EST (4 November 05:00 SGT), with individually recorded vendor quote timestamps. Daily change compares the 2 November ordinary close. Yahoo supplies seconds for some observations; Stock Analysis supplies minute precision, preserved without invented seconds. These are saved closes, not live or exact 08:00 SGT prices. No after-hours price has been substituted for a regular close; premarket fields are null. TSM is the US-listed USD ADR. Cumulative return = 100 × (3 November 2026 adjusted close ÷ baseline adjusted close − 1). The 1–6 calendar-month baselines are 2 October, 3 September, 3 August, 2 July, 3 June and 1 May 2026. October 3 and May 3 fall on weekends; July 3 is the observed US Independence Day market holiday, so preceding sessions are used. All 72 dated inputs were independently checked. Adjusted closes incorporate split and dividend/distribution adjustments; ordinary previous closes remain separate. These are cumulative returns before fees and taxes, not six individual monthly returns. We could not independently verify a reliably timestamped after-hours price for this edition. Quotes and financial events use separate timestamps. AMD results and Meta pricing occurred after the regular close; the close prices do not include their subsequent after-hours reaction. All prices and 72 adjusted-close baseline inputs were independently rechecked. Vendor values may later be revised. Current endpoints were crosschecked against completed history rows; intraday or unfinalized observations were rejected. Direct Yahoo pages were rate-limited. Current search-indexed Yahoo historical rows, including regional pages, supplied some older adjusted baselines; direct Stock Analysis and current Quiver history supplied others. Sources are linked beside every calculation. TSM uses Yahoo-adjusted historical baselines consistently, including 3 September at 415.89 rather than the 416.13 in Stock Analysis. Its finalized 404.80 close is not the earlier 15:59:59 observation of 404.66. Existing dated editions, calls, reports and their qualifications are retained unchanged. Old active-session and premarket snapshots remain in their original archives rather than being represented as current observations. Watch only: no current holding, executed trade, user buy call or recommendation is implied. No private diary, brokerage record, personal account information or restricted screenshot is included. Apple’s Siri developer-preview post is timestamped 18:00:20 UTC before this window and explicitly labelled earlier catch-up. Meta priced terms do not establish completed settlement. Reuters coverage used targeted searches and accessible indexed syndication. Direct Reuters AMD article could not be opened, and direct access to the two syndicated articles returned 403; indexed versions were readable. Coverage is partial. Alphabet, Meta and Micron news-release lists were incomplete or did not render. Broadcom’s current list was successfully accessed at its new financial-news URL. No unverified after-hours percentage from Reuters is included: syndicated copies carry differing market reactions and do not expose a reliable final update timestamp. AMD official release and SEC earnings filing were read; a complete earnings-call transcript was not independently reviewed. All 12 SEC recent-submission feeds were checked through the cutoff. This does not constitute a complete census of third-party ownership filings or every company announcement. No newly verified item for a ticker is not a blanket no-news finding. Facts, generated research analysis, risks and next catalysts are labelled separately. Report formatting adds no later evidence to the original edition. Source timestamps and coverage limits remain fixed. Amazon’s previously unavailable SEC feed was not retried. Reuters and issuer access is partial, and a quiet-name result does not mean no news occurred. Prior editions remain unchanged. No private notes or restricted research screenshots are included. This website is a research and financial-literacy project. Read the following before relying on an article, market dashboard, calculator or portfolio simulation. 1. A published yield is not necessarily a tradable executable price or the return an investor will receive after fees, taxes and FX movements. Check every security identifier, quote convention, ex-coupon and settlement date, accrued interest, clean versus dirty price, minimum denomination, embedded option, liquidity, counterparty and transaction cost with the actual dealing platform or offering documentation before acting. The website does not place orders, hold client assets, verify account balances or guarantee access to any market. 4. Models, calculators and Portfolio V6/V7 Portfolio simulations, bond calculators, retirement and CPF examples, insurance illustrations, options tools and structured-investment scenario analyses are hypothetical decision-support tools . Results depend on input quality, formulas, timing, accounting conventions and assumptions. Past performance, backtests, distributions and scenario paths do not establish future outcomes. A scenario may exclude or simplify transaction costs, taxes, spreads, funding resets, early redemption, default, issuer call rights, liquidity, FX conversion, drawdowns, fees, policy charges and changing regulations. A return shown as an annualised rate may be materially different from realised cash profit or a money-weighted return. Different versions, including V6 and V7, may not use identical methodologies. For leveraged simulations: portfolio net asset value, liabilities, financing cashflows, FX translation and capital outlay must be kept separate. Do not assume an illustration captures margin calls, financing constraints or all contractual obligations. 5. AI-assisted research and automated updates Some content, categorisation, charts, summaries, translations or code may be AI-assisted or automatically produced. Such outputs can contain false statements, incorrect calculations, incomplete sources, stale data, misunderstood context and plausible-looking but invalid citations. A “verified” label should be used only for figures and statements actually checked against their cited sources. Research updates and corrections may be published later. The site is not obliged to maintain a historical version or notify readers of every change. Check the article's publication date, any correction notice, data cutoff and underlying source. 6. Market and product risks All investments carry risks, potentially including complete loss of invested capital. Leveraged positions can generate losses beyond the initial cash outlay or require additional funding. Foreign-currency investments involve translation and funding risk even where the underlying instrument pays its coupon or dividend as expected. Products discussed may be complex, unsuitable for some investors, or unavailable in certain jurisdictions. Read the dedicated Investment & Modelling Risks page and the actual prospectus, term sheet, product highlights sheet or insurance policy terms. 7. entries.title: Editorial standards & conflicts | Market Intelligence Hub
entries.text: Editorial standards & conflicts | Market Intelligence Hub M MARKET INTELLIGENCE Legal & transparency Legal & transparency Disclaimer Privacy Policy Terms of Use Risks Editorial Market Intel / Legal / Editorial standards & conflicts Legal & transparency Editorial standards & conflicts How sources, AI, corrections and interests are handled. DRAFT · REVIEW REQUIRED 6 November 2026 Singapore context Independent research & modelling Not yet approved as a final policy. The legal operator, privacy-request process, separately hosted app data flows and any professional compliance requirements must be confirmed before this can be presented as a final notice. The Market Intelligence Hub is designed to explain financial markets using sourced reporting, transparent mathematics and plain-language analysis. This page sets out the publishing standard the project intends to follow. It does not certify that every historical article already meets every standard. Colour & formatting guide Open the unified research standard: style, colours and gatekeeper . The complete working guide is together on one page; this editorial-policy source remains available. The practical reference below brings together the V3 presentation combinations, V1.2 text tags, and examples of section headings and separators. 9. Colour combinations 10. Text and tagging 11. Sections and separators 12. Formatting checklist 13. Reusable research prompt 1. Separate facts, interpretation and scenarios Each publication should distinguish reported facts from analysis and opinion , hypothetical calculations from actual market prices, and current data from historical observations. A model-derived price or forecast should never be styled as if it were an official issuer or exchange quote. The central claim of a report should be understandable without the chart. Charts should show units, date or cutoff, source and enough context to avoid distorted comparisons. 2. Date and source discipline Time-sensitive reporting should carry a Singapore-time publication timestamp and a clearly labelled market-data cutoff or overseas session date. A Friday Singapore morning report can be based on Thursday's US session; those are not the same date, and they should be described as such. Priority should go to primary documents where appropriate: issuer filings, government and central-bank releases, official data, prospectuses and term sheets. Trusted professional reporting, including Reuters when used, should be properly attributed and linked. Secondary commentary should not be mistaken for a primary record. Source links should support the specific figure or assertion next to which they appear. A general bibliography does not substitute for evidence on a contested point. 3. Research status and corrections A publication may be labelled Verified , Analysis , Scenario , Preliminary or Correction only if its current review status justifies the label. “Verified” means the material point or number was checked against identified evidence; it does not mean every prediction is correct. When a material error is found, update the page, describe the correction with a date, and avoid silently rewriting a historical thesis as if it were the original conclusion. If sources conflict, report the disagreement rather than inventing certainty. 4. Mathematical transparency Calculators and charts should disclose significant assumptions, cashflow timing, units, formulas and data origin. Distinguish nominal from real returns, yield from coupon, realised from unrealised P&L, and assets from debt and capital contributions. For financed portfolios, net asset value after any FX translation must not have that same adjustment subtracted again. Comparison calculations should not mix cashflows from different periods or claim precision beyond the source data. 5. AI assistance and human review AI can assist with research collection, language, visualisation and code generation, but it can hallucinate prices, names, legislation and citations. Important prices, issuer terms, calculations, financial claims and quotations should be tested against their sources before publication. Machine-generated explanations should be marked or described where that context matters. Automation schedules and scraped feeds do not guarantee completeness, continuity or timeliness. A missed update is not a signal that the market did not change. 6. Conflicts of interest and employment boundaries Writers and contributors may have direct or indirect exposure to instruments discussed, including personal holdings, model positions or hedges. Material interests should be disclosed when relevant and legally permissible. A public article is not an official recommendation from a writer's employer or associated financial institution unless expressly authorised and identified as such. The project should never publish client-confidential, employer-proprietary, inside or unpublished price-sensitive information. Institutional branding, research extracts and professional titles must not imply endorsement, licensing or regulatory review that has not occurred. 7. Copyright, quotations and third parties Quote only what is lawfully permitted or licensed, make source attribution specific, and prefer original charts over copying protected charts. Linking to Reuters, bank research or Morningstar does not establish the right to republish their full articles, pricing feeds or images. Third-party logos and trademarks remain the property of their owners. 8. Corrections and transparency Material factual errors should be corrected transparently, with the correction and its date recorded. Do not send confidential account details in a public issue. Once operational, an article should show its original date and material revision history, not merely a “live” label. Required subject-to-theme guide All future research follows the approved main-subject guide. Select the main analytical question, then use its V3 presentation theme. V1.2 company, ticker and keyword colours remain unchanged. See the ten subjects, palette names and exact colour swatches · See each published article’s existing colours and prescribed next-edition palette Historical pages have not been automatically recoloured. A prescribed theme is distinct from an applied template. For mixed subjects, explain the route choice rather than matching an incidental keyword. 9. Colour combinations Use one presentation theme for each article. V3.0 controls page backgrounds, text, cards and chart composition. The V1.2 Merged standard keeps the approved meanings and colours of company, country, instrument and keyword tags. Reference: V3.0, 7 November 2026, with V1.2 Merged semantic mappings. Validate the entity and context, then match the longest valid whole phrase. Numeric priority breaks equal-span matches only after identity is valid. Use whole-word boundaries: US must not match USD; Fed must not match FedEx. Preserve punctuation in OPEC+, S$NEER and qualified tickers. Ordinary phrases may be case-folded. Short tickers and ambiguous acronyms need the correct case and financial context. Leave unresolved BOC, C, SE, AI or DE unmapped. Keep USD/SGD and SGD/USD distinct. A company-name mention alone does not establish a listing, share class, headquarters or index membership. Retain the original V1 mappings, then the specific reconciled extensions, then the documented generic fallback. Never replace a company colour with a guessed brand colour. One story may carry several independent tags. A single text span has one dominant semantic colour. Keep entity, location, instrument, story status, evidence status and market direction separate. 31 named semantic palettes. These examples are existing canonical labels, not new assignments. Several palettes share some HEX values; retain their different names and meanings. The full keyword map has every canonical ID, alias, matching rule and priority. The company directory preserves each supplied company and listing. For example, a country using a red palette does not imply a negative assessment. Apply “Verified”, “Scenario” or “Correction” only when the actual review state supports it. Copy-ready tagging instruction Apply the V1.2 Merged canonical tag, exact light/dark text and chip colours, aliases, matching rules and priority. Validate context first; use the longest valid whole phrase; leave unresolved identities unmapped. Preserve company, listing and share class separately. Use V3 only for the presentation theme. Keep a readable text label and never use colour alone to communicate meaning. 11. Sections and separators Make the reading order visible. Use numbered headings, generous space, a restrained 1px separator and short paragraphs. Keep body text around 16px with at least 1.5 line spacing; use roughly 24–32px section headings and adapt the layout instead of shrinking everything on a phone. The examples below use neutral Earth & Slate 03 . A different approved theme supplies its own matching tokens. These layout labels do not create new semantic tags or evidence states. SECTION 01 · EVIDENCE What the evidence shows Begin with a clear takeaway. Follow it with the source, observation date and a plain-language explanation. SECTION 02 · INTERPRETATION Why it matters Separate the reported result from interpretation, assumptions and what could change the conclusion. Page #FEFDFB Card #FFFFFF Secondary panel #F4F5F1 Focus panel #EBF4F6 1px divider / border #D8E9EE Heading / body #222D31 Secondary text #45535A FACT State the reported observation. Include the source, data date and units. ANALYSIS Explain the mechanism and distinguish interpretation from the reported fact. TEACH ME Explain the concept in simple terms, with a short relevant example. RISKS Show limitations, counterarguments and what would change the view. Use a heading and spacing as well as a divider. A faint border is decorative; it should never be the only way to identify a section. Keep the same treatment for similar content. On narrow screens, stack panels and keep wide tables inside their own scrollable container. Copy-ready section instruction Use one approved V3 theme with a near-white page, white main cards, pale secondary and focus panels, dark readable text and thin matching separators. Organise the report with numbered headings and clear FACT, ANALYSIS, TEACH ME and RISKS labels where appropriate. Keep colours restrained, spacing generous, and the mobile reading order logical. 12. Formatting checklist Required prompt reference: every article and posting prompt must link to this editorial policy and apply it alongside the current approved colour and tagging sources. Start with the answer: a clear title, reporting cutoff and one to five supported takeaways. Choose a theme deliberately: follow the question and the route table. Keep semantic identity colours separate. Explain every useful visual: title, date or period, instrument, units, source, “How to read this”, finding and limitations. Preserve exact values where rounding matters. Show honest comparisons: ordinary bars begin at zero; line scales are labelled; actuals and projections look different; missing data stays missing. Check readability: exact tokens, contrast on the real background, visible labels, mobile layout, table scrolling, links and printed output. Keep the review honest: automated checks validate declared tokens and required structure. They do not prove source accuracy, suitable tagging, legal clearance or rendered accessibility. New authored research HTML follows the existing publication gate . Older reports are preserved; generated watchlist reports retain their separate checks and are not certified as V3. This addition documents the design standard and does not turn the draft legal policy into a final approved notice. All 150 swatches · All 437 tags · Company directory · Excel, PDF and full research prompt · Precise publication rules Colour, tagging, layout and reusable prompt added 8 November 2026. The original editorial clauses and draft-policy status are retained. 13. Reusable research prompt Use this link for future research. Specify the topic, sources, cutoff, format and destination, then ask for the report to follow this prompt and the standards on this page. Every article and posting prompt must include this editorial-policy link as a required reference. Example request Use the research prompt and editorial standards here to research [TOPIC], using [SOURCES], checked up to [DATE AND TIME ZONE]. Deliver [FORMAT AND DESTINATION]. The reusable prompt below preserves the supplied research requirements. The example video is omitted. The reference instruction makes the required editorial and tagging links explicit. The separate V3 design master prompt remains available for detailed implementation. Copy full research prompt Download as text Read the full reusable prompt Create a detailed, client-friendly research report on [TOPIC] , using [SOURCES / ATTACHMENTS] , with information checked up to [DATE AND TIME ZONE] . Reference style Use my DBS and STI banks report as the main reference for its card layout, charts, explanations and overall presentation. Inspect it first. Adapt the design to the new topic rather than copying its figures or conclusions. My colour and presentation standard Apply my current approved Colour & Tagging Standard. The Excel governs keywords, tickers, aliases, tags and colour mappings. The matching PDF governs visual design, charts and layout. Follow the documented precedence rules and do not invent or overwrite mappings. Each report can have a different colour theme and background shades, while keeping approved colours for the same companies, terms and concepts consistent. If the current standard cannot be accessed, say so and continue the research without claiming it has been applied. Research and writing Start with one to five key takeaways. Explain what happened, why it matters, what the evidence supports, the outlook, risks and what could change the conclusion. Use plain English, short paragraphs and point form where helpful. Include a bold key takeaway in each paragraph, but avoid making everything bold. Explain unfamiliar terms and make the report easy to understand without sounding condescending. Separate verified facts, source opinions, forecasts and your own analysis. Include counterarguments and material risks. Cite sources and distinguish the date of the data from the date it was published. Don’t invent figures or present forecasts as guarantees. Charts and market context Inspect the charts and data already available on my Market Intelligence Hub and reuse suitable components and verified data where practical. Where relevant to the research, include: Prices of the security, commodity or index discussed. Bond yields, yield curves or credit spreads. Relevant FX pairs. S&P 500 / SPX prices or performance. Include only charts that help explain the report. Identify the instrument, currency, units, source, data date and whether prices are adjusted or include dividends. Label FX direction and yield tenor clearly. Do not describe dated data as live. Targets, scenarios and calls Where the research provides them, add base-case, bull-case or bear-case levels, targets and calls to the relevant chart. Label each with its source, date, horizon, assumptions and units. Clearly distinguish actual data from forecasts. If only a target level is available, show a labelled target line or marker. Don’t invent a forecast path, missing target, probability or analyst call. Explain qualitative scenarios in a card rather than assigning them invented numbers. Show the reference price and date for any calculated upside or downside. Card style and visual explanations Aim for roughly half meaningful charts, tables and diagrams and half concise explanation. Each substantive card should have: A clear takeaway title. A relevant chart, table, diagram or comparison. A short layman explanation of how to read it and why it matters. Source, date and units where applicable. Choose the visual that best explains the point; don’t add decorative charts just to fill space. Use direct labels and avoid misleading scales, tiny text and clipped headings. Ensure the report works on mobile and remains understandable in greyscale. File size and checks Keep files small for later upload to Market Intel. Use lightweight code-drawn visuals and editable charts rather than large embedded images. State the final file size. Check figures, calculations, chart labels, links and the rendered desktop and mobile layouts. Clearly identify any unresolved gaps. Deliver: [REPORT FORMAT AND DESTINATION] . Do not change my websites, files or scheduled tasks, or publish the report, unless I explicitly ask. Required colour and editorial references Read and apply these references as part of every article and posting prompt: Tag and event atlas Editorial standards & conflicts Required for all future research: apply the main-subject theme guide , record the selected theme and preserve V1.2 identity colours. This requirement is included in the copied and downloaded prompt. This page is a reusable reference. Its publication does not update every existing chat or scheduled task, and the prompt does not authorise changes or publication unless explicitly requested. Public-source research addendum Added 15 November 2026 (Singapore time). This section supplements the existing copyright, quotation and source-attribution standards. Purpose and independence. Market Intelligence Hub publishes original research, commentary, criticism, review and analysis informed by information lawfully accessed from public sources. These may include company disclosures, official statistics, market information and publicly reported analyst opinions, valuations and forecasts. References to third-party opinions record or examine what an identified source reported at a particular time; they do not present those opinions as established facts. Attribution and context. Our editorial standard is to identify the relevant provider, the author where identified, the publication or work, its date and the source actually consulted, with a link where available. Where an estimate is reported through another publication, we distinguish the original estimate provider from the publication consulted. Third-party figures, statements and opinions are distinguished from our own calculations, charts, interpretations and conclusions. References to a provider do not imply affiliation, sponsorship, endorsement or approval. Lawful use of source material. We may refer to factual information and reproduce limited extracts or individual data points where permitted by applicable law, licence or permission. Where applicable, this includes fair use for criticism, review or reporting, assessed in the circumstances of the particular use. Reproduced material must be limited to what is reasonably necessary for the stated analytical purpose and legally permitted. Public accessibility, attribution, free access to this website or presentation in a new format does not, by itself, authorise republication. Third-party rights. Any intellectual-property rights in third-party material remain with their respective owners. Creating an original chart, calculation or summary does not remove rights that may subsist in its source material. We do not reproduce complete reports, protected charts, proprietary feeds or substantial or systematically reconstructed third-party datasets unless a sufficient lawful basis for that use has been established. Where that basis has not been established, we provide a link to a lawful source or omit the material. This policy neither grants readers rights in third-party material nor limits uses permitted by applicable law. Analyst estimates and comparisons. We distinguish long-term fair-value estimates from price targets and other forecasts with specified horizons. Comparisons identify the relevant estimate date, instrument, currency and stated horizon where available. Any scoring explains the observation period, assessment criteria, sample size and material exclusions. Missing observations remain unscored. Repeated observations of an unchanged estimate are not presented as separate new forecasts, and later revisions are not substituted retrospectively for the estimate originally assessed. A difference between a later market price and a long-term valuation does not, by itself, establish that the valuation was incorrect. Results reflect the disclosed methodology and available evidence. Corrections and rights concerns. Readers and rights holders may raise concerns about factual accuracy, attribution, methodology or alleged unauthorised use through the project’s public issue tracker . Please identify the affected page, the material concerned and the basis of the concern. The issue tracker is public; do not include confidential information, account details or personal identification documents. We will review sufficiently detailed notices and make appropriate corrections, qualifications or removals. This process does not restrict anyone’s rights or remedies under applicable law. entries.text: Privacy Policy | Market Intelligence Hub M MARKET INTELLIGENCE Legal & transparency Legal & transparency Disclaimer Privacy Policy Terms of Use Risks Editorial Market Intel / Legal / Privacy Policy Legal & transparency Privacy Policy What the Hub stores, what requires verification and your choices. DRAFT · REVIEW REQUIRED 6 November 2026 Singapore context Independent research & modelling Not yet approved as a final policy. The legal operator, privacy-request process, separately hosted app data flows and any professional compliance requirements must be confirmed before this can be presented as a final notice. We want readers to understand what data a research website or portfolio tool may handle. This document distinguishes functionality confirmed in the Market Intelligence Hub from data handling that still needs verification in separately hosted apps. Draft limitation: Responsibility for the services, the privacy-request process and the V6/V7 data-flow inventory remain unconfirmed. This page is not a final privacy notice. 1. Operator and scope Responsibility for the services described here remains to be confirmed. This draft covers the Market Intelligence Hub, its own research and calculators, and related Portfolio V6/V7 and options tools only to the extent that the same operator controls their processing . Third-party sites, including those opened by external links, apply their own policies. 2. Information that may be processed Category What this can include Why it matters Browser preferences and research notes Saved watchlists, selected securities, chart settings, language preferences and notes To retain the workspace across visits on the same browser Portfolio or calculator inputs Amounts, assumed returns, loan balances, rates, holdings and uploaded files, if a feature asks for them To calculate or display the scenario you requested Technical and usage information IP address, device/browser details, request timestamps, page addresses and errors processed by hosting or service providers To serve pages, protect infrastructure and diagnose faults Voluntary correspondence Contact details and content you send to the operator To reply to enquiries, corrections or privacy requests External service data Information handled when opening a linked website, loading external resources or using an integrated service Subject to the relevant provider's practices Do not put account credentials, identity documents, bank-client information, NRIC numbers, full account numbers, passwords or other highly sensitive data into a public research tool. If a feature requires such information, do not use it until its data protection and authorisation have been explicitly verified. 3. What has been checked in the Hub A review of the public Market Intelligence Hub V4 source on 6 November 2026 identified use of browser localStorage for some settings, saved security selections, watchlists and workspace notes. The Hub also fetches public data files for research displays. Data held in browser storage can remain on that device until removed by the user, application or browser. This finding does not prove that every tool is browser-only. The separately hosted Portfolio Simulator V6/V7, Options Lab, external data feeds, embedded content and any future features require their own technical checks. We cannot responsibly promise that all portfolio inputs “never leave your device” without that verification. 4. How information is used Where applicable, information is used to deliver the pages and features you request, remember your on-device preferences, calculate entered scenarios, respond to correspondence, investigate errors, protect the service, and meet applicable legal obligations. Personal data should not be collected for unrelated marketing or sold by the project operator without a separate, properly disclosed basis. If analytics, newsletters, feedback forms, login accounts, advertising, cloud synchronisation or AI APIs are added, this policy must be updated before deployment to describe their purposes and relevant recipients; any consent or controls required by applicable law must also be implemented. 5. Browser storage, cookies and analytics Browser localStorage is different from an HTTP cookie. Clearing site data for the relevant domain may remove saved preferences and notes. Blocking local storage may stop parts of a workspace from working or prevent persistence. Hosting services and third-party websites may use cookies, request logs or similar technologies. No statement is made here that analytics or tracking are absent from the entire suite , because every separately hosted tool has not been audited. If non-essential analytics or advertising trackers are deployed, provide an accurate disclosure and appropriate choice mechanisms for the relevant jurisdictions. 6. Hosting, transfers and outside websites The public Hub is hosted using GitHub Pages; certain linked tools are served from different hosting domains. When you access an online service, its hosting provider can process network and technical information required to deliver the site. Some processing may occur outside Singapore. External market-data sites, news publishers, chart services or AI services may process data under their own terms when opened or used. Any transfer of personal data controlled by the project operator must satisfy applicable requirements, including Singapore's PDPA where it applies. We do not guarantee that external services operate under Singapore law. 7. Disclosure, retention and safeguards Information may be available to infrastructure and technical providers insofar as needed to run the relevant service, or disclosed where lawfully required. The final notice should list material providers and categories of data once the technical audit is complete. Browser-stored information remains subject to browser and app behaviour; clearing it can make stored workspaces unrecoverable. Operator-held correspondence should be kept only while reasonably needed for the stated purpose or legal requirements. Hosting logs may follow the provider's retention schedule. We use or will implement reasonable safeguards appropriate to information actually handled, but no internet service can guarantee perfect security. 8. Your choices and rights You can generally delete the Hub's device-specific preferences by clearing saved data for the site in your browser. Before doing so, export or copy anything you wish to retain. For personal data held by the operator, you may request information, access, correction or withdrawal of consent where applicable under Singapore law. Some requests may be limited by legal exceptions or information the operator does not possess. Do not publish identifiable portfolio information or privacy requests in public comments or GitHub issues. For information kept only in your browser, the operator may not have a copy to provide or delete remotely. 9. Children and sensitive financial information These financial research and modelling tools are not designed to solicit personal information from children. The operator should not deliberately seek highly sensitive identifiers or confidential client data through general-access tools. If such information is accidentally received, it should be handled according to applicable law, institutional obligations and a documented incident procedure. 10. Updates Changes in hosting, analytics, processing, forms, accounts, APIs or data retention may require a new version of this policy. The date below identifies this draft, not proof that every technical system has been audited. Draft date: 6 November 2026, Singapore time. On this page 1. Operator and scope 2. Information that may be processed 3. What has been checked in the Hub 4. How information is used 5. Browser storage, cookies and analytics 6. Hosting, transfers and outside websites 7. entries.text: Investment & modelling risks | Market Intelligence Hub M MARKET INTELLIGENCE Legal & transparency Legal & transparency Disclaimer Privacy Policy Terms of Use Risks Editorial Market Intel / Legal / Investment & modelling risks Legal & transparency Investment & modelling risks Bond, leverage, FX, derivatives and scenario risks explained. DRAFT · REVIEW REQUIRED 6 November 2026 Singapore context Independent research & modelling Not yet approved as a final policy. The legal operator, privacy-request process, separately hosted app data flows and any professional compliance requirements must be confirmed before this can be presented as a final notice. A financial model can be mathematically correct and still lead to a terrible financial decision. The calculator only knows what went into it; markets, borrowers and funding desks have no obligation to follow the spreadsheet. Product risk at a glance Area What can go wrong What to verify Government bonds, UST and SGS Yield rises cause price falls; real returns lose to inflation; long duration magnifies price sensitivity Yield convention, maturity, duration, accrued interest, cashflows and FX STRIPS and long-dated fixed income No interim coupons; large sensitivity to rate changes and terminal assumptions Exact maturity/ISIN, zero-coupon price, volatility and exit liquidity Investment-grade and high-yield credit Credit spreads widen; issuer downgrade/default; liquidity disappears Issuer obligations, ranking, covenants, credit spread and recovery assumptions CHF or other FX financing Funding resets, FX loss, margin calls, forced sales and negative carry Loan currency, FX direction, collateral rules, renewal rate and repayment timing Equities, ETFs and REITs Earnings disappoint, concentration, dividends cut, valuations fall Holdings, leverage, index weightings, cashflows and distributions Options and hedges Gap moves, time decay, volatility changes, exercise/assignment and liquidity loss Contract multiplier, expiration, strike, premium, assignment obligations and fees Structured products Path-dependent knock-in/knock-out, autocall, early redemption, issuer default Term sheet, observation dates, barriers, underlyings and credit exposure Insurance and retirement illustrations Policy charges, caps/floors, surrender penalties, FX, longevity and changing rules Full policy terms, guaranteed versus non-guaranteed benefits, age and timing Gold and commodities No contractual coupon; sharp price and FX moves; storage or product costs Vehicle, bid/offer, custody, exposure and liquidity 1. Bonds: yield is not the same as a guaranteed profit A fixed coupon does not make a bond's market price fixed. Duration measures sensitivity to yield changes, while convexity and non-parallel curve shifts alter the actual outcome. A long-dated Treasury or zero-coupon STRIP can fluctuate dramatically before maturity even when the issuer continues to meet its obligations. Yield to maturity assumes specified cashflows and treatment of reinvestment, defaults and calls. Clean price, dirty price, accrued coupon and settlement cash paid are different amounts. Callable or structured notes may require yield-to-worst and a review of embedded options rather than relying on a headline yield. 2. Leverage and CHF funding: assets and debts must stay separate A financed portfolio may look attractive when bond coupons exceed the initial borrowing rate. That comparison excludes what happens when the exchange rate changes, financing rolls at a different rate, collateral values fall or a lender changes lending ratios. Foreign-currency shocks can move faster than a bond's monthly coupon accrual. Keep the underlying portfolio's market value, net asset value, liabilities, financing interest, currency translation, realised cashflow and investor capital outlay in separate lines. Do not double-count a currency adjustment already reflected in NAV. A positive expected carry is not a cap on losses or a guarantee against forced liquidation. Historical stress events such as the Swiss franc's abrupt repricing in 2015 are useful risk scenarios, not predictions of the next move. 3. Options: premium received is not a free yield A short put can lead to assignment at the strike price when the market price has fallen substantially. Cash-secured or margin-backed structures differ in capital requirements. A long put hedge costs premium and loses time value; option values also move with implied volatility, interest rates and remaining maturity. A simulated one-week result should not be confused with profit held to expiry. Strategies involving spreads, covered calls, collars and structured options may have early exercise, gap, liquidity, counterparty or settlement risks. Profit-and-loss displays should identify assumptions and contract multipliers, not hide them behind a single annualised percentage. 4. Structured investments and insurance: read the contract Knock-in and knock-out barriers, autocall terms, issuer credit risk, coupon conditions and observation dates matter as much as the advertised headline coupon. A step-down schedule changes possible redemption dates and subsequent cashflows. Insurance projections, index floors and caps, policy fees, mortality charges where applicable, surrender conditions and income conversion mechanics must be based on the actual contract. Illustrations are not the same as guaranteed payouts. CPF and CPF LIFE scenarios must use the rules, rates and eligibility conditions applicable to the stated date and participant. 5. Model and market-data risks Even a precise formula can produce misleading results if a quote is stale or the model mixes cashflows, FX, gains, debt balances and returns. Backtests may suffer from survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, selective history, curve-fitting and underestimated costs. AI-written explanations can introduce further mistakes. Always verify source dates and sessions, units and quotation conventions, instrument identifiers, rounding and fee assumptions. Compare optimistic, base and adverse scenarios, including an explicit funding or liquidity shock where leverage is involved. 6. Your portfolio and privacy A simulation may reveal more than you intend about your wealth, assets, borrowing and risk exposure. Never paste confidential client holdings, non-public investment instructions, passwords, access tokens or full account statements into an unverified online tool. Review the Privacy Policy before entering real figures. Bottom line: A useful tool helps you understand a decision, not outsource responsibility for it. Consult current issuer terms and an appropriately qualified adviser before making a commitment. On this page Product risk at a glance 1. Bonds: yield is not the same as a guaranteed profit 2. Leverage and CHF funding: assets and debts must stay separate 3. Options: premium received is not a free yield 4. Structured investments and insurance: read the contract 5. Model and market-data risks 6. These terms set out how the Market Intelligence Hub and the related services operated by the same project maintainer may be used. Please also read the Disclaimer and Privacy Policy . 1. Scope and agreement “Services” means the Market Intelligence Hub, its research articles, dashboards, market-data displays, and related portfolio, options, bond, foreign-exchange, CPF, retirement and financial-modelling tools that expressly refer to this legal hub. A separately owned or operated service has its own terms. By accessing a Service, you agree to these terms to the extent that a valid agreement can be formed under applicable law. If you do not agree, do not rely on or use the Service. 2. Educational and research use Services are provided to assist financial understanding, comparison and scenario analysis. They are not a brokerage, investment adviser, automated portfolio manager, financial-planning engagement, custody arrangement or official institution channel. No account, trade or professional advisory relationship is created merely by visiting a page or using a calculator. A numerical output, target, buy/sell label, watchlist entry, model score or illustrative position does not establish that a product is suitable for you. Your own independent investigation and relevant regulated advice are necessary before action. 3. Accuracy and time sensitivity Content may be delayed, estimated, hypothetical, automatically generated or subsequently corrected. Data may not reflect the price or terms available at execution. You must verify live prices, conventions, fees, eligibility, legal restrictions and product documentation independently. We may update, remove, suspend, discontinue or change Services and content without guaranteeing availability or continued access to an earlier version. Historical articles remain analyses of their publication dates, even if they are linked from a current dashboard. 4. Responsible use of tools and inputs Only enter information you are authorised to use. Do not upload or paste confidential employer records, client portfolios, client identifiers, passwords, security credentials or third-party proprietary material without the required permission. entries.text: AI data centres: from power to profit | Research Explained ← Research Explained · 40-company business-quality companion Research Explained / My thoughts / 05-Nov-2026 (Thu) AI data centres: from power to profit Technology, company financials and investment choices—built around durable core earnings Equities / shares Cloud / data centres Semiconductors United States Singapore Analysis / inference Approved company colours identify entities; they do not mean buy or sell. Forecasts use outlines and explicit labels. Unmapped companies retain neutral text. Print / save PDF Self-contained · vector diagrams · external source links only Public research edition. This separate report explains the AI infrastructure chain with 11 original vector visuals and financial comparisons for 52 companies. Proprietary analyst valuation tables and rankings derived from those estimates are excluded. Issuer financial data, definitions and source links are retained. Educational research, not personalised investment advice. Download the public financial data and definitions (JSON) . Two five-slide presentations Public summaries with editable charts and tables, source links, and speaker notes on every slide. Proprietary valuation estimates and price-based rankings are excluded. Financial briefing (PowerPoint, 49 KB) Clear visual story (PowerPoint, 50 KB) Read or print the formatted presentation notes . Prepared 5 November 2026. Historical issuer periods and forward-looking scenarios are labelled separately. These are educational summaries, not personal investment recommendations. Contents — jump to a section 01. AI data centres: from power to profit 02. The full system—and where investors get paid 03. What changed since the late-2022 AI inflection? 04. What happens when someone asks an AI a question? 05. Electricity: scale matters, location matters more 06. Who earns from power—and what does a PPA buy? 07. Cooling: remove heat without confusing rack generations 08. Compute: compare complete systems, not isolated headline numbers 09. Memory and storage are complementary, not interchangeable 10. Networking: bandwidth, latency and supplier concentration 11. Software is a moat—but switching costs vary by workload 12. The economic engine: useful output, utilisation and price 13. Cash generation and the investment bill must be read together 14. Depreciation, impairment and cash spending are different 15. Growth, profit and cash can tell different stories 16. Revenue diversification: count demand drivers, not tickers 17. Original companies: questions before committing capital 18. Additional companies: breadth and execution risks 19. Stress the shared demand driver before adding more names 20. Singapore: efficient capacity matters more than headline scale 21. What the supplied notes needed to qualify 22. Additional financials: power and electrical systems 23. Additional financials: connectivity, optics and storage 24. Original universe: annual financials 1 / 4 25. Original universe: annual financials 2 / 4 26. Original universe: annual financials 3 / 4 27. Original universe: annual financials 4 / 4 28. Additional company map: use the correct business and listing 29. How to read the financial tables: earnings and attribution 30. How to read the financial tables: cash and investment 31. Method, evidence and use of the report 32. Source register 1 33. Source register 2 34. Source register 3 35. Source register 4 36. Source register 5 37. Source register 6 01 / Five takeaways / investment judgement AI data centres: from power to profit A company and financial guide to the machinery behind generative AI, built around durable core earnings and sensible entry prices. 1. Start with the business that survives a slower AI spending cycle. For a focus on established earnings, Alphabet and Microsoft remain the first core candidates to assess. Their existing distribution and cash-generating franchises support AI investment; spending itself does not establish shareholder value. [S001] [S002] 2. Diversification must reach beyond the same customer budgets. GPUs, HBM, switches, optics and cooling are different products, but their orders can depend on the same cloud buildouts. Amphenol , Schneider Electric and Eaton deserve attention for broader end markets. Their price, acquisition funding and changing revenue mix still matter. 3. Follow cash after investment, not the largest growth or margin figure. The financial appendix states seven financial measures for all 40 original companies and adds 12 targeted power/connectivity spotlights. Definitions are preserved; unlike cash-flow measures are flagged. 4. The physical constraints are real, but specifications need dates and units. A deployed rack, a future platform roadmap and an entire campus are different things. InfiniBand is an industry standard; NVIDIA acquired Mellanox. The 600 kW claim in the notes is qualified in the technology review. [S047] [S048] 5. Buy in stages against evidence of returns. Prefer understandable earnings, defendable customer relationships and a valuation cushion. Treat high AI dependence as a shared portfolio risk; require improving utilisation and cash conversion before increasing exposure. Decision lens Preferred starting point What can overturn it Core earnings GOOGL / MSFT Weaker legacy economics; AI investment outruns monetisation Manufacturing capability TSM / ASML / KLAC Semiconductor downturn; export limits; valuation Broader infrastructure APH / SU.PA ; ETN on price Customer concentration; acquisition/debt execution AI satellites NVDA / AVGO / VRT One shared capital-spending cycle; rapid product changes Scope: Research as of 05-Nov-2026 (Thu), Singapore time. Financial periods are separately labelled. This is a public adaptation of the completed research, not a new live-price update. Original explanatory diagrams replace third-party artwork. 02 / From power to profit The full system—and where investors get paid Many suppliers; one connected economic system 1 Electricity Grid, generation, substations GEV • ENR • CEG • VST 2 Power delivery Switchgear, UPS, distribution ETN • Schneider • Vertiv 3 Cooling Move heat from chips Vertiv • Ecolab/CoolIT 4 Compute GPU / CPU / custom ASIC NVIDIA • AMD • Broadcom 5 Data movement HBM, host memory, fabrics Micron • Arista • optics 6 Software Kernels, orchestration, models CUDA • cloud platforms 7 Customer service Search, copilots, enterprise Microsoft • Google • others 8 Cash receipts Subscriptions, ads, usage Retention and pricing 9 Investor return Cash after reinvestment Debt, dilution and valuation Takeaway: The last two boxes determine whether a successful deployment becomes a successful investment. Read: Follow the arrows. These are functional relationships, not a literal electrical circuit or a claim that every vendor supplies every site. Units: Conceptual map; no quantitative scale · Date: 5 Nov 2026 · Source: Primary technical sources [S049] [S050] [S051] ; author synthesis. Physical inputs support a digital service. Power operates the equipment; cooling removes heat; processors run calculations; memory and networks keep data moving. Software schedules the work and turns model output into something customers use. All layers must work together, so the slowest constraint can delay revenue. Cash does not flow automatically to every layer. Contracts, pricing power, working capital and financing determine who retains the value. A manufacturer can ship record volumes while funding inventory; a cloud operator can show rising sales while construction absorbs cash. Those are different economic risks. Layman’s summary: Think of a factory with reliable power, production machines, conveyors and an order book. Fast machines help only when the complete factory delivers useful output that customers pay for. 03 / From power to profit What changed since the late-2022 AI inflection? Revenue growth has been extremely uneven 1× reference NVDA FY2026 8.01× MU FY2026 4.33× ANET FY2025 2.06× VRT FY2025 1.80× MSFT FY2026 1.67× GOOGL FY2025 1.42× DELL FY2026 1.12× INTC FY2025 0.84× Takeaway: The strongest AI supplier growth did not translate into an equal uplift across all technology businesses. Read: Each bar is latest annual revenue ÷ its own baseline; labels rounded to 2 decimals. 1× means unchanged. This is not a share-price return. Exact inputs are in the data file. Units: Revenue multiple; native currency cancels within each company · Date: Baseline FY2022 except NVIDIA FY2023; fiscal dates differ. Latest FY2025/26, see appendix. · Source: [S015] [S052] [S032] [S053] [S036] [S054] [S039] [S055] [S002] [S056] [S001] [S057] [S033] [S058] [S020] [S059] Phase What changed Investment consequence Late 2022–2023 Generative AI moved into broad commercial experimentation; accelerator demand accelerated. Installed software distribution mattered; the first bottleneck was often compute. 2024–2025 Larger clusters drew in HBM, networking, power equipment and cooling. A wider supplier list did not remove dependence on hyperscaler investment. 2026 Serving, long context and agent workloads increased attention to the entire system and customer economics. Track actual utilisation, cash conversion and replacement needs alongside orders. Periodisation is analytical, not an attribution of all company growth to AI. Acquisitions, pricing, recovery from weak years and ordinary cloud demand also contribute. Layman’s summary: AI has reshuffled the profit pool. It has not made every technology supplier a winner, and past revenue growth says little about what is already in the share price. 04 / From power to profit What happens when someone asks an AI a question? Training and serving are different workloads Training Examples → update model weights Trained model Stored weights are reused A user request Prompt text → tokens Prefill + decode Process context, then generate output using trained weights Response Decode / format and return the output KV cache = reusable attention state It occupies memory; it is not another physical memory-chip category. Takeaway: An ordinary response does not require training the whole model again. Read: Read the top path as model creation and the bottom path as serving one request. The dashed arrow denotes temporary serving state. Units: Conceptual process; conventional decoder-style language model · Date: Technical sources accessed 5 Nov 2026 · Source: [S060] [S049] Term Plain explanation Why investors should care Token A model-readable unit that can be a word, fragment or character. Revenue or cost per token is not the same as value per useful task. Prefill Process the known prompt and prepare attention state. Long prompts can require substantial computation. Decode Generate the response using earlier context and state. Interactive, low-batch serving can be memory-limited; other designs differ. Batching / caching Share work across requests or reuse already computed state. Can improve efficiency, but latency, memory and workload mix constrain gains. Architecture, context length, batch size and precision change the bottleneck. Avoid a single universal energy-per-query or tokens-per-second number. [S049] [S061] Layman’s summary: Training is preparing the factory’s process. Inference is using that process to fulfil orders. Better machines, memory and scheduling can each improve the result. 05 / From power to profit Electricity: scale matters, location matters more Global data-centre electricity demand is projected to almost double 2025 estimate 485 TWh 2030 projection 950 TWh Takeaway: The IEA projection implies substantial extra infrastructure demand, with uncertainty around the pace and location. Read: The filled bar is the 2025 estimate. The outlined bar is the IEA 2030 projection; it is not a reported outcome. Units: TWh per year; all data centres, not AI-only consumption · Date: IEA, 16 Apr 2026 · Source: [S041] A global energy total cannot tell you when one campus will connect. Local transmission capacity, transformers, permits and dependable supply determine the delivery schedule. Proposed grid-connection queues can contain speculative or duplicate projects, so announced megawatts are not the same as funded, operating demand. [S042] Measure What it means Do not confuse it with kW / MW / GW Power: the rate of energy use or supply. 1 GW = 1,000 MW = 1,000,000 kW. kWh / MWh / TWh, which measure energy over time. PUE Total facility energy ÷ IT equipment energy. The efficiency of the model, or useful output per token. Nameplate capacity A design or connection rating. Actual average use, customer utilisation or revenue. Illustration—not a project forecast: 100 MW of IT load at PUE 1.25 requires 125 MW at the facility level. If held constant for 8,760 hours, that equals 1,095,000 MWh, or 1.095 TWh. Lower PUE reduces overhead; it does not guarantee efficient computation. Investment implication: Equipment qualification, service capability and delivery reliability can be valuable. The test is whether orders convert into cash at an adequate return on the additional factories, inventories and warranties needed to fulfil them. 06 / From power to profit Who earns from power—and what does a PPA buy? Buying electricity and owning a power plant are different exposures Grid-connected supply Utility / generator → grid Contract may be a PPA Onsite generation Fuel, plant, permits, backup Grid connection may remain Reliable delivery Substation + switchgear UPS / storage + controls IT facility Compute + cooling Customers and service levels Takeaway: A power purchase agreement is a contract; it does not by itself transfer plant ownership or remove grid dependence. Read: Both supply routes still need reliable equipment and operational redundancy. This is a commercial schematic. Units: Conceptual relationships · Date: 5 Nov 2026 · Source: [S042] ; issuer contracts listed in the power source notes. [S076] [S077] [S078] Business Relevant companies Core-business comfort / risk Generation CEG / VST Existing nuclear/gas fleets and retail or contracted supply; power prices, outages, hedges and policy matter. Turbines / grid GEV / Siemens Energy Broader power-system demand and service fleets; long delivery cycles and execution obligations. Electrical management ETN / Schneider Electric Buildings, industry, utilities and other markets alongside data centres; acquisition and leverage risks. Engines / backup CAT / CMI Established industrial and transport demand; backup power does not equal continuous prime power. Company roles from annual filings and official disclosures. [S078] [S079] [S080] [S081] [S082] [S083] [S084] [S085] Contracted megawatts need a timetable. The Meta–Vistra agreements cover existing output and planned uprates over different dates; they do not mean Meta bought those plants. The power continues into the public grid. Similar care is needed with restart projects and nuclear approvals. [S076] [S077] [S078] Onsite power can solve one constraint and introduce others. Fuel supply, equipment lead times, redundancy, emissions approvals and operating economics still apply. An announced generation project should be followed through financing, construction and actual service. [S042] Layman’s summary: A long-term electricity contract resembles reserving supply. It is not the same investment as owning the factory that makes it. 07 / From power to profit Cooling: remove heat without confusing rack generations Direct-to-chip cooling transfers heat through connected loops Hot chips CPU / GPU Cold plates Rack loop Liquid carries heat away CDU Heat exchanger and controls Facility Heat rejection to outdoors Residual air cooling can remain for components outside the liquid loop. Closed liquid circuits do not mean zero water use across the whole facility. Takeaway: Liquid cooling changes the equipment mix; the facility still has to reject the heat. Read: Solid arrows show a simplified hot-side path; dashed arrows show return circulation. System boundaries vary by design. Units: Conceptual thermal flow; not a plumbing design · Date: 5 Nov 2026 · Source: [S086] [S138] [S087] Claim / reference Correct reading Status at the research cut-off GB200 NVL72 ~120 kW One named rack-scale system; source gives an approximate power rating. Current product documentation; CPUs/GPUs use liquid cooling, some air cooling remains. MGX 1.2 up to 250 kW Platform support / design envelope, not the measured demand of every rack. NVIDIA announcement, 12 Oct 2026. 600 kW A dated GTC 2025 roadmap statement for Rubin Ultra in the second half of 2027. Do not label as the verified operating rating of current Vera Rubin NVL72. Air cooling “stops at 50 kW” Cooling feasibility depends on airflow, temperatures, layout and equipment. No universal physical cutoff at exactly 50 kW established. Power is per rack only where specified. A rack, multi-rack domain and campus are not interchangeable. [S086] [S138] [S088] [S089] [S090] [S087] Ownership and product boundaries matter for the company map. Vertiv, Schneider, Eaton and other firms overlap in power/thermal systems. CoolIT is now an Ecolab subsidiary after the July 2026 acquisition; it has no standalone quoted share. This does not make every parent’s revenue an AI-cooling revenue stream. [S091] [S092] Layman’s summary: Cooling is a chain of heat transfers. The relevant investment question is who supplies the difficult, qualified parts—and whether the margin survives competition and redesign. 08 / From power to profit Compute: compare complete systems, not isolated headline numbers Role What it does Selected companies CPU Control, application and general-purpose work; also performs AI tasks. Intel, AMD, Arm-based designs and NVIDIA Vera. GPU / accelerator Highly parallel calculation for suitable model operations. NVIDIA, AMD; workload and software determine realised performance. Custom ASIC Purpose-designed architecture for a class of work; can support many models. Google TPU; Broadcom/Marvell custom-silicon programmes. Foundry / equipment Manufacture chips and supply the process tools. TSMC, Samsung, Intel; ASML, AMAT, Lam, KLA and Tokyo Electron. Intel is an integrated designer/manufacturer, not a fabless company. Foxconn is principally an assembly/manufacturing partner, not an advanced-node wafer foundry. [S050] [S062] [S020] [S029] One coherent specification sheet Pinned reference: DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 Source-stated rack figure GPU / CPU count 72 Rubin GPUs / 36 Vera CPUs GPU memory 20.7 TB HBM4 Aggregate GPU-memory bandwidth 1,400 TB/s NVLink bandwidth 216 TB/s Units: All figures refer to one rack; bandwidths are aggregate vendor ratings. Date: current 2026 datasheet accessed 5 Nov 2026. Source: [S051] Read: These are vendor specifications, not measured tokens/second or application-level throughput. The earlier July article has different per-GPU figures; they are not combined here. System economics depend on usable output at the required quality and latency. A faster arithmetic peak may have little value if memory, communication or power limits the workload. Costs include host CPUs, fabrics, storage, software and idle time, not simply the quoted accelerator price. Layman’s summary: A powerful engine is only one part of a vehicle. Assess the complete system and the task it must perform before comparing the manufacturers. 09 / From power to profit Memory and storage are complementary, not interchangeable Separate working memory from persistent storage On-chip cache / scratchpad Fast local working data; typically SRAM Accelerator HBM Stacked DRAM: model weights, activations and KV state Host DDR / LPDDR CPU working memory and data staging NAND SSD Persistent data with fast access Magnetic HDD Persistent mass-capacity data pools Takeaway: HBM is DRAM. The KV cache is data stored in memory, not a sixth chip type. Read: Top rows are volatile working memory; bottom rows retain data without power. No quantitative speed or capacity scale is implied. Units: Conceptual layers · Date: 5 Nov 2026 · Source: [S049] [S062] [S063] [S064] Capacity and bandwidth solve different problems. Capacity determines what fits; bandwidth affects how quickly data can move. A larger context or batch can consume more memory, while faster memory helps only when data movement is limiting performance. Neither removes all compute or network constraints. [S049] [S061] The three established HBM suppliers are a starting supplier map, not a permanent guarantee of scarcity. Micron, SK hynix and Samsung disclose HBM businesses. Generation qualification, yields, customer allocations and future capacity determine pricing. An undated “sold out” label is insufficient evidence of durable excess returns. [S063] [S065] [S066] Update the storage company boundary. Sandisk separated from Western Digital in February 2025 and trades as SNDK . WDC and STX represent HDD and mass-capacity storage exposure; they should not be credited with the separated Sandisk NAND/SSD business. [S067] [S068] Layman’s summary: HBM is a very fast workbench beside the processor. SSDs and hard drives are storage rooms. They solve different problems and have different pricing cycles. 10 / From power to profit Networking: bandwidth, latency and supplier concentration Different communication layers solve different problems Scale-up domain Accelerators cooperate closely Example: NVLink within a rack Scale-up domain Another rack / compute domain Its own local memory and links Scale-out fabric InfiniBand or Ethernet / RoCE connects domains Physical links to the fabric may be optical or copper, as appropriate. Takeaway: Optics, switch silicon and complete switches occupy related but distinct parts of the system. Read: Read the upper boxes as local compute domains and the bottom box as the wider cluster fabric. Physical media and protocol are different dimensions. Units: Conceptual topology; no bandwidth scale · Date: 5 Nov 2026 · Source: [S047] [S048] [S051] Layer / choice Company exposure Main qualification InfiniBand / Ethernet NVIDIA offers both; Arista and Cisco supply Ethernet systems. InfiniBand is an IBTA industry standard. Neither protocol is universally superior for all deployments. Switch / custom silicon Broadcom, Marvell; connectivity specialists such as Astera. Design wins, architecture changes and customer concentration drive results. Optical components / modules Coherent, Lumentum, InnoLight, Fabrinet. Optical technology, qualification, yields, inventories and manufacturing capacity matter. Fibre / connectors Corning and Amphenol. End-market breadth can help; growth still depends on mix and spending. RDMA allows direct memory access across systems; RoCE implements RDMA over Ethernet. Standards status does not imply a fragmented supplier market. [S047] [S048] [S069] [S070] [S071] [S072] [S073] [S074] Layman’s summary: More traffic creates demand for roads, junctions and connectors. Owning several road suppliers can still leave you exposed to one construction programme. 11 / From power to profit Software is a moat—but switching costs vary by workload Judge the cost of switching, not the slogan Source of advantage Why customers may stay What can weaken it Optimised libraries / kernels Proven performance and numerical behaviour save engineering time. Portable frameworks, better alternatives and standardised workloads. Production operations Teams know how to deploy, monitor and recover the platform. A sufficiently large cost/performance gain justifies migration work. Enterprise distribution Contracts, integrations, identity and data access make adoption easier. Customers resist extra charges or use competing applications. Workflow / proprietary data The application solves a valuable repeat problem. A cheaper model alone is not a moat; useful outcomes must persist. CUDA’s advantage includes an ecosystem of tools and operating experience. It is more than a programming-language label. However, high-level code is not always a complete rewrite: PyTorch’s HIP backend deliberately reuses CUDA-facing interfaces. Custom kernels, unsupported features and performance validation can still demand substantial work. [S062] [S075] Business group Existing revenue engine AI test Microsoft / Google / Amazon Enterprise software, advertising, cloud and commerce. Incremental customer spend and useful output versus infrastructure cost. Salesforce / ServiceNow / Intuit / Atlassian Business workflows, finance tools and collaboration. Attach rates, retention and whether automation changes seat-based pricing. Adobe / IBM / Palantir / Snowflake Creative software, enterprise platforms/services and data systems. Defendable workflows and data access; competition and valuation. These are qualitative business descriptions, not separately disclosed AI revenue figures. Annual sources appear with each company’s financial table. Layman’s summary: Familiar software reduces the customer’s effort and risk. The investment case is strongest when that convenience produces repeat revenue and cash, rather than merely a high switching-cost claim. 12 / From power to profit The economic engine: useful output, utilisation and price Idle capacity raises the fixed cost of each unit of useful output 1× 2× 3× 4× 25% 4.00× 50% 2.00× 75% 1.33× 100% 1.00× Productive utilisation (illustrative) Takeaway: At half utilisation, the fixed-cost component per unit doubles under these assumptions. Read: The curve assumes the same hardware, annual fixed cost, task mix and output per active hour. It excludes variable costs and is not an estimate for any company. Units: Fixed cost per unit relative to 100% utilisation = 1 ÷ utilisation · Date: Author illustration, 5 Nov 2026 · Source: Author calculation; serving-efficiency context [S093] [S049] Question Evidence to seek What it protects against Is output useful? Task success, quality, latency, paid adoption and retention. Token growth with little customer value. Is capacity productive? Utilisation, delivered sites, power availability and workload scheduling. Paying for installed assets that cannot earn. Does price cover cost? Realised pricing, service margin, support and replacement investment. Price competition outrunning efficiency improvements. Who funds the expansion? Customer advances, cash flows, leases, debt and stock issuance. Profitable accounting supported by fragile funding. Lower cost per task can expand demand without guaranteeing higher profit. Customers may consume more, competitors may reduce prices, or the mix may shift toward harder tasks. The useful test is the return earned on additional capital after these changes, not a fixed energy cost attached to one query. Layman’s summary: A cheaper factory process helps. Shareholders benefit when enough customers buy the output at a price that also pays for the machines, finance and future replacements. 13 / From power to profit Cash generation and the investment bill must be read together Large operating cash flow can coexist with a thin cash surplus Operating cash flow Cash capital expenditure GOOGL FY2025 164.7 91.4 MSFT FY2026 182.9 115.9 META FY2025 115.8 69.7 AMZN FY2025 139.5 131.8 ORCL FY2026 32.0 55.7 Takeaway: Oracle’s shown annual cash capex exceeded CFO; Amazon’s residual was small. Read: Compare the filled CFO bar with the outlined cash-capex bar within each company. Fiscal periods differ and lease-funded additions are not fully captured. Units: US$ billion; annual reported cash measures · Date: FY2025 or FY2026 as labelled; fiscal dates in appendix · Source: [S001] [S002] [S004] [S003] [S006] More recent evidence Period / amount Interpretation GOOGL Q3 2026 FCF −US$9.1bn; TTM FCF US$19.7bn Quarterly spending accelerated well beyond the old annual baseline. MSFT FY2027 Q1 FCF US$18.6bn; broader capex US$45.2bn Cash PP&E differs from capex including finance leases. AMZN TTM through Q3 2026 FCF −US$42.4bn This is a trailing year, not the same interval as the other rows. META Q3 2026 issuer FCF −US$2.12bn Issuer capex definition includes finance-lease principal. Latest released updates at 5 Nov 2026. Issuer FCF definitions and periods differ; do not add these rows or rank their magnitudes. [S094] [S095] [S096] [S097] A falling near-term cash surplus can be rational investment, but it raises the required evidence. Capacity must become usable, win paying workloads and earn attractive returns before replacement is needed. Monitor the business trajectory; do not equate every negative quarter with failure or every capital programme with value creation. 14 / From power to profit Depreciation, impairment and cash spending are different Company Verified policy / change What it means MSFT FY2026 server/network lives: 2–6 years. FY2027 announced building lives: 15 → 25 years. The latest change concerns datacentre/office buildings, not a blanket GPU-life extension. META Most servers/network assets extended to 5.5 years from 1 Jan 2025. FY2025 depreciation fell US$2.92bn; net income rose US$2.59bn for the stated asset cohort. AMZN A subset of servers/network equipment shortened from 6 → 5 years from 1 Jan 2025. FY2025 D&A rose US$1.4bn; net income fell US$1.0bn. The subset qualification matters. Sources: annual filings, September 2026 interim filings and Microsoft FY2026 Q4 call. Cash paid now; leases and vendor financing can shift the timing/classification. Depreciation Allocates depreciable cost over estimated useful life.
