entries.text: AI data centres · presentation notes Back to report and PowerPoint files AI data centres: presentation notes Formatted companion to the two five-slide public presentations. Prepared 5 November 2026. Historical evidence, projections and author interpretation retain their source-specific dates and caveats. Educational research, not personal investment advice. Financial briefing Slide 1 Key Message Begin with durable existing earnings, then test the return on new investment and the entry price. Talking Points Alphabet combines advertising, distribution and cloud. Microsoft combines enterprise productivity, cloud, security and developer tools. Existing customer relationships support the thesis; they do not guarantee profitable AI investment. Capital expenditure is an investment commitment, not AI revenue. Total R&D is also not a separately disclosed AI-only spending measure. GPUs, memory, networking and cooling can depend on the same customer budgets. Diversification requires different economic drivers, not just different product names. Alphabet and Microsoft are research candidates because they have substantial existing businesses. This is the author’s analytical judgement about business durability. It does not establish an entry price, allocation or expected return. How To Read Treat the three rows as separate tests: core earnings, investment payback and price/concentration. The counterargument challenges the core-business thesis. Assumptions / Risks AI may change search behaviour and software pricing. Established distribution can lose value if customer behaviour changes. Cash investment can rise faster than revenue. Investment valuation gains can also inflate accounting profit. No portfolio weights are assumed. Refresh prices and cash-flow evidence before dealing. These are simple residuals, not harmonised distributable cash. Later evidence is tighter: Alphabet Q3 2026 reported CFO 42.3, capex 51.4 and issuer FCF −9.1, in US$ billion. Its 2026 capex guidance was US$195–205bn. Amazon ’s trailing issuer FCF through September was US$−42.4bn. Microsoft ’s September quarter cash capex was US$39.367bn. Slide 3 Key Message Several technologies can still concentrate a portfolio in one capital-spending cycle. Talking Points Microsoft and Alphabet have established software, advertising and cloud businesses. Their breadth helps, but AI can change existing revenue economics and increase infrastructure spending. NVIDIA , Broadcom, HBM manufacturers, Arista and Vertiv supply different products. Hyperscaler buildout budgets can nevertheless affect them together. HBM is a memory category, not a ticker. Eaton and Schneider Electric serve buildings, industry and wider power systems. Amphenol serves several equipment markets. Check actual customer mix and cash conversion rather than counting end-market labels. Acquisitions change the comparison: Eaton completed Boyd Thermal in March 2026; Schneider’s announced PTC deal remained pending; Amphenol completed the CommScope connectivity deal in January 2026. How To Read Read across each row from business type to earnings support and exposure. This qualitative matrix assigns no AI-revenue percentages or diversification scores. Colours identify companies, not investment direction. Assumptions / Risks Broader operations do not remove leverage, cyclicality or dependence on a few large buyers. Broadcom’s software business does not eliminate concentration in incremental AI-silicon demand. Specialised suppliers can have strong qualification, software or process advantages. Diversification alone does not establish a superior investment. Review the post-acquisition mix, debt and customer exposure before purchase. Fabrinet: 256.725 − 252.503 = 4.222, US$ million. Deducting the excluded US$1.181m purchased intangibles leaves US$3.041m. Net income includes a US$56.743m non-marketable equity-security gain. Coherent/Fabrinet use FY2026; Amphenol uses FY2025. These are different annual periods, with exact dates shown. The residual excludes acquisitions, intangibles and noncash additions. Slide 5 Key Message The company list is the author’s analytical judgement about established business support and the questions that require further research. Talking Points Alphabet has advertising, cloud and distribution businesses. Research whether AI adoption preserves search economics and produces durable operating cash returns. Microsoft has enterprise software and cloud franchises. Assess cash returns after infrastructure investment, competition and changing software pricing. TSMC manufactures chips for AI and other markets. Taiwan exposure, capital intensity, utilisation and customer concentration remain material. NVIDIA combines accelerated computing with a software ecosystem. Demand depends on customer investment, product competitiveness and competing chip designs. Amphenol remains an additional research candidate. Acquisitions change its business mix and funding needs. How To Read Each row pairs existing business support with a principal risk and a research condition. The rows are qualitative assessments rather than a return ranking. Assumptions / Risks No share-price snapshot, fair-value estimate, allocation or instruction to transact is supplied. A separate current valuation assessment is necessary before any investment decision. Hardware suppliers can share exposure to the same hyperscaler spending cycle. Public filings describe historical performance and risks rather than guaranteed future outcomes. TSM denotes the US ADR. TSMC reports its financial statements in New Taiwan dollars. HPC revenue includes non-AI computing. Investment valuation gains and OpenAI-related impacts may affect headline profit. Review recurring operations and funding separately. Clear visual story Slide 1 Key Message AI demand growth creates opportunities, but shareholder returns still depend on the durability of existing earnings, cash after reinvestment and the entry price. Talking Points The central investment preference is a business with valuable customers and revenue engines that can support it through a slower AI capital-spending cycle. Alphabet and Microsoft are examples of businesses with substantial existing advertising, enterprise software and cloud franchises. These franchises remain exposed to competition and AI-driven changes. Higher sales or reported net income do not ensure stronger cash generation. Inventory, new factories, data-centre construction, debt and acquisitions can absorb cash before shareholders receive it. Price determines the margin for error. The company list at the end identifies questions for further assessment. It represents the author’s analytical judgement, without an entry price, allocation or instruction to transact. How To Read Read the three rows as independent tests of one investment. A company needs a credible core business, economic cash generation and an acceptable price. This opening contains no return forecast. Caveats These are analytical judgements based on the stated preference for core-business breadth. Diversifying across several suppliers does not necessarily diversify the common hyperscaler spending cycle. The research cut-off is 5 November 2026 in Singapore. Source fiscal years differ. Historical statements do not guarantee future cash generation or share-price performance. Sources Alphabet Inc.: FY2025 financial statements, segments and investment gains. Publication / update: 2026-02-05. Period / scope: FY2025. Accessed 5 November 2026. Microsoft Corporation: FY2026 statements, segments, OpenAI impact. Period / scope: FY ended 2026-06-30. Accessed 5 November 2026. Slide 2 Key Message An AI answer relies on a complete operating system. Faster chips alone cannot ensure faster or cheaper service. Talking Points Conventional language-model inference tokenises a prompt, processes it during prefill and generates tokens during decode. It reuses trained weights for each response. CPUs handle general and control work. GPUs and custom ASICs such as TPUs accelerate suitable workloads. Software schedules work. Power supplies equipment and cooling carries heat away. HBM is stacked DRAM for weights and working state. Capacity determines what fits. Bandwidth affects data movement. The KV cache is stored data, not a chip category. Local scale-up links and wider scale-out fabrics serve different roles. InfiniBand is an industry standard. RoCE carries RDMA over Ethernet. NVIDIA acquired Mellanox, not the standard. How To Read Centre: calculation. Top: software control. Sides: electricity and heat. Lower double-headed links: data communication. These arrows show functional relationships rather than a serial pipeline. Caveats CPU-only deployments may not need HBM. The diagram omits host DRAM, cache, storage and other support systems. Low-batch decode can be memory-bandwidth-limited. Long-prompt prefill is often compute-intensive. Batch size, model design and workload can change the bottleneck. No networking protocol wins universally. This diagram supplies no rack-power, energy-per-query or performance estimate. Sources LLMs: What is a large language model?. Mastering LLM Techniques: Inference Optimization. Publication / update: 2023-11-17. Period / scope: Causal language-model inference, prefill/decode, weights, KV cache, model parallelism and serving optimizations. Read article body, not its generated summary. Accessed 5 November 2026. TPU architecture. Publication / update: 2026-10-26. Period / scope: CPU/GPU/TPU roles, ASIC definition, matrix operations and host/device relationship. Date is last update. Period / scope: Product definitions: DRAM/HBM/DDR/LPDDR/GDDR/NAND; HBM production; capacity, demand, qualification and cyclicality risks. Filing date: 9 October 2026. Accessed 5 November 2026. InfiniBand Specification Frequently Asked Questions. Publication / update: 2026-09-21. Period / scope: Visible page revision timestamp. InfiniBand industry standard; IBTA defines InfiniBand and RoCE; RDMA over Ethernet. Trade-association performance promotion is not treated as an independent comparison. Accessed 5 November 2026. NVIDIA DGX GB200 hardware guide. Publication / update: 2026-09-17 (last update). Accessed 5 November 2026. Slide 3 Key Message The IEA projects a large increase in global data-centre electricity use, but the investment opportunity depends on where and when usable capacity arrives. Talking Points The IEA estimates 485 TWh of global data-centre electricity consumption in 2025 and projects 950 TWh in 2030. These are the exact source-stated values used in the chart. The series covers all data centres, including AI and other computing workloads. It must not be relabelled as AI-only electricity demand. The forecast strengthens the case for examining power delivery, grid equipment, cooling and reliable operations. It does not establish the margins or returns that any individual supplier will earn. The timing of a local campus depends on transmission and connection capacity, equipment, construction and reliable supply. Announced megawatts and project queues can overstate capacity that will actually enter service. How To Read Both bars use the same scale in terawatt-hours per year. The filled bar is the 2025 estimate. The outlined bar is the 2030 projection. Zero is the chart baseline. The forecast is visibly distinct in colour and in greyscale. Caveats 2030 is a forecast rather than a reported outcome. Its path can change with AI adoption, efficiency, utilisation, geography and the delivery of power infrastructure. TWh measures energy over time. It is different from the kW, MW or GW ratings of equipment and campuses. This chart cannot establish the energy used by one query or one rack. No percentage or multiple has been rounded onto the slide. The comparison uses the exact source-stated 485 and 950 TWh values. Sources International Energy Agency: Key Questions on Energy and AI, executive summary. Publication / update: 2026-04-16. Period / scope: 2025 estimate and 2030 projection. Accessed 5 November 2026. International Energy Agency: Powering Artificial Intelligence, executive summary. Publication / update: 2026-10-14. Period / scope: Power and infrastructure constraints. Accessed 5 November 2026. Attribution Chart recreated from IEA (2026), Key Questions on Energy and AI, IEA, Paris. Values retained and visual format adapted. Source: Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Slide 4 Key Message Reported profit can stay positive while cash after equipment investment turns negative. Coherent illustrates why cash conversion matters. Talking Points FY2026 ended 30 June 2026. Coherent reported US$786.884 million of consolidated net income, US$79.514 million of operating cash flow and US$1,102.909 million of cash PP&E capex. Exact calculation: US$79.514 million − US$1,102.909 million = −US$1,023.395 million of simple free cash flow. Management attributed weaker operating cash flow primarily to inventory growth, partly offset by payables and higher earnings. Inventory used US$1,183.000 million of cash. Additional capacity can create future value, but the investment must earn an adequate return and the funding must last. How To Read Read the left profit figure separately from the cash table. Subtract capex from operating cash flow. Minus signs identify the outflow and deficit. Caveats Net income is consolidated. It differs from income attributable to Coherent and income available to common shareholders. Simple FCF is our calculation and may differ from the issuer’s definition. It excludes acquisitions, purchased intangibles and noncash additions, and does not equal automatically distributable cash. This table does not reconcile profit to operating cash flow. Other adjustments included business disposals. Amounts preserve US$1 thousand precision, converted exactly to US$ million. This is a historical year, not a forecast. Slide 5 Key Message These companies are research candidates based on the author’s analytical judgement about established core businesses. Cash returns, valuation and concentration require separate checks. Talking Points Alphabet has advertising, cloud and distribution businesses. Review search economics and the cash returns on AI investment. Microsoft has enterprise software and cloud franchises. Review competitive pressure, investment intensity and cash generation after infrastructure spending. TSMC adds manufacturing exposure across AI and other markets. Taiwan exposure, capital intensity, customer concentration and chip cyclicality remain material. Amphenol serves several connectivity markets. Review acquisition integration, funding and its growing data-centre exposure. ASML and KLA carry semiconductor-cycle and export-control risks. Schneider and Eaton require checks on acquisitions and leverage. NVIDIA and Vertiv share exposure to customer investment budgets. How To Read Each row pairs a research lens with business support and a material condition. The company selection is qualitative and does not prescribe a transaction. TSMC reports its accounts in New Taiwan dollars. HPC revenue includes non-AI computing. Several hardware holdings can depend on the same hyperscaler spending cycle. entries.text: The AI selloff hit suppliers hardest | 6 November 2026 Skip to report MARKET INTELLIGENCE HUB RESEARCH BRIEF / 06 NOV 2026 ← Research Explained · Download the six-page PDF Historical public-market research, not personalised investment advice. Prices are dated observations, not live quotes. Public edition checked 6 November 2026; two sector observations that could not be independently confirmed are omitted. MARKETS RESEARCH / 5 NOVEMBER US CLOSE The AI selloff hit suppliers hardest A selloff in memory and chipmakers reached every S&P 500 sector. The companies buying the equipment held up better. Shorter Treasury yields fell furthest, and the Swiss franc strengthened in Asia. FIELD NOTES 05 / 11 US market session Issued 6 November 2026 Singapore United States Singapore AI US Treasuries USD/CHF Elections SEMICONDUCTORS −12.2% Philadelphia chip index 5 Nov US close [4] 2-YEAR TREASURY −12 bp Yield fell to 4.46% 5 Nov US session [11] SWISS FRANC +0.2% CHF versus USD 6 Nov early Asia [13] In this report Overview 01 · US close 02 · AI companies 03 · Treasuries & FX 04 · Singapore 05 · Portfolio review 06 · Sources Next section ↓ US close · AI companies · Treasuries & FX · Singapore · Portfolio review · Sources 01 THE US CLOSE How the rally reversed EXHIBIT 01 • PRICE PERFORMANCE Chip shares fell more than twice as far as the Nasdaq Composite US market close · 5 Nov 2026 · one-day price change (%) Philadelphia Semiconductor Index −12.2% Nasdaq Composite −5.52% S&P 500 −4.36% Dow Jones Industrial Average −3.44% −15% 0% How to read Each bar starts at zero. A longer bar to the left means a larger one-day loss. Each benchmark holds a different basket of shares. Sources [2] Reuters · [4] Reuters View data table Benchmark Price change Philadelphia Semiconductor Index −12.2% Nasdaq Composite −5.52% S&P 500 −4.36% Dow Jones Industrial Average −3.44% The divergence started during the rally On 4 November the S&P 500 gained 1.6% as the election result reduced uncertainty, yet the Philadelphia chip index fell 3.1%. The next day the S&P 500 closed at 7,353.73 and all 11 sectors declined. The market had already begun to distinguish equipment suppliers from their customers before the broad selloff. Sources [1] Reuters · [2] Reuters · [3] Reuters via CNA ANALYSIS Why the election mattered to investors Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Local votes and opposition to data-centre projects raised questions about permitting, power and water. A longer approval process can push a chip order into a later quarter. The size of that delay remains unknown. Sources [1] Reuters · [6] Reuters 02 THE AI VALUE CHAIN One buyer’s spending is another company’s revenue A delay can move the same cash payment in opposite directions on two companies’ accounts. That difference helps explain the relative share-price moves. EXHIBIT 02 • COMPANY COMPARISON Three ways to own the AI buildout Selected US shares · 5 Nov 2026 close · one-day price change (%) 01 Memory and storage SanDisk −22.26% Micron −17.46% Seagate −16.25% Customers can defer purchases of memory and drives when new server capacity is delayed. 02 Chips and equipment AMD −17.26% Lam Research −16.36% Nvidia −9.26% Chip and equipment orders depend on build schedules. When many funds hold the same shares, selling can magnify price moves. 03 Cloud platforms Amazon −2.2% Alphabet −2.2% Microsoft −3.58% Later payments can preserve near-term cash. Delayed capacity can also postpone future cloud revenue. How to read Read across each row from the share-price change to the possible business effect. These are individual stocks. Amazon and Alphabet are shown at Reuters’ reported precision. Sources [2] Reuters · [3] Reuters via CNA · [8] Closing-price cross-checks Amazon shows why investors weighed both sides AWS sales grew 39.3% year on year in the September quarter. At group level, Amazon reported a US $42.4 billion free cash outflow over the trailing twelve months. Microsoft reported 48% year-on-year growth in Azure revenue in its September quarter. Sales growth and cash available after investment answer different questions. Sources [9] Amazon · [10] Microsoft ANALYSIS Who was selling? Managers interviewed by Reuters described institutional selling and hedge funds reducing leverage. Qualcomm ’s smartphone-chip sales missed estimates, while Arm guided next-quarter revenue slightly above consensus. Positioning helps explain why selling spread across companies with different earnings news. The interviews give no seller-by-seller flow totals. Sources [2] Reuters · [6] Reuters · [7] Reuters via MarketScreener 03 CROSS-ASSET MARKETS Treasury yields fell fastest at the front end Treasuries , gold and the Swiss franc provided three different price signals. They were observed at different times and reveal no dollar amount transferred from equities. EXHIBIT 03 • INTEREST RATES The 2-year yield fell four times as much as the 30-year yield US Treasury par yields · 4–5 Nov 2026 · % per annum and basis points −12 bp 2 years −10 bp 5 years −6 bp 10 years −3 bp 30 years Maturity 4 Nov 5 Nov Change 2 years 4.58% 4.46% −12 bp 5 years 4.69% 4.59% −10 bp 10 years 4.90% 4.84% −6 bp 30 years 5.28% 5.25% −3 bp How to read A longer downward bar shows a larger yield decline. Lower yields generally mean higher bond prices. These are indicative constant-maturity par yields near 3:30 pm New York time. An individual bond’s price return depends on its duration. Sources [11] US Treasury ANALYSIS The curve bull-steepened The 10-year minus 2-year spread widened by 6 bp. On 4 November, 4.90% − 4.58% = 0.32 percentage points, or 32 bp. On 5 November, 4.84% − 4.46% = 0.38 percentage points, or 38 bp. Both yields fell, with the short yield falling faster. One basis point equals 0.01 percentage point. Sources [11] US Treasury Gold gained, then gave back part of its rise Spot gold reached US $4,146.63 per troy ounce during 5 November trading. At 2:05 pm New York time Reuters put it at US $4,100.27 , up 1% on the day. The high and the later quote describe two different moments. Sources [12] Reuters Yes, CHF strengthened In early Asian trading on 6 November, CHF gained 0.2% against USD . The yen also gained 0.2% before giving back part of its move. The US dollar index was roughly flat at 101.55. For someone funding USD assets in francs, a stronger CHF increases the debt measured in USD. Sources [13] Reuters 04 SECTORS AND SINGAPORE Singapore ’s link runs through the chip supply chain The sector spread shows how differently businesses traded on the same day. For a Singapore holding, its customers and order book are more informative than the exchange where its shares trade. EXHIBIT 04 • PRICE PERFORMANCE Technology fell furthest among these four sectors Selected S&P 500 sector indices · 5 Nov 2026 close · one-day price change (%) Information technology −7.30% Industrials −4.12% Communication services −1.86% Utilities −0.71% −8% 0% How to read All 11 sectors fell. These four selected sector price indices show the range of declines. A longer bar to the left means a larger one-day loss. These are sector indices, not ETF returns. Sources [3] Reuters via CNA · [5] Sector-price cross-checks View data table Benchmark Price change Information technology −7.30% Industrials −4.12% Communication services −1.86% Utilities −0.71% The regional exposure is tangible In Asian trading on 6 November, Reuters reported Samsung Electronics down nearly 10% and SK Hynix down 12% during the session. In Singapore , Micron broke ground in January on a NAND flash-memory fab, with about US $24 billion planned over ten years and wafer output scheduled for the second half of 2028. Sources [4] Reuters · [14] Micron ANALYSIS What to check in a Singapore holding Start with the company’s customers. A supplier of specialised parts may see orders move if a fab delays equipment deliveries. A Singapore bank would need a different transmission route, such as borrower or collateral exposure. A manufacturer’s investment plan alone gives no estimate of the STI’s sensitivity. 05 PORTFOLIO REVIEW Review the same risk across shares, notes and loans An investor can hold a chip company directly, own it again through a fund and write downside exposure on it through a structured note. Each position responds differently to the same fall. 01 · Find repeated holdings List direct shares, look through fund holdings and record each structured note’s underlyings. Keep funded equity exposure and contingent note exposure in separate columns. Summing all note notionals as if they were shares would overstate or understate the immediate price sensitivity. 02 · Locate the weakest share in each fixed coupon note For a worst-of basket, divide each share’s spot price by its own initial fixing and rank the results. Then check the barrier, observation method, strike and maturity in the term sheet. If the share is above the barrier, the fall from today’s price to the barrier equals 1 − (barrier price ÷ current price). A prior knock-in can still lead to par redemption under some terms. Sources [15] Standard Chartered Singapore 03 · Match Treasury duration to the cash need A STRIP makes one payment at maturity and pays no interim coupon. A holder needing cash earlier can compare the current bid on the actual STRIP with the proceeds and reinvestment yield available at a shorter maturity. Shortening duration reduces sensitivity to a renewed rise in long yields but introduces earlier reinvestment risk. Sources [11] US Treasury · [16] TreasuryDirect ANALYSIS 04 · A CHF loan can magnify a USD drawdown With USD/CHF quoted as francs per dollar, USD value of CHF debt = CHF principal ÷ USD/CHF . A lower USD/CHF raises the USD liability. If pledged US stocks fall at the same time, collateral also shrinks. Check the facility’s recognised collateral values, loan balance, liquidity and margin threshold. For SGD borrowing, run the comparison using USD/SGD . Sources [13] Reuters · [17] DBS Singapore Next evidence to watch Compare data-centre approvals with actual equipment orders, cloud revenue with cash capex, and the returns of suppliers with those of buyers. Order deferrals and cancellations have different implications for future sales. 06 SOURCES AND DEFINITIONS Sources and reading notes US equity changes compare the 5 November close with the previous close. The 6 November Asian moves are intraday observations. Calculations use the displayed source values. 01 Reuters · Wall Street rallies after the midterms 4 Nov 2026 02 Reuters · Nasdaq correction and US closing prices 5 Nov 2026 03 Reuters via CNA · Trading Day market recap 5 Nov US session 04 Reuters · Asia trading and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index 6 Nov 2026 05 Public sector-price cross-checks 5 Nov 2026 close: Xinhua via The Star · technology and industrials ; MarketScreener · utilities ; EODData · communication services . Quote pages may show later sessions. 06 Reuters · Fund managers on selling and data-centre permitting 5 Nov 2026 07 Reuters via MarketScreener · Arm’s revenue outlook 4 Nov 2026 08 Public closing-price cross-checks 5 Nov 2026 close: Swingfolio · dated US stock recap ; Quant500 · Seagate closing-price table . Quant500 updates after later sessions. 09 Amazon · Third-quarter results, SEC exhibit 99.1 29 Oct 2026 10 Microsoft · First-quarter FY2027 results 28 Oct 2026 11 US Treasury · Daily Treasury par yield curve 4–5 Nov 2026 12 Reuters · Spot gold and US gold futures 5 Nov 2026 13 Reuters · Dollar, yen and Swiss franc in Asia 6 Nov 2026, early Asian trading 14 Micron · New Singapore NAND wafer fab 27 Jan 2026, Singapore dateline 15 Standard Chartered Singapore · Fixed coupon notes Product mechanics, accessed 6 Nov 2026 16 TreasuryDirect · How Treasury STRIPS work Instrument reference, accessed 6 Nov 2026 17 DBS Singapore · Understanding investment financing Facility mechanics, accessed 6 Nov 2026 Figures retain their source precision. bp = basis point. Capex = capital expenditure. NAND = non-volatile flash memory. A hyperscaler operates cloud infrastructure at very large scale. Sector figures use S&P 500 sector indices. Chart values are available in text. MARKET INTELLIGENCE HUB Independent market commentary · 6 November 2026 · Singapore Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged Back to top ↑

entries.text: AI & Technology | My thoughts | Research Explained ← Research Explained Research report · 5 November 2026 · Singapore AI & Technology: My business-quality and cash-flow framework Which companies still deserve new capital? A 40-company comparison built around established businesses, cash generation, revenue resilience and the price paid. My thoughts · Public research edition · 5 November 2026, Singapore time. Original analysis, issuer financials and external source links. Third-party valuation/rating tables are omitted from this edition. My central test Verify the starting financial claims What changed after late 2022 Follow the demand dependencies R&D is not total AI investment Audit of your 20 R&D figures Cash generation versus reinvestment The latest cash-payback test Normalize the earnings denominator Physical businesses and pricing power Financing links and correlated risk Risk scenarios and buying discipline Issuer financial comparisons Search 40 company profiles Methodology and sources 01 My central test I look for an established business that can fund investment, survive competition and turn growth into shareholder cash. The largest announced AI budget is not itself an investment merit. Microsoft offers several established revenue engines. Alphabet combines Search, YouTube and Cloud, but advertising and investment payback remain central. TSMC, ASML and KLA provide different capabilities within a shared semiconductor spending cycle. Meta adds another company, but limited diversification of the advertising driver. Business quality does not settle the purchase price. This public edition retains the operating analysis and issuer financials, while omitting the third-party valuation/rating dataset and the chart derived from it. It therefore does not present a current buy-price ranking. External research stays with its publisher. 02 Verify the starting financial claims Most of the supplied revenue and margin figures are supported once their periods are identified. Sources: company filings and official releases. Source details and exact chart data in chart_metadata.json. As of 5 Nov 2026 SGT · Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged · Unmapped issuers: ordinary slate. The first wave rewarded scarce compute and supporting infrastructure. Accelerators, high-bandwidth memory, advanced manufacturing and networking expanded as cloud platforms built capacity. New product launches and customers appear in the company timelines. Revenue growth alone does not establish how much of the change was caused by AI. The next investment question is cash payback. entries.text: AI & technology: business quality and cash discipline My Research Earlier published edition All editions Research Explained · 7 November 2026, Singapore · Public-source abridged edition AI & technology: business quality and cash discipline Pending further review of the information. This edition publishes only the public-source material and original explanatory analysis retained after removing unsuitable third-party content. It is not the complete original V2 report. No current market prices or investment returns are asserted. What survives the public-source review Start with the underlying earnings engine. An AI label is not a valuation method. Examine the business that funds investment and the return earned on new capacity. Different suppliers can depend on the same budgets. Hardware, networking, power and cooling can share exposure to a small group of infrastructure buyers. Accounting profit and cash after investment are different tests. Review working capital, physical investment, leases, acquisitions and dilution separately. This edition has no analyst-derived buy list. Target prices, fair values, ratings and proprietary valuation comparisons have been removed, together with conclusions that depend on them. The demand chain is not independent diversification Demand and monetisation Customers must obtain enough value to keep paying. Software adoption, cloud utilisation and pricing determine whether infrastructure produces attractive revenue and margins. Infrastructure suppliers Customer capital expenditure becomes supplier revenue. Chip, networking, server and component demand can rise together, but can also slow together if investment budgets are cut. Physical constraints Compute requires operating infrastructure. Power availability, connections, cooling, construction and delivery schedules can limit deployment even when chips are available. Portfolio implication Count shared customers, not only ticker symbols. Owning several supply-chain layers may leave the portfolio concentrated in one spending cycle. This is original risk analysis, not a forecast of a downturn. A verified historical business anchor Microsoft, fiscal year ended 30 June 2025 Issuer-reported result Revenue US$281.7 billion Operating income US$128.5 billion Microsoft had a substantial operating business before any new investment case is made. These rounded historical figures come from its FY2025 annual report. They are not current run-rate estimates, AI-only revenue or evidence that the shares are attractively priced. [1] The next question is incremental return. Established earnings can fund investment, but that alone does not show whether each new data centre or product earns enough to justify its cost. Read later filings before making a current investment decision. Power demand: an estimate is not a realised outcome Historical source vintage: IEA Energy and AI, 2025. All data centres worldwide; electricity in terawatt-hours (TWh). Not AI-only consumption. 2024 estimate 415 TWh 2030 forecast 945 TWh 0 1,000 TWh Original chart from IEA 2025 figures, zero baseline. Dashed outline marks the forecast, not an observed value. Source [2], CC BY 4.0. No intermediate forecast path is inferred. The forecast describes potential system demand, not guaranteed company revenue. Efficiency, utilisation, local grid constraints and deployment timing can change electricity needs. This intentionally uses the identified 2025 publication rather than claiming to reproduce the latest IEA forecast. Technology specifications need their own boundaries NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL72 is a specific system. The official product page describes 36 Grace CPUs and 72 Blackwell GPUs in a liquid-cooled rack-scale design. [3] These are product specifications, not the installed global fleet or a forecast of unit sales. Distinction Why it changes the investment reading Delivered product versus roadmap A future architecture limit does not establish actual power demand, deployment or sales today. Physical equipment versus software Hardware replacement, software migration, support and compatibility affect customer economics differently. Memory versus storage Serving a similar end market does not mean each component supplier has the same demand, substitution risk or pricing power. Accounting life versus economic usefulness Depreciation is an accounting allocation. It does not guarantee that equipment will remain competitive for the assumed life. No generic rack-power figure is asserted here. Power, cooling and networking claims must be tied to the exact configuration and document date. A cash-flow checklist that does not depend on analyst ratings Test What to inspect Common misreading Operating cash generation Cash-flow statement, receivables, inventory and payables. Assuming one strong quarter represents durable conversion. Cash remaining after equipment investment Operating cash flow less cash purchases of property, plant and equipment. Calling this a universally comparable free-cash-flow figure without checking definitions. Leases and commitments Lease notes, financing cash flows and purchase commitments. Assuming all infrastructure investment appears in cash PP&E immediately. Acquisitions and dilution Acquisition cash outflows, new debt, stock consideration and share count. Ignoring the cost of buying growth or treating share compensation as costless. Valuation Current price, current balance sheet, consistent earnings/cash definitions and explicit assumptions. Treating a discount to an old model as a promised return. Use comparable periods and currencies. Quarterly, annual and trailing figures should not be silently mixed. Compare both the cash-flow measure and the obligations excluded from it. What would strengthen or weaken the thesis? Stronger evidence Customer usage and paid adoption rise alongside margins. Operating cash growth supports the investment programme. New capacity produces returns without repeated external financing. Customer concentration falls or contracts become more durable. Weaker evidence Orders rise but cash collection deteriorates. Equipment deployment outpaces utilisation. Price competition erodes cash returns. Debt, leases or acquisition integration create additional funding needs. These are monitoring conditions, not numerical forecasts. No probability, target price or purchase recommendation is manufactured to fill the removed analyst sections. Scope of the public edition This is an abridged replacement, not the complete 49-page V2. The proprietary analyst profiles, ratings, fair values, target-price screens and valuation-derived calls are omitted. The full multi-company financial appendix and refreshed quarterly figures are not reproduced because their precise source records were not independently reverified for this edition. entries.text: Compare the 2041 bonds before adding more duration Research Explained · 7 November 2026, Singapore · Public comparison addendum Compare the 2041 bonds before adding more duration Temasek 2041 is the closer maturity comparison to the 2041 Treasury. The 2070 bond is a substantially longer risk position, even if its extra quoted yield looks small. Pending further information review. This public addendum uses the selected dated facts already checked in the 6 November bond report . It is not a new live quote or an update after US payrolls. The requested bulk market-price comparison and buyback analysis are omitted pending compatible source evidence. Three takeaways Match the cash flows, not just the maturity year. Two bonds both labelled 2041 can have different coupons, maturities, duration and call terms. The quoted yield gap is not a clean credit spread. These observations have different timestamps; an exact spread needs aligned market inputs and appropriate cash-flow discounting. More maturity is not automatically better value. The 2070 quote gives 15bp more yield than Temasek 2041 but about 65% more modified duration. Read the original quote timestamps before comparing Instrument Coupon / maturity Clean ask per US$100 Ask YTM Displayed quote US Treasury 4.75% / 15 Feb 2041 97.006 5.046% 6 Nov, 1:01pm Temasek Financial (I) 2.375% / Aug 2041 69.964 5.347% 5 Nov, 4:28pm Temasek Financial (I) 2.50% / 6 Oct 2070 50.514 5.497% 5 Nov, 4:28pm These are historical indicative ask observations, not executable offers. The source displayed no timezone. They were checked at 13:06 Singapore time on 6 November in the original report. Clean prices exclude accrued interest; fees, FX and dealer markup can change the cost. The arithmetic gap between the two 2041 yields is 30.1 basis points. Calculation: (5.347 − 5.046) × 100 = 30.1bp. This is a non-synchronous quoted-yield difference, not an option-adjusted or matched-cash-flow credit spread, and not evidence of current cheapness. The 2070 adds much more price sensitivity Modified duration, years · 5 November snapshot Treasury 2041: 10.081 Temasek 2041: 11.550 Temasek 2070: 19.042 Common scale: 0–20 years. Selected Bondsupermart duration observations retained in the original report; not newly refreshed. Duration approximates the price response to a small yield change. A duration of 19 implies approximately a 19% price fall for a one-percentage-point yield rise, before convexity and other effects. It does not mean a guaranteed loss, a maturity date or a holding period. The maturity extension increases quoted duration by 64.87%. Calculation: (19.042 ÷ 11.550 − 1) × 100. The corresponding ask-YTM increase is only 0.150 percentage points, or 15bp. This comparison is descriptive, not a complete valuation model. Corporate yield changes contain more than Treasury-rate changes. Interest-rate risk, credit spreads, liquidity and call-option effects can move in different directions. These source durations are not independently reconstructed effective durations or option-adjusted estimates. A fair same-maturity comparison takes four steps 1 · Match currency Compare USD cash flows with a USD benchmark. 2 · Align timestamps Use the same quote time, side and settlement. 3 · Match cash-flow risk Account for coupon, maturity, duration and calls. 4 · Compare net outcomes Include accrued interest, fees, spread and FX. The Treasury par curve is a benchmark, not a menu of executable securities. There is no official 15-year point in the standard US Treasury par table. Interpolating between 10Y and 20Y is an approximation, not proof that a specific bond is undervalued. The 2070 also has no matching 44-year Treasury benchmark. Use the full verified curve alongside this comparison. The separate bond review contains 14 official tenors for 3–5 November. Source: US Treasury interest-rate statistics . Issuer strength does not remove credit or currency risk Temasek bonds are not Singapore government bonds. They are issued by Temasek Financial (I) with a Temasek Holdings guarantee, not a Singapore Government guarantee. Check Temasek’s bond disclosures and the relevant issue documents, including call terms. A USD gain is not necessarily an SGD gain. Without hedging and intermediate cash flows, SGD return = (1 + USD investment return) × (1 + USD/SGD change) − 1. For example, a hypothetical 2% USD gain and 3% USD depreciation produce −1.06% in SGD before costs. Review notes: what is not included No WSJ bulk price table or third-party chart screenshot is reproduced. Public visibility alone does not establish reuse rights. This addendum instead carries forward a small, attributed set of already-published facts and original calculations. It does not reproduce the private 37-page source PDF. The requested exact same-maturity market comparison is still incomplete. It needs synchronous executable quotes, settlement conventions, accrued interest, cash-flow schedules, call terms and dealer costs. No buyback programme, offer price, eligibility or effect is asserted without an issuer notice. The old reports and their dated inputs remain separate. Nothing here refreshes their observation date or represents a trade as executed. Information is pending further review; the limitations above are specific rather than a substitute for evidence. Original educational analysis using dated cited observations. No personalised recommendation or promise of return. entries.text: The bond story across the earlier reports | 6 Nov 2026 Market Intelligence Hub Research Explained All editions Skip to research Yield desk Bonds Scenario maths Global Markets & Credit Research Bond review • 6 November 2026 • Dated educational research The bond story across the earlier reports Three risks. One bond portfolio. The real choice is not simply “Treasuries or corporate bonds”. It is how much interest-rate risk, borrower risk and financing risk to accept, and what compensation each one offers. Review window: 23 October–6 November 2026 • Editorial cutoff: 6 November 2026, 16:57 SGT Daily yield exhibit: 5 November U.S. observations • Shared history: completed monthly periods only US Treasuries Investment-grade credit High-yield credit Private credit CHF financing Research synthesis, not a trade instruction 01 / DURATION Lower yields help, but not equally. A long bond’s cash-flow timing matters as much as the direction of the yield move. 02 / CREDIT Separate the yield from the spread. A large coupon can compensate for a weak borrower, not just reward patience. 03 / REPAYMENT Watch cash payments before defaults. Arrears, nonaccruals, PIK and formal defaults are different signals. 04 / FINANCING Holding power needs a liquidity buffer. Positive investor equity does not mean a financed account has sufficient collateral headroom. Pinned yield desk Treasuries Earlier bond watchlist Credit stress Scenario maths Strategy Sources Pinned yield desk The same history. No second dataset. One shared Hub feed powers this panel. The compact chart adapts the presentation for this article; the original workspace retains its full controls. Load shared yield history Open original chart ↗ Not loaded. No historical series is embedded in this article. The shared file is fetched only when requested. Yield history Curve comparison Period Last 5 years Last 10 years All available history Earlier month Later month Monthly Treasury history 2Y · 5Y · 10Y · 20Y · 30Y Data stays in the Hub. No screenshots or copied history files. How to read: history compares maturities over time; curves compare maturities at two dates. The vertical axis shows annualised yield in percent, not bond-price returns. Exact observations and source dates Canonical feed: Hub monthly Fed history ↗ . Loaded values retain source dates. First-of-month labels identify monthly periods, not that day’s quote. Dated article, shared data: this panel excludes months after October 2026. Provider revisions to older observations can still occur. It does not turn the article into a live quote service. The separate SGS workbook is not merged here. 01 / What the earlier Treasury reports were really testing Lower yields are useful. The reason they fall matters. The reports contained several different bond theses. One concerned duration, another credit quality, and a third the ability to finance a position through volatility. Treating them as one “buy bonds” call would hide the main risks. Exhibit 1 • Rechecked official observations The short end fell more than the long end. U.S. Treasury constant-maturity par yields, % per year Tenor 3 Nov 2026 5 Nov 2026 Change 2 years 4.61% 4.46% −15bp 5 years 4.74% 4.59% −15bp 10 years 4.95% 4.84% −11bp 20 years 5.35% 5.27% −8bp 30 years 5.32% 5.25% −7bp How to read: the 10-year yield fell by 0.11 percentage points, or 11 basis points. A smaller yield decline in a longer bond can still produce a larger price move because its duration is higher. Evidence boundary: these are daily par yields, not the monthly history in the pinned panel and not executable prices for a particular Treasury. The comparison alone does not prove election-driven money flows. Source: [1] . Changes are original calculations. Read all 14 Treasury tenors · 3, 4 and 5 November The full official curve preserves the short and long end. Each column is a separate daily observation, not a live security quote. Official daily Treasury par yields · % per annum Tenor 3 Nov 2026 4 Nov 2026 5 Nov 2026 1M 4.03% 4.01% 4.03% 1.5M 4.09% 4.08% 4.07% 2M 4.15% 4.15% 4.15% 3M 4.21% 4.21% 4.17% 4M 4.18% 4.20% 4.16% 6M 4.26% 4.25% 4.19% 1Y 4.40% 4.39% 4.28% 2Y 4.61% 4.58% 4.46% 3Y 4.68% 4.64% 4.53% 5Y 4.74% 4.69% 4.59% 7Y 4.83% 4.77% 4.70% 10Y 4.95% 4.90% 4.84% 20Y 5.35% 5.30% 5.27% 30Y 5.32% 5.28% 5.25% How to read: compare across a row to see how one maturity changed; read down a column to see the curve on one day. These are indicative bid-side par-curve observations at or near 15:30 New York. A particular bond’s yield and executable bid or offer may differ. Source: U.S. Treasury official daily par curve . Rechecked 6 November 2026. The existing buy-bonds article and its later instrument-specific quotes are retained: Treasuries, CHF and gold . Three risk channels, three different questions. Interest-rate risk What happens to the bond’s price if its required yield changes? Borrower risk Will the issuer pay, and is the additional spread enough? Financing risk Can the investor meet interest and collateral requirements without selling? Government bonds are not an automatic hedge against every equity decline. The Fed’s 16 October research argues that inflation dynamics and the type of economic shock influence safe-haven behaviour. An inflation shock can hurt bond and equity valuations together. [2] The counterargument to buying the longest maturity is straightforward: yields can remain high, or rise further, if inflation or term-premium concerns persist. A higher yield is compensation to examine, not proof of a bargain. Coupon Treasuries and STRIPS Choose the cash-flow profile before choosing the maturity. Instrument Cash-flow pattern Useful decision question Coupon Treasury Periodic coupons and principal at maturity Does the income and duration fit the holding period? Principal STRIP A single payment at maturity Can the investor tolerate high sensitivity and no interim coupon? How to read: at the same yield and final maturity, concentrating cash flow at the end generally increases duration relative to a coupon-paying bond. A long STRIP is not an income substitute. Product mechanics: TreasuryDirect [12] . Analysis is general; no new security-level prices, yields, ISINs or collateral rates are asserted for the earlier 2041–2054 examples. 02 / The bonds discussed in the previous editions Keep the issuers. Recheck the price. The earlier reports’ useful comparison was borrower quality, not the AI label. Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, P&G and Main Street appeared in the archived issuance discussions. Below is the analytical role of each, rather than a recycled quotation presented as current. Microsoft Corporate-bond comparison Use it as a benchmark for the premium another issuer pays. Compare similar maturities, contractual ranking and yield conventions before treating a higher yield elsewhere as extra value. What to check next: current bid/offer, exact maturity, issue versus secondary spread, and the effect of capital expenditure on future free cash flow. Meta Investment versus cash generation Focus on whether future cash flow supports the funding programme. A financing announcement, a priced issue and a completed settlement are different stages. An orderbook is demand, not the final amount borrowed. What could change the view: better cash generation, lower capital intensity, wider compensation for risk, or deterioration in creditor protection. Oracle Refinancing and spread discipline A large spread deserves a larger due-diligence effort. The 2 November SEC filing exists, but its full pricing text could not be re-opened in this review. Earlier quoted terms are retained only in the labelled archive below, not promoted to current verified prices. [6] What to check next: cash interest coverage, debt maturities, liquidity, contractual obligations and whether the new funds refinance old debt or increase leverage. P&G Non-AI comparison Keep a non-AI issuer in the comparison set. The question is whether the difference in yield adequately pays for different business, leverage, maturity and liquidity risks. An unrelated business model is not, on its own, a guarantee of lower risk. What to check next: same-date yields at comparable duration, not just coupons printed in different offering documents. Main Street Capital Lender and funding risk A lender’s bond requires analysis on both sides of its balance sheet. Examine the loans it owns and the borrowing it uses to finance them. A bond replacing a revolver changes the funding profile; it does not necessarily add the same amount to net debt. What to check next: nonaccruals, cash versus capitalised interest, portfolio marks, funding maturities and secured versus unsecured claims. Source discipline • archived illustration A yield decomposition explains more than a coupon. The earlier Oracle 2029 example separated three different numbers. It quoted a 7.000% coupon, an issue price of 99.835 and a 7.062% issuance yield. The issue spread was reported as 240bp over a 4.662% Treasury benchmark. 4.662% benchmark + 2.400% spread = 7.062% issue yield Coupon = 7.000% of face value; it is not the issuance yield. Archive, not a refreshed market quote. These terms are reproduced from the prior report for explanation. The SEC filing identity was confirmed, but full-text pricing revalidation was blocked. Do not use them to place an order. [6] [7] Other archived spread comparisons, not newly verified Figures quoted in earlier editions; not a current executable comparison Issuer / maturity Reported pricing date Archived spread Microsoft 2036 29 Oct 2026 +65bp Meta 2036 3 Nov 2026 +160bp Oracle 2037 2 Nov 2026 +310bp Differences in trade dates, maturities, structure and verification status prevent treating this as a current matched-risk ranking. No chart of these archived figures is presented as fresh market evidence. Corporate debt is not project debt A famous tenant is not the same as a debt guarantee. Customer or tenant Pays for computing capacity, equipment or space under a contract. Project or equipment borrower Owns or finances the assets and owes lenders under separate debt documents. Secured and unsecured creditors Have different claims on cash flow and collateral if the borrower cannot pay. Read the legal claim, not just the company name beside the project. Construction delays, power access, utilisation, equipment resale values and customer concentration can matter independently. The relevant protections must be verified in each transaction’s documents. Original conceptual diagram. It does not assert the legal terms of any named AI financing transaction. 03 / What repayment evidence can and cannot tell us Prices can move before payments fail. Exhibit 2 • What a credit spread measures A credit spread is compensation for risk, not a default count. Lower-risk benchmark A Treasury yield is the reference rate for the comparison. Extra compensation The spread reflects credit, liquidity and other risks beyond that benchmark. Borrower outcomes A price change alone does not prove an improvement or deterioration in actual debt payments. Read spreads alongside borrower cash flows and repayment evidence. A narrow spread is not proof that every borrower is safe, just as a wider spread is not a default count. Original conceptual diagram. Licensed ICE index observations and their derived changes are not reproduced. The provider’s original series and usage conditions remain linked for further reading. [3] Exhibit 3 • Lagged household data Separate the date of the report from the date of the borrower data. Annualised flows into 90+ day delinquency, % of relevant prior balances Loan type Q2 2025 Q2 2026 Change Mortgages 1.29% 1.52% +0.23pp Auto loans 2.93% 3.00% +0.07pp Credit cards 6.93% 6.97% +0.04pp How to read: these are new transitions into serious arrears, not the stock of all overdue balances. The source was published on 11 August and describes Q2, not November. New York Fed Consumer Credit Panel. Different products have different risk profiles; the percentages are not a like-for-like investment ranking. Exact 30- and 60-day current values are not inferred from the 90+ day table. [4] Payment stress needs a precise vocabulary. Signal Meaning and limitation 30 / 60 / 90+ days late Different depths of arrears. Report the population, definition and denominator. Nonaccrual Interest is no longer accrued normally. Not the same as a realised investor loss. PIK interest Interest is capitalised or paid in securities rather than current cash. It need not be a contractual default. Distressed exchange A restructuring that may count as default under the relevant agency’s methodology. Payment default A contractual failure, subject to the debt terms and applicable grace period. Charge-off A lender records a loss. Fed charge-off rates are annualised and net of recoveries. Fed bank-series definitions include 30+ days past due and accruing plus nonaccrual; they differ from borrower-panel transition measures. [5] Other rows are general analytical definitions, not findings of a new default. Practical watchpoint: investigate cash interest, refinancing needs and the ability to cure arrears together. Do not turn one PIK figure or one rating downgrade into a claim that the whole credit market is defaulting. 04 / Keep the detailed maths A price loss and a margin shortfall are not the same thing. This is a labelled illustration, not a client portfolio. It retains the earlier reports’ hypothetical values so the mechanics can be checked. No current bond duration, bank lending rule, CHF balance or mortgage input is invented. Exhibit 4 • Treasury duration / convexity What a parallel yield shock does to an assumed long bond. Assumptions: assets US$1,000,000 ; modified duration 16 ; convexity 300 . ΔP / P ≈ −16 × Δy + ½ × 300 × Δy² Δy is in decimal units: +100bp = +0.01. Treasury yield shock +100bp Price approximation −14.500% Bond value US$855,000 Equity after loan US$155,000 Reference cases, holding all other inputs unchanged Yield shock Price change Bond value −100bp +17.500% US$1,175,000 −50bp +8.375% US$1,083,750 0bp 0.000% US$1,000,000 +50bp −7.625% US$923,750 +100bp −14.500% US$855,000 Original second-order calculations using explicit assumptions, not measured characteristics of any named Treasury. Excludes coupon accrual, financing interest, FX, default and liquidity effects. Chart labels and selected output use display rounding; exact selected arithmetic is retained below. Selected scenario: arithmetic and exact values Financing amplifies losses and can trigger a collateral call. Loan L = US$700,000; initial equity = US$300,000. Illustrative maximum loan / collateral ratio h = 75%. Equity = V − L. Borrowing headroom = h × V − L. Yield shock Investor equity Borrowing headroom 0bp US$300,000 +US$50,000 +50bp US$223,750 −US$7,187.50 +100bp US$155,000 −US$58,750 At +100bp, the investment loses US$145,000. That is US$145,000 ÷ US$300,000 = 48⅓% of initial equity. The separate US$58,750 headroom deficit must not be added to that loss. Two different remedies: repay US$58,750 of the loan using external cash, or add collateral worth exactly US$235,000 ÷ 3 = US$78,333⅓ if that added collateral receives the same 75% advance rate. Different collateral recognition produces a different requirement. Funding cost is another calculation. A 1 percentage-point annual rate increase on a US$700,000 unchanged loan adds US$7,000 of annual interest. It is not another bond-price loss. Original illustrative maths. The 75% limit is not an OCBC or other bank’s actual rule. Actual margin calculation, cure period, haircuts and cash treatment must be confirmed with the lender. Repayment here assumes external cash, not a sale that also reduces collateral. Corporate debt can face two yield shocks at once. Separate synthetic IG bond: duration 7; convexity 60. +50bp Treasury move +100bp spread move = +150bp all-in yield. −7 × 0.015 + ½ × 60 × 0.015² = −9.825% . This is a sensitivity example, not a forecast. Real rate duration and spread duration can differ. A smooth duration formula cannot describe a sudden default or forced-sale gap. For CHF-funded portfolios: value the liability and collateral in a consistent currency. Do not subtract CHF debt again from NAV that is already net of that debt. No personal ROI or mortgage simulation is calculated here. 05 / Strategy, risks and actions Make the next decision bond by bond. Decision Evidence required Risk control Extend Treasury duration Specific security YTM, price, duration and convexity Stage exposure; test adverse yield moves Add corporate spread Same-date, comparable-maturity spreads; creditor ranking Test weaker cash flow and refinancing Buy AI-linked project debt Actual borrower, guarantee, collateral and payment waterfall Do not substitute a tenant’s reputation for a legal claim Use financing Loan currency, interest, advance rate and cure terms Hold cash and stress collateral independently of P&L The constructive case is income plus possible duration gains if yields decline. The opposing case is persistent inflation, higher risk premiums or weaker borrower cash flow. Neither case removes the need to survive interim volatility. What would change the conclusion: a material change in issue-level spreads, debt-service coverage, inflation expectations, collateral recognition or available liquidity. No numerical price target, forecast path or probability is invented. Client explanation: “A bond can have a reliable borrower and still move sharply in price. The decision depends on the yield, the time until repayment, and whether we can hold it through a difficult market without being forced to sell.” 06 / Reading and source boundaries A focused review, not another unverified daily roundup. The new checks in this edition are deliberately narrow. Daily Treasury observations, the Fed’s safe-haven research, New York Fed repayment data and bank-delinquency definitions were checked against original sources. The Oracle filing identity was confirmed, but full pricing-document retrieval failed. Older report claims are not silently refreshed. The archived issuer examples remain labelled. No new Reuters scan, global central-bank sweep, JPM slide review or live security quotation is claimed in this focused rewrite. The shared chart remains one source, not a second historical database. It loads only the existing Hub feed, filters to completed months no later than October 2026, and displays source metadata. It does not load the full dashboard, overwrite history or create a separate feed. The visual standard was inspected. Relevant V1.2 Merged Excel mappings and the companion PDF’s card, chart-note and responsive-layout guidance were applied. Neutral labels are used where a company’s mapping was not confirmed. Colours are reinforced by labels and line patterns. Local desktop/mobile rendering, arithmetic and shared-feed controls were tested. Shared-feed functional tests used synthetic fixtures that are not included in this file; live feed retrieval failed from the test environment. Data-feed availability still needs checking in the final hosting context. If network or browser policy blocks access, the panel shows a visible message and the original Hub link instead of invented observations. This is a dated public edition; it does not change any schedule. Source appendix Original destinations and access notes. Source status is part of the evidence.
