The Q3 figure is US$42.290bn less US$51.355bn, or −US$9.065bn. Across all four quarters the company still generated positive free cash flow . A quarterly shortfall can be funded through existing cash or financing, and part of the investment may generate income later. The filing puts a number on the timing gap while leaving the return on AI open. The figures include spending and operating cash from the entire business. A project-level judgment would require incremental receipts, the operating costs to serve those users, and the replacement cost of the equipment. Alphabet reports free cash flow as a non-GAAP measure. Sources E1 · Alphabet · Q3 2026 earnings release , SEC Exhibit 99.1, free cash flow reconciliation M3 · 26 Feb 2026 · AI Hurtles Ahead M4 · 9 Dec 2025 · Is It a Bubble? EVIDENCE 05 / META HYPERION 12 / 18 Three clocks inside one data centre Meta ’s Hyperion joint venture shows why a lease, a renewal option and a guarantee deserve separate lines in a credit review. Meta Data centres Private credit Exhibit 04 The durations Meta disclosed for Hyperion The durations Meta disclosed for Hyperion Initial committed lease: 4 years. Conditional residual-value protection: 16 years. Occupancy if all renewal options are exercised: 20 years. Durations have different starting conventions; the 20-year bar is not committed rent. 0 4 8 12 16 20 Initial lease Committed 4 Residual-value protection Conditional 16 Potential occupancy Includes renewal options 20 Duration (years) Only the initial four-year period is a committed lease term in this disclosure. Lease durations run from commencement, identified in the 2025 filing as 2029. The 16-year protection runs from the start of operations. The bars compare durations, rather than calendar endpoints. A small equity share can sit beside a substantial contractual obligation. Meta disclosed a 20% membership interest, with 80% held by an affiliate of Blue Owl-managed funds. It also disclosed an initial lease commitment of approximately US$12.3 billion. The four-year lease includes renewal options that could extend occupancy to 20 years in total. The residual-value protection has a trigger, a cap and a declining threshold. For the first 16 years of operations, specified conditions following non-renewal or termination can trigger a payment if the property’s value falls below the agreed threshold. The obligation differs from a promise to make every payment on the project’s debt. The amount depends on the asset value and contractual threshold at the relevant time. The underwriting question What cash is enforceable between the end of committed rent and the final repayment date? Read the borrower’s actual maturity schedule alongside the lease, guarantee and recourse terms. The two ownership percentages tell the reader who owns the venture. They do not establish how much a creditor would recover. Sources E2 · Meta Platforms · Q3 2025 Form 10-Q, Note 13, subsequent event E3 · Meta Platforms · 21 Oct 2025 Hyperion joint venture announcement M4 · 9 Dec 2025 · Is It a Bubble? CROSS-MEMO ANALYSIS / ONE TECHNOLOGY, THREE CLAIMS 13 / 18 The same AI success can help one borrower and hurt another A portfolio can contain opposite business exposures that depend on the same source of finance. AI Software Private credit Equities Follow a customer choosing between old software and a new AI tool. If the new tool genuinely lowers the customer’s cost, the customer benefits first. The incumbent may face weaker pricing or lower renewals. The new supplier may gain users while competition forces it to pass the savings on. A successful technology can produce all three outcomes at once. Position What has to work First evidence to request Position Software lender What has to work The borrower retains customers and cash after replacement spending. First evidence to request Paid renewals, churn by cohort, cash interest coverage. Position Compute owner What has to work Utilisation and realised prices cover power, replacement and capital costs. First evidence to request New orders converting to paid usage, contracted rates and contract length. Position Supplier shareholder What has to work Profits grow enough to justify the entry valuation. First evidence to request Incremental margins, share count and the expectations implied by price. Position Infrastructure creditor What has to work Binding project receipts last long enough to service the debt. First evidence to request Lease maturities, tenant credit, reserves and enforceable recourse. The connection becomes important when financing is scarce. An incumbent needing time to redesign its product and a new operator needing money to finish construction might both approach lenders when appetite is weak. Exposure to different companies can still leave the portfolio dependent on the same refinancing window. Evidence that would change the view Track paid customer retention and contract cash, then look at the terms on which fresh capital is actually available. A fully funded borrower with sticky customers presents a different risk from one whose plan depends on raising money every year. Technology labels alone cannot distinguish them. Sources M2 · 9 Apr 2026 · What’s Going on in Private Credit ? M3 · 26 Feb 2026 · AI Hurtles Ahead M4 · 9 Dec 2025 · Is It a Bubble? E1 · Alphabet · Q3 2026 earnings release , SEC Exhibit 99.1, free cash flow reconciliation E2 · Meta Platforms · Q3 2025 Form 10-Q, Note 13, subsequent event PORTFOLIO APPLICATION / SINGAPORE 14 / 18 The bond matures in USD. The bills arrive in SGD. For a Singapore investor using CHF financing , a single headline yield leaves three cash-flow questions unanswered. Singapore US Treasuries USD/SGD CHF financing Start with the dated payments of the asset. A conventional fixed-rate US Treasury has a contractual USD coupon and principal schedule. A Treasury STRIP pays at maturity and provides no periodic coupon to meet financing costs. A low-coupon bond bought below par can offer a yield to maturity above its coupon rate because part of the prospective return comes from the move toward redemption value. Exposure What to put on the sheet What can interrupt the plan Exposure USD bond What to put on the sheet Dirty purchase price, coupons, maturity proceeds, prospective sale price at the chosen horizon. What can interrupt the plan A higher market yield lowers the sale value of a fixed-rate bond before maturity. Exposure CHF loan What to put on the sheet Drawn amount, reset dates, contracted interest, principal due and collateral terms. What can interrupt the plan Refinancing rates rise, CHF appreciates or eligible collateral value falls. Exposure SGD spending What to put on the sheet Dates and amounts needed in SGD, with FX conversion shown at each relevant date. What can interrupt the plan A weaker USD/SGD can reduce spendable proceeds even when every USD coupon is paid. Positive carry and a positive total return answer different questions. Interest received can exceed financing cost while the bond’s market value falls. A stronger CHF can simultaneously raise the SGD value of the liability. If the lender requires more collateral before the bond matures, the investor’s ability to wait becomes a source of risk in its own right. Practical next step Place the nearest loan reset, spending need and bond cash receipt on the same calendar. Then identify which cash or committed liquidity covers the earliest shortfall. This is a review framework. A numerical return would require actual prices, FX rates, funding terms and cash-flow dates. Sources M1 · 22 Sep 2026 · Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics – Part III M2 · 9 Apr 2026 · What’s Going on in Private Credit ? T3 · US Treasury Department · September 2026 daily par yield curve T4 · US Treasury Department · November 2026 daily par yield curve DECISION REVIEW / STRATEGY AND RISK 15 / 18 What would make you change your mind? Write down the evidence that would weaken a position before the market gives you a reason to defend it. US Treasuries Private credit AI FX Working thesis Evidence to review Decision affected Working thesis Long bonds can earn an adequate return at the entry yield. Evidence to review Compare changes across maturities with the date cash is needed. Review new auction demand and the cost of maintaining funding. Decision affected Duration, liquidity reserve and ability to hold through a price decline. Working thesis A private loan is adequately protected. Evidence to review Reconcile reported earnings to cash interest paid. Check collateral ownership, other liens, amendment history and redemption rules. Decision affected Accept the terms, require better protection, or pass. Working thesis AI investment will earn an attractive return. Evidence to review Look for paid utilisation at durable prices, incremental margins and replacement spending as assets age. Decision affected The price justified for equity and the maturity justified for debt. Working thesis Funding in CHF improves portfolio cash flow. Evidence to review Reprice the next loan period and measure the liability in the currency in which the investor spends. Decision affected Currency hedge, borrowing size and cash to meet a collateral call. The best test is one that can genuinely disappoint you. High usage, a smooth net asset value or a large government buyer can each be true without settling the investment question. State which missing observation would connect that fact to the cash you expect. A useful file note records the source, the date and what your conclusion would be if the next reading went the other way. The five-memo conclusion Marks changes his confidence when the evidence changes, and keeps asking what the price already assumes. For a portfolio review, write one sentence per holding naming who pays, when payment is due, and what has to remain true until the investor receives it. Where the sentence depends on a friendly refinancing market, that is the risk to examine first. entries.text: Howard Marks · Conviction needs a price · 6 Nov 2026 Howard Marks · revised 6 November 2026 5 November · earlier edition All report editions Research Papers Skip to report RESEARCH NOTE Howard Marks · November 2026 edition FIVE MEMOS / ONE INVESTMENT DISCIPLINE Conviction needs a price. An attractive investment needs a credible route from today’s price to tomorrow’s cash. Howard Marks’s latest five written memos connect long-term interest rates, private credit and AI through that question. This report pairs his arguments with dated primary evidence and a practical review framework. Research cutoff · 6 November 2026, 16:44 Singapore · Standalone draft US Treasuries Private credit AI USD/SGD Interpretation 5.25% 30-year Treasury par yield 5 Nov 2026 · annualised 5% Intended quarterly fund repurchase cap Most perpetual BDCs · manager discretion −US$9.065bn Alphabet Q3 2026 free cash flow Company-wide · quarter to 30 Sep Five takeaways Long maturities stayed more expensive to fund. From 22 September to 5 November, the two-year Treasury yield fell 25 basis points and the 30-year fell 4. Access to cash deserves its own review. Borrower repayment, loan protection and fund withdrawal terms answer different questions. AI ’s usefulness leaves the purchase-price question open. A business can grow while investment spending absorbs its operating cash. The strength of a contract depends on its terms and dates. A committed lease, a conditional guarantee and an optional renewal create different claims. The funding plan affects how long an investor can wait. Align asset cash flows, borrowing obligations and the currency of future spending. The five memos Rates Credit AI economics Funding & FX Outlook Sources 01 / memos Five letters ask increasingly connected questions The archive’s latest five written memos span 6 November 2025 to 22 September 2026. The latest listed title remains the September letter at the research cutoff. The summaries below preserve the date and status of Marks’s views. 22 September 2026 · Long-term rates Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics – Part III Policy can improve market functioning while underlying borrowing pressures persist. Marks argues that persistent inflation, fiscal borrowing and competing capital demands help explain higher long-term yields. He questions whether bond buybacks can durably offset these pressures. The memo acknowledges Treasury’s stated liquidity-support purpose, so yield suppression is Marks’s interpretation of the policy. He distinguishes nominal dollar repayment from preservation of purchasing power. His fiscal concern has an uncertain timetable. He recognises the dollar’s reserve role and the strengths of US businesses, and he sees risks in a large move away from US assets. Investors with non-dollar spending needs may have a reason to diversify currency exposure. DECISION QUESTION What return compensates for inflation, future borrowing and the time you commit your money? Reading qualification. Treat numerical macro claims as observations cited in a September memo until checked against their primary releases. Source opinion · 22 September 2026 Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics – Part III 9 April 2026 · Private-credit ownership What’s Going on in Private Credit ? Credit quality, valuation and access to cash require separate checks. Marks argues that competition weakened direct-lending terms. Infrequent valuations can conceal changing credit risk. He connects software disruption, withdrawals and refinancing, while distinguishing sentiment from borrower performance. Redemption restrictions had helped avoid forced sales. He also sees opportunities as lenders become more selective and loan terms improve. DECISION QUESTION Can the borrower pay, can the lender enforce, and when can the investor receive cash? Reading qualification. Oaktree’s comments about its own underwriting and relative positioning are the manager’s assessment. Source opinion · 9 April 2026 What’s Going on in Private Credit ? 26 February 2026 · Technology conviction AI Hurtles Ahead Greater confidence in AI ’s usefulness still leaves its investment value uncertain. Marks becomes more confident in AI ’s usefulness and demand for inference, the work a trained model performs. He still questions future capacity, revenue quality and investment pricing. He sees a continuing role for judgment in unfamiliar situations and retains his preference for moderate, selective participation. DECISION QUESTION How does demonstrated usefulness become a durable, paid-for service? Reading qualification. Much of the memo draws on a Claude-generated tutorial. Treat capability and adoption claims as attributed discussion unless independently verified. Source opinion · 26 February 2026 AI Hurtles Ahead 9 December 2025 · AI investment pricing Is It a Bubble? A transformative industry can produce poor returns at the wrong price or financing terms. Marks questions which AI businesses will earn durable returns after competition, investment and financing costs. He highlights capacity, obsolescence and debt risk, while recognising real demand and profitable established participants. He declines to make a definitive bubble call and favours selective exposure at prices supported by cash flows. DECISION QUESTION How much future success is already required by the entry price and funding terms? Reading qualification. Historical bubble comparisons express a risk framework. They supply no crash date, probability or price target. Source opinion · 9 December 2025 Is It a Bubble? 6 November 2025 · Underwriting quality Cockroaches in the Coal Mine Benign conditions can hide weak underwriting until scrutiny rises. Marks uses First Brands and Tricolor to discuss how plentiful money, relaxed due diligence and incentives to deploy capital can leave weaknesses undiscovered. He treats defaults as part of sub-investment-grade lending and declines to infer a system-wide breakdown from these episodes. The First Brands discussion concerns allegations, opaque financing and receivables control. He describes credit research as an accumulated assessment of evidence and uncertainty. He also acknowledges that Oaktree has suffered defaults and frauds, which matters when reading its successful case study. DECISION QUESTION Which independent evidence establishes asset ownership and the route of collections? Reading qualification. Preserve the allegations wording used at the November 2025 memo date. Later legal developments need their own dated primary source. Source opinion · 6 November 2025 Cockroaches in the Coal Mine Archive sequence checked 6 Nov 2026, 16:44 SGT Oaktree memo archive 02 / rates Long-term borrowing costs proved more persistent Shorter yields declined more than longer yields between 22 September and 5 November. The latest verified Treasury observation is 5 November. Comparing the same maturities shows how the curve changed. Identifying the cause requires separate evidence. Compare matching maturities on the two dates. Units are annualised percent. The horizontal axis is years, and the vertical scale starts at 3.5%. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point. Bars start at zero and show the magnitude of the decline. The 10-year minus two-year gap widened from 25 to 38 basis points. A short-rate forecast is only one input to a long-bond decision. A long bond also exposes its holder to many years of changing required returns. A sale before maturity turns that price sensitivity into a realised result. Calculated change · (5 Nov yield − 22 Sep yield) × 100 · basis points Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, 2026 EXHIBIT 03 · POLICY & COUNTEREVIDENCE Better liquidity is a real potential benefit 01 Treasury operation Buy back older long-dated securities 02 Trading effect Give dealers an outlet for inventory 03 Investment test Assess the return required to hold long-dated bonds The stated policy objective was liquidity support. Treasury’s 19 August announcement increased the maximum per-operation size in the 10–20-year and 20–30-year nominal sectors from US$2 billion to at least US$4 billion, effective 9 September through 4 November. Dealer feedback supplies an important counterargument. Minutes of the 3 November meeting reported at least modest liquidity and market-functioning improvements for most dealers. Effects on handling client flows were mixed. The minutes were published on 4 November. Policy announcement · 19 Aug 2026 · dealer assessment at 3 Nov meeting, published 4 Nov Treasury Announces Increased Sizes of Nominal Long-End Liquidity Support Buybacks Beginning September 9 Minutes of the Meeting of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee November 3, 2026 EXHIBIT 04 · ANALYSIS The policy needs more than one scorecard Three questions for the same policy Question Evidence to seek Is the market easier to trade? Bid–ask spreads, depth, dealer inventory and execution quality. Is the long-term return adequate? Entry yield, inflation compensation and the value of waiting. Has the debt burden changed? Net borrowing, refinancing dates and the interest bill. Improved trading and persistent long-term yields can coexist. The curve alone cannot establish a buyback effect. Treasury also explains that new issuance replaces repurchased securities. A change in which securities investors hold can therefore occur without a corresponding reduction in net borrowing. The portfolio implication depends on the holding period. An investor meeting dated cash needs can compare maturities with those dates. An investor seeking a capital gain needs a view on the yield at the future sale date, alongside a plan for an adverse move. Interpretation informed by Treasury releases · 2 and 4 Nov 2026 Treasury Announces Marketable Borrowing Estimates Report to the Secretary of the Treasury from the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee 03 / credit Income quality and exit terms need separate tests Private credit combines a borrower, a contract and an investment vehicle. Looking through all three makes it easier to distinguish business deterioration from investor withdrawals. It also identifies the documents that can answer each concern. EXHIBIT 05 · CASH-FLOW DIAGRAM Follow the cash through three layers 01 Borrower Pays interest from its business 02 Loan Sets collateral and enforcement rights 03 Fund Sets distributions and repurchases Regular distributions and an available exit have different funding needs. A fund may collect interest over time while an investor requests the return of principal now. The amount available to meet those requests depends on cash, new subscriptions, asset sales and the fund’s rules. Independent analysis · conceptual cash-flow map. EXHIBIT 06 · REPORTED FUND TERMS The exit window can be smaller than the holding 5% of fund NAV per quarter Intended aggregate repurchase cap The Fed reported this intended cap for most perpetual-life BDCs. Business development companies (BDCs) are business-lending investment vehicles. NAV means net asset value, broadly assets less liabilities. The cap concerns aggregate fund repurchases. Managers retain discretion over how much they accept. The Fed ’s stability assessment was specific to further redemption requests. It judged those risks manageable at publication. The May 2026 report used a general information cutoff of 23 April. That is a dated system assessment alongside the restrictions an individual investor faces. Central-bank analysis · May 2026 edition · Q1 flow period · general information cutoff 23 Apr · HTML updated 28 May Financial Stability Report, May 2026, Funding Risks, Box 4.1 EXHIBIT 07 · ANALYSIS Ask for the evidence behind the reported number A practical evidence checklist Layer Evidence worth checking What would weaken confidence Borrower Cash collected, interest paid, customer retention and refinancing schedule. Income rises while collections weaken or interest is repeatedly capitalised. Loan Signed security, collateral ownership, seniority and covenant terms. Another creditor has an earlier claim or the recovery estimate relies on unclear title. Fund Repurchase policy, accepted requests, cash buffer and concentration. Withdrawals rise while available cash falls and assets take longer to sell. Independent confirmation helps test the lending story. For receivables-backed lending, reconcile the customer’s obligation, the borrower’s records and the lender’s claim. Trace where collections actually land. A document with a familiar name becomes more informative when the counterparty confirms it independently. Each weakness suggests a different response. A timing mismatch calls for a liquidity plan. An uncertain collateral claim calls for legal and operational clarification. Deteriorating cash coverage calls for a new repayment assessment. Treating them separately makes a review more precise. Independent review framework · historical allegations discussed in the 6 Nov 2025 memo retain their original status Cockroaches in the Coal Mine 04 / ai AI adoption leaves a cash-return test to pass The investment question becomes clearer when growth, cash generation and valuation are examined separately. The following corporate example tests the timing of cash. It supplies a measurable exhibit alongside the more qualitative debate about technological change. EXHIBIT 08 · ANALYSIS A useful technology must pass three investment tests 01 Useful technology Does it solve a problem people care about? 02 Durable business Can the provider collect cash after competition and costs? 03 Attractive investment Does the price leave room for a satisfactory return? These tests can produce different answers for the same company. A service can become widely used while competing suppliers reduce its price. A business can earn money while its shareholders receive a disappointing return because the purchase price already assumed stronger growth. Independent analysis · qualitative investment framework. EXHIBIT 09 · REPORTED DATA Alphabet ’s spending overtook quarterly cash generation Upper bar · Operating cash flow Lower bar · Property & equipment purchases Q4 2025 52.4 27.9 Q1 2026 45.8 35.7 Q2 2026 39.1 44.9 Q3 2026 42.3 51.4 Zero-based bars · common maximum US$60bn · labels rounded to 1 decimal Capital spending exceeded operating cash in Q2 and Q3. Read each quarter’s paired bars on the same scale. Property and equipment purchases include the company’s wider operations. The figures cover all of Alphabet . Exact cash-flow reconciliation US$ million · source values before rounding Period Operating cash Property & equipment Free cash flow Q4 2025 52,402 27,851 +24,551 Q1 2026 45,790 35,674 +10,116 Q2 2026 39,069 44,924 -5,855 Q3 2026 42,290 51,355 -9,065 Issuer data · quarters through 30 Sep 2026 · released 28 Oct 2026 · US$bn in bars, US$m in exact table Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results, Exhibit 99.1 EXHIBIT 10 · CASH-FLOW RECONCILIATION The quarter and the trailing year tell different stories −US$9.065bn Q3 2026 free cash flow 42.290 − 51.355 = −9.065 Operating cash − property & equipment purchases · US$bn The trailing four-quarter total remained positive at US$19.747 billion. The four quarters total US$179.551 billion of operating cash and US$159.804 billion of property and equipment purchases. Alphabet labels free cash flow a non-GAAP measure, meaning it supplements the standard financial statements. A quarterly deficit creates a timing question for future cash returns. It can accompany investment that ultimately earns attractive returns. The next tests are utilisation, payments from customers, useful asset lives and the continuing spending required to maintain the business. This exhibit does not isolate the return on AI projects. Calculated from the issuer reconciliation · four quarters ended 30 Sep 2026 Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results, Exhibit 99.1 EXHIBIT 11 · CONTRACT COMPARISON Four, sixteen and twenty years mean different things 4 years Initial lease term 16 years Conditional residual-value support 20 years Possible total lease period with renewals Meta disclosed three different time horizons in the Hyperion transaction. The initial lease was expected to begin in 2029. Conditional, capped residual-value support runs for 16 years from operations starting. Extension options could take the total lease period to 20 years. The legal conditions determine the economic value of each period. The chart compares disclosed lengths, with different line patterns for commitments, conditional support and options. A longer possible period carries different certainty from the initial lease. Historical case · transaction 21 Oct 2025 · Form 10-Q filed 30 Oct 2025, accepted 29 Oct · years from each relevant commencement Meta Platforms Q3 2025 Form 10-Q, Note 13, Subsequent Event Meta Announces Joint Venture With Funds Managed by Blue Owl Capital to Develop Hyperion Data Center EXHIBIT 12 · ANALYSIS Ownership and lending carry different cash claims The same industry creates different financial claims Claim What the investor receives What matters most Equity ownership Cash left after operating needs, investment and prior claims. The price paid, competitive position and future cash available to owners. Lending Contractual interest and principal subject to repayment. Coverage, legal priority, maturity and recoverable collateral. Leased infrastructure Rent and any residual asset value under the agreement. Lease commitment, counterparty strength, useful life and renewal economics. The practical next step is to read the claim you are buying. Identify what is owed, when it is owed, who pays and which conditions change the amount. Then ask what evidence supports the collateral value or earnings estimate at the date you would need to exit. Independent analysis · qualitative comparison of financial claims. 05 / funding Match the currency and the payment dates For a Singapore -based investor, the currency of future spending gives the analysis a concrete anchor. The same asset can have a different purpose when held for USD spending, SGD spending or repayment of a CHF loan . Keep each cash flow in its own currency until conversion is required. EXHIBIT 13 · CASH-FLOW DIAGRAM A funding plan determines the freedom to wait 01 USD asset Coupons, distributions and sale proceeds 02 CHF borrowing Interest reset and principal repayment 03 SGD spending The currency and dates of household needs The asset, loan and spending plan can react differently to the same market move. A bond may keep paying its stated coupon while its sale price changes. A revolving loan may reset earlier than the asset matures. Converting the proceeds adds another market price to the eventual cash result. A workable holding period includes the dates when cash is required. List scheduled payments, possible collateral calls and the amount available without selling the investment. That schedule shows where the investor has flexibility and where a market move could create a forced decision. Portfolio interpretation · conceptual cash-flow map, with no assumed client position or loan terms Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics – Part III What’s Going on in Private Credit ? EXHIBIT 14A · REPORTED FX DATA USD/SGD changes the cash available 1.2776 SGD per USD 30 Oct 2026 A lower quote gives fewer SGD for one USD. Multiply USD proceeds by USD/SGD to find the SGD amount before conversion costs. Exact daily reference rates USD/SGD · 26–30 Oct 2026 Date SGD per USD 26 Oct 1.2809 27 Oct 1.2804 28 Oct 1.2827 29 Oct 1.2801 30 Oct 1.2776 Reference observations · 26–30 Oct 2026 · release 2 Nov · quote direction shown above · execution costs excluded Federal Reserve H.10 exchange rates EXHIBIT 14B · REPORTED FX DATA USD/CHF changes the cash available 0.8230 CHF per USD 30 Oct 2026 A lower quote gives fewer CHF for one USD. Repaying a fixed CHF amount then requires more USD. Divide the CHF principal by USD/CHF to find that USD requirement before costs. Exact daily reference rates USD/CHF · 26–30 Oct 2026 Date CHF per USD 26 Oct 0.8275 27 Oct 0.8287 28 Oct 0.8301 29 Oct 0.8267 30 Oct 0.8230 Reference observations · 26–30 Oct 2026 · release 2 Nov · quote direction shown above · execution costs excluded Federal Reserve H.10 exchange rates EXHIBIT 15 · ANALYSIS & ACTION Review the next cash date before increasing the position Review the funding schedule alongside the investment thesis Position or need Dates and terms to align Evidence that requires a fresh review Bond holding Coupons, maturity, intended sale and currency. A change in required yield or a cash need before maturity. Private-credit fund Distributions, repurchase window and settlement. Weaker collections, changing NAV methods or reduced accepted withdrawals. AI -related equity Entry valuation, cash reinvestment and investment horizon. Demand, competition or replacement spending changes the cash outlook. CHF loan Reset date, principal due, collateral and recognition terms. Funding cost, exchange rate or collateral requirements change. SGD spending Payment dates and liquid funds already held in SGD. Expected receipts arrive later or in a less favourable currency amount. The useful output is a dated cash schedule and a documented investment thesis. Record which observations would support holding, adding, reducing or asking for further evidence. An explicit review condition makes it easier to update a view when the facts change, without needing to predict the exact market turning point. The margin of safety has both a valuation and a financing dimension. An attractive entry price helps absorb forecast error. Adequate accessible cash helps the investor remain in control of the sale date. A position can satisfy one condition while leaving the other exposed. 06 / outlook Use conditions that can change your mind The central conclusion is a method for making a decision. Start with the cash claim, test the assumptions behind it and compare those assumptions with the price and funding plan. This supports a more selective review across assets. EXHIBIT 16 · QUALITATIVE SCENARIOS Set review conditions before the next headline Qualitative monitoring conditions · analyst framework Area Supportive conditions Adverse conditions What to monitor Long-duration bonds Lower inflation compensation and credible fiscal funding plans. Higher required compensation or an earlier need to sell. Entry yield, inflation measures, auction demand and the holding-period cash plan. Private credit Resilient collections and refinancing on workable terms. Borrower stress combined with limited investor liquidity. Cash coverage, payment-in-kind interest (added to the loan balance), recoveries and accepted repurchases. AI investments Paid usage and durable margins grow into the asset base. Capacity, competition or obsolescence outpaces monetisation. End-user payments, utilisation, replacement spending and free cash flow . Multi-currency funding Receipts arrive when the liability falls due. Currency moves or a loan reset erodes the available cash. Asset and debt currencies , reset dates and collateral headroom . These conditions describe what would strengthen or weaken an investment case. They are a monitoring framework. The five memos provide qualitative judgments that require security-specific valuation and funding data before becoming a trade decision. EXHIBIT 17 · COUNTERARGUMENTS Give the opposing evidence a fair test Counterarguments to keep in the review Cautious observation The strongest counterargument What would settle the issue Long yields remain elevated. Market functioning can improve even when yields stay high. Trading evidence alongside inflation, issuance and required-return data. Repurchases can be restricted. Restrictions can protect a fund from forced sales at poor prices. Borrower performance, liquidity resources and actual investor requests. Capital expenditure absorbs cash. Spending can create assets that produce attractive future returns. Paid demand, asset utilisation and cash returns over an adequate horizon. Contract terms are complex. Well-designed conditions can allocate risks to capable counterparties. The actual contract, enforceability and counterparty capacity. A balanced conclusion changes when the evidence changes. A strong business result, better contractual protection or a lower entry price can improve the expected return. A weaker cash result or an earlier funding obligation can reduce it. The discipline is to update those inputs explicitly. Ask who pays, what price is justified and whether you can wait. Those questions connect the memo series to a portfolio review while leaving room for opportunity when the evidence, price and terms improve. 07 / sources Trace the evidence and its limits The report distinguishes observation dates from publication dates. A verified release can describe an earlier period. Treasury yields run through 5 November, Alphabet cash flows through 30 September and the FX observations through 30 October. Each exhibit states its units and source. COVERAGE Use the dates attached to each exhibit Coverage and remaining data gaps Item Coverage in this draft Howard Marks memos Latest five public written memos checked against the Oaktree archive at the stated cutoff. Market observations Official Treasury par curve and Fed H.10 daily FX reference rates. Corporate evidence Alphabet company-wide cash reconciliation and Meta ’s historical transaction terms. S&P 500 / SPX The inspected Hub module records an unconnected dataset and unresolved reuse permission. The FRED source page is linked for reference. Price targets and calls The source memos provide no complete numerical target framework. Qualitative monitoring conditions are labelled as analysis. Security-specific implementation Actual entry price, transaction costs, cash requirements and loan terms would be needed for a position-level return calculation.
