[S9-S11] 17 / RESEARCH Dividends and settlement prevent a casual comparison SPX price return, total return and an investor's account return are different series. The module should name the series beside every chart. A price index excludes dividends. A total-return index includes their reinvestment according to the index methodology. S&P DJI separately defines net-total-return calculations incorporating withholding adjustments. Do not take an annual dividend yield, append it casually to every clipped result and call the output an exact self-financing collar. Timing, reinvestment and hedge resizing matter. [S4-S5] A stock basket or ETF can distribute cash. Direct ownership may receive dividends, subject to tax and expenses. The price component can be hedged, while the dividends remain a separate cashflow or are reinvested. Retained dividends can also take the total account outcome beyond the price-only ceiling; costs can reduce it below a price-only floor. Reinvestment can change exposure and notional matching. ETF expenses and tracking differences also separate its price from the reference index. SPX options settle in cash and use European exercise. One full-size SPX contract has a USD 100 multiplier per index point. Traditional AM settlement uses component opening prices; SPXW PM settlement uses closing prices. An annual close-to-close scenario is not automatically identical to the settlement value of a particular contract. [S6-S7] Do not assume a basket is physically deliverable against SPX. Gains or losses on cash-settled options become cash obligations; shares are not transferred to satisfy the SPX call. A portfolio hedge must match the economic notional and account for basis, tracking and settlement differences. A beta hedge may reduce systematic risk without creating an exact floor. ETF/equity options introduce a different assignment mechanism. American-style short calls can be assigned before expiry, including around ex-dividend dates. That can alter holdings and cashflows. This early-assignment issue should not be attributed to European SPX options. [S6; S8] Exposure What needs separate accounting SPX price reference No dividend cashflow in the index return Total-return benchmark Dividend reinvestment; gross or net tax convention ETF/stock collar Cash dividends, tracking, expenses and assignment where relevant Cash-settled index collar Notional, settlement basis, cash margin and liquidity Any documented product Actual contractual crediting and payout rules 18 / RESEARCH Net outcomes depend on the investment wrapper A maturity floor addresses a specified payoff, not every risk in the account. The report should show an explicit limitations panel beside the key figures. Premiums, trading costs and financing. Buy-at-ask/sell-at-bid implementation, commissions, fees and slippage reduce returns. Financing the underlying or an option debit creates a separate cashflow. Funding rates can improve one part of an option quote while increasing the cost of a financed investment. Collateral and liquidity. Broker and clearing requirements can change the cash or collateral needed to carry a position. Economic coverage by a stock basket does not guarantee identical regulatory margin treatment. A maturity hedge does not remove the need to meet interim obligations or the risk of selling assets at a poor time. Taxes and distributions. Tax depends on the instrument, ownership structure and investor circumstances. Do not transplant US option-tax treatment into an unspecified Singapore investor account. The research figures are pre-tax; no tax rate or personal suitability assumption is applied. Currency and purchasing power. These results measure nominal USD index exposure. For an SGD-based account, currency conversion is a separate source of gains or losses: (1 + USD return) x (ending USD/SGD / starting USD/SGD) - 1. A 0% USD price floor is not an SGD floor and does not protect purchasing power against inflation. Issuer, early exit and actual product rules. A contractual product may expose holders to an issuer/guarantor or other counterparties and may apply early-exit valuation, surrender terms, deductions, participation limits or reset rights. Which of these apply must come from its documents. No such terms, issuer identity, guarantee or charges are assumed for IFI here. The scope of protection needs a visible label. State: maturity only; specified reference exposure; gross or net basis; subject to the stated implementation and counterparty assumptions. Keep the language close to the headline instead of relying on a remote disclaimer. This is research and presentation analysis. It does not recommend a product, transaction size or personal investment strategy. 19 / RESEARCH A historical options backtest remains unsubstantiated This research verifies the index calculations and hypothetical transformation, not a 1961-2025 investable zero-premium collar. The missing evidence is specific. The price-history window is longer than the instrument history. SPX options were introduced on 1 July 1983, so the pre-1983 years cannot be described as a listed-SPX-options track record. Contract conventions and available expiries also changed over time. [S14] The required archive was not obtained. An executable backtest needs dated SPX/SPXW contract identifiers, expiries, available strikes, bid and ask prices and sizes at the selected roll time, plus settlement values, quote-quality flags, relevant underlying prices, distributions, funding, fees and margin rules. Closing index levels and a volatility index do not supply these missing trades. A realistic rule must handle missing matches. If no listed pair satisfies the proposed zero-premium condition, the backtest must record infeasibility, change a strike under a predeclared rule, or pay/receive a disclosed premium. Do not create an interpolated executable strike or retrospectively select the best expiry. Cboe documents a potential data route. Its Option Quote Intervals product advertises historical coverage from January 2012 and NBBO-related fields. This establishes an available research source, not that a suitable archive was purchased, checked or used here. [S13] Existing benchmarks are useful context, not substitutes. Cboe CLL uses a different collar rule; CLLZ uses a monthly 2.5%-5% put spread funded by a call. A put spread only offsets losses across a limited band, so CLLZ is not a 0% full floor. Its returns cannot validate this annual 0%-9% illustration. [S12] An honest panel can remain informative. Display the historical quote section as Not backtested - contract quote dataset required, and give the required schema. Keep the completed historical-index and hypothetical sections available. 20 / RESEARCH Recommended dashboard: answer one question per section Use a mobile-first report with a persistent evidence label and a short reading path. Let users reveal detail without losing the main distinction. Start with the conclusion and its boundary. Place the three frequency cards above the distribution, with the period, denominator, price-return basis and hypothetical label always visible. The user should not need to open a tooltip to discover that the result is not product performance. Then show the cost of the benefit. Put raw-versus-clipped annual returns beside the wealth comparison on desktop, and stack them on a phone. Display the sacrificed upside and avoided losses with equal visual weight. Offer total return as an explicitly labelled comparator, using a different line pattern. Separate a pricing panel from the scenario result. A user changing a cap in the scenario calculator changes a mathematical assumption. Only a market-data pricing panel should claim the cap was solved from option quotes. Store the selected expiry, quote timestamp, bid/ask convention, strikes and net premium with that result. Use the verified colour standard without relying on colour alone. Apply V1.2 Merged: Equity Cyan for equity-series identity, Policy Plum for hypothetical analysis, Company Magenta for option legs, and explicit Risk Red only for identified risk/loss meaning. Retain direct labels, signs, hatching and line styles for greyscale. Keep the display lightweight. Use inline SVG or Canvas charts, compact JSON/CSV data and text-based tooltips. No chart screenshots are needed for the module. Use at least the guide's 16 px web body baseline, roughly 1.5 line spacing, responsive cards and table-contained horizontal scrolling. Order Section User question 1 Overview and historical frequencies How often did each annual outcome occur? 2 Annual returns and wealth What does the transformation change? 3 Regimes and monthly starts How dependent is the answer on the sample? 4 Payoff and pricing feasibility What is promised mathematically, and what would it cost? 5 Limits, methodology and annual audit What is excluded, and can I reproduce it? 21 / RESEARCH Labels and tooltips should prevent predictable mistakes Keep essential caveats visible; use tooltips for detail. A small label can prevent a much larger misunderstanding. Element Recommended wording Main chart title Historical SPX price returns and hypothetical 0%-9% annual-reset outcomes Always-visible subheading 1961-2025 | 65 complete calendar years | USD price return | no dividends | before costs Transformation badge HYPOTHETICAL PAYOFF - NOT ACTUAL PRODUCT PERFORMANCE Frequency tooltip Computed from unrounded year-end level ratios. R<0; 0<=R<=9%; R>9%. Exact boundaries enter the middle bucket. CAGR tooltip Annualised geometric growth over the selected complete years. Not the arithmetic average of annual returns. Drawdown tooltip Measured at calendar-year endpoints only. Does not measure intra-year or daily option portfolio losses. Total-return toggle S&P 500 published total return: dividends reinvested; separate benchmark, not clipped Pricing status Illustrative model / historical quotes / live indicative quotes: display the actual evidence type Zero-premium tooltip Net option premium only. Costs, funding, capital and foregone upside remain. Incomplete-year badge YTD - excluded from completed-year statistics Historical-quote gap Historical collar backtest unavailable: required option quote archive not obtained Product boundary Contractual terms must be checked against the product documents; this is a generic scenario analysis Audit drawers should expose the two endpoint levels, calculated return, bucket, transformed return and accumulated wealth for every year. Tooltips must work by tap and keyboard focus, not hover alone. The following chart briefs and slide plan describe a proposed implementation. Full-series charts or downloadable audit data require suitable display and redistribution rights. This public edition uses aggregate replacements. 22 / RESEARCH Chart briefs: history and the transformation Every chart should have a takeaway, dates, units, source and reading guide. These briefs can be copied into the module specification. 1. Return distribution. Purpose: show the shape of annual SPX price outcomes. Takeaway: returns above 9% occurred in 38 of 65 years. Units: annual percentage return on the horizontal axis; year count on the vertical. Data: NYU levels, 1961-2025; retrieved 5 November 2026. How to read: each equal-width bar counts years in a return range; vertical lines mark 0% and 9%. [S1] 2. Frequency counts. Purpose: make the three buckets exact. Takeaway: 17 below zero, 10 in the inclusive middle, 38 above 9%. Units: counts and percent of 65. Data/date: same as chart 1. How to read: a bar's length is its number of years; printed labels retain counts and denominators. Boundary classification uses unrounded calculations. 3. Raw versus clipped annual returns. Purpose: locate the years when the hypothetical rule matters. Takeaway: protection and forgone upside both recur. Units: annual percentage returns; calendar years. Data/date: S1, 1961-2025. How to read: bars are historical returns; dots are formula results for the same years. A dashed 9% line exposes the ceiling. 4. Wealth growth. Purpose: show compounded outcomes on identical dates. Takeaway: 100 becomes 11,780 for price returns and 3,872 for the hypothetical path; total-return context differs materially. Units: indexed wealth, start 100; use a clearly marked logarithmic axis for the long period. Data: S1-S2, year-end 1960 to 2025; retrieved 5 November 2026. How to read: equal vertical distances on the log axis are equal percentage changes. 5. Drawdown. Purpose: distinguish annual-endpoint stability from daily safety. Takeaway: zero hypothetical drawdown follows from the formula. Units: percent below the prior sampled high. Data: derived from S1 on the same dates. How to read: deeper troughs mean larger losses from a previous annual close; the chart does not represent daily option values. 23 / RESEARCH Chart briefs: path dependence and feasibility The remaining visuals explain why the statistical illustration is not a product promise. Give model and historical panels visibly different evidence labels. 6. Regime small multiples or paired bars. Purpose: show bull, bear and nearly flat or poor-return examples. Takeaway: the relative outcome changes by window. Units: terminal wealth from 100, with each window length printed. Data: S1, selected complete windows ending no later than 2025; retrieved 5 November 2026. How to read: compare the pair within each window, not dollar heights across unequal lengths. 7. Monthly-start sensitivity. Purpose: reveal calendar alignment. Takeaway: the bucket split depends on entry date and sample window. Units: counts and shares of eligible overlapping 12-month observations. Data: official ERP Table B-56 (2020/2023/2026 editions), month ends December 2016-December 2025; 97 windows maturing December 2017-December 2025, retrieved 5 November 2026. Show the 2017-2025 calendar-year subset alongside it. How to read: each observation is one full year beginning at a different monthly endpoint; adjacent observations share 11 months. 8. Maturity payoff diagram. Purpose: explain the mechanism before discussing pricing. Takeaway: long underlying plus long put minus short call bounds the price-related expiry outcome. Units: underlying return versus payoff return, both percent. Source/date: analytic formula; assumptions fixed for this report on 5 November 2026. How to read: the line is flat below zero and above 9%. Label zero premium as assumed. 9. Pricing-feasibility panel. Purpose: show how the put premium compares with call proceeds. Takeaway: the desired strikes need not match in premium. Units: option value per 100 of underlying notional and resulting cap/floor percentages. Source/date: own Black-Scholes-Merton illustration, assumptions dated 5 November 2026. How to read: put cost less call proceeds is the net debit. Actual quote data, when introduced, must replace the model label. 10. Limitations panel. Purpose: prevent a scenario being read as product history or a guarantee. Takeaway: dividends, costs, pricing feasibility, mark-to-market, issuer risk and contractual terms remain separate checks. Units: categorical evidence status; no invented score. Source: this methodology and S5-S14, reviewed 5 November 2026. How to read: each row states what is verified, assumed or unavailable. 24 / RESEARCH A ten-slide narrative: establish the evidence first Build the presentation around one conclusion per slide. The narrative should remain balanced even if a reader views only the opening and closing slides. Slide 1 - The proposed section is a scenario, not a track record. Show three cards: historical index, hypothetical transformation, executable collar. Opening message: the arithmetic is calculable, but premium equality needs market evidence. Put the full title and sample period here. Slide 2 - The cap would have bound in 38 of 65 years. Use the distribution with 0% and 9% markers plus the exact 17/10/38 frequency strip. State the price-return definition and no-YTD rule directly below the headline. Slide 3 - The rule changes both tails. Use the annual return chart with labelled 2008 and 1995 examples. Message: the 0% floor removes losses at annual maturity; the 9% cap also removes gains. Slide 4 - Lower annual variability did not deliver higher full-period growth. Show the wealth chart and a compact table with terminal wealth, CAGR, annual volatility and annual-endpoint drawdown. Use log-scale disclosure and a separate total-return line. Slide 5 - The answer changes with the window. Show bear, bull and nearly flat or poor-return regime pairs plus monthly-start sensitivity. Explain overlap and avoid presenting sample percentages as future probabilities. Slide 6 - At expiry, the payoff can be drawn exactly. Use the maturity diagram and a small worked table for final levels 70, 106.50 and 120. Message: the payoff identity is simple; the price of obtaining it is a different question. Each slide should retain a one-line footer with data source/date, units and evidence type. The visual briefs on the preceding pages supply the layman explanations. 25 / RESEARCH A ten-slide narrative: finish with the trade-off The final slides should explain implementation, uncertainty and the release decision. The reader should leave understanding both what the analysis proves and what remains open. Slide 7 - A zero-premium cap is solved, not declared. Show the put-cost/call-proceeds bars: 7.08 versus 5.01 in the illustrative model. Then show the alternative model cap of 3.30% with the 0% floor. Place THEORETICAL - NOT A MARKET QUOTE above the chart. Slide 8 - Dividends, costs and settlement change investor results. Use a concise bridge: price exposure, separate distributions, net option cashflow, costs/funding/tax, resulting account return. Do not imply an additive annual shortcut is an exact self-financing strategy. Slide 9 - A floor at maturity is not daily liquidity protection. Combine the annual-endpoint drawdown visual with the limitations panel. Flag mark-to-market, basis, collateral, currency and any documented issuer/early-exit terms. Slide 10 - Implement the history and scenario panels; validate pricing and product logic separately. Show a practical release checklist with evidence status: annual calculations verified; monthly sensitivity qualified by sample; historical option execution not backtested; actual product terms unassessed. Suggested closing wording. In this historical sample, the 0%-9% annual transformation removed negative annual price returns and lowered variability, while sacrificing strong-year gains and reducing long-run wealth. It is a useful explanation of a trade-off. It is not evidence that an identical zero-premium collar or an actual product produced those results. Presentation discipline. Do not title the wealth chart IFI historical performance, guaranteed 9%, no-loss investing or free protection. Prefer price-return scenario and hypothetical annual reset. Put the investment objective and evidence boundary before any product-specific discussion. 26 / RESEARCH Reusable formulas and calculation outline The audit reproduces the historical and hypothetical headlines from frozen inputs. The reviewed calculation code uses stored source precision and separates calculation from display rounding. Annual price return. R_y = P_y / P_(y-1) - 1. Hypothetical return: g_y = min(max(R_y, 0), 0.09). The classification is R_y < 0, 0 <= R_y <= 0.09, or R_y > 0.09. Compounding and CAGR. W_0 = 100; W_y = W_(y-1) x (1 + R_y), with g_y substituted for the hypothetical series. Cumulative return = W_N / 100 - 1. CAGR = (W_N / 100)^(1/N) - 1. Volatility and drawdown. Annual volatility is the sample standard deviation of the N annual returns, with denominator N - 1. No square-root-of-12 scaling is applied to annual returns. Drawdown at sampled date t = W_t / max(W_0,...,W_t) - 1; maximum drawdown is the minimum of those values. Floor benefit and cap sacrifice. A_y = max(-R_y, 0); B_y = max(R_y - 0.09, 0). Then g_y = R_y + A_y - B_y. Annual sums of A and B are arithmetic attribution, not compounded returns. Rolling one-year sensitivity. R_12,m = P_m / P_(m-12) - 1 on a verified complete monthly grid. If a month is missing, stop or explicitly mark the affected windows; do not silently forward-fill. Do not compound overlapping twelve-month outcomes into one investment path. European model illustration. d1 = [ln(S/K) + (r - q + sigma^2/2)T] / (sigma sqrt(T)); d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt(T). C = S exp(-qT) N(d1) - K exp(-rT) N(d2); P = K exp(-rT) N(-d2) - S exp(-qT) N(-d1). N is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The model is used only to explain pricing sensitivity. Reproduce in order. Validate dates and uniqueness; calculate unrounded returns; apply buckets and clipping; compound identical dates; calculate metrics; reconcile terminal price wealth to 100 x final/initial level; export the annual audit; then round the displayed labels. The reviewed Python code and frozen source snapshots implement this sequence; raw snapshots are not republished here. 27 / RESEARCH Source register Sources were reviewed on 5 November 2026. Publication dates and market observation dates are distinct. Exact source links are provided below. [S1] NYU Stern / Aswath Damodaran, Historical Implied Equity Risk Premiums. HTML table dated January 2026. S&P 500 year-end levels, 1960-2025. Primary calculation input. The linked XLS retrieved in this session had an older update; the HTML snapshot governs this report. [S2] Slickcharts, S&P 500 Return Details. Published annual price, dividend-contribution and dividend-reinvested total returns. Total-return comparator uses 1961-2025, at the source's two-decimal percentage precision. Secondary compilation; not a direct licensed SPTR level download. [S3] S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P 500 index page. Official index definition and launch date: 4 March 1957. Index history before launch is labelled hypothetical/back-tested by S&P DJI. [S4] S&P DJI via FRED, S&P 500 [SP500]. Daily closing price index; excludes dividends. FRED describes a rolling ten-year daily-history limit. Used to verify price-index definitions; the attempted daily CSV retrieval was unavailable. The monthly sensitivity instead uses the official government tables in S16-S18. [S5] S&P DJI, Index Mathematics Methodology. September 2026 version inspected; total return and net total return, printed pages 21-22. Distinguishes price changes from dividend reinvestment and withholding adjustments. Style reference: Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged, paired Excel and PDF dated 5 November 2026. The pair was retrieved and inspected for this report. Product-specific documents and the existing IFI implementation were not inspected. 28 / RESEARCH Source register (continued) Sources were reviewed on 5 November 2026. Publication dates and market observation dates are distinct. Exact source links are provided below. [S6] Cboe, SPX Options Fact Sheet. European exercise; cash settlement; USD 100 per index-point multiplier; traditional AM and SPXW PM settlement conventions. [S7] Cboe, End-of-Month SPX Options Specifications. PM settlement on the last business day; listed tenors/strikes and settlement calculation. Current specifications do not establish historical contract availability. [S8] OCC / Options Industry Council, Collar (Protective Collar). Long underlying, long put and short call; capped upside; strike and premium effects; American equity-option assignment considerations. [S9] OCC / OIC, Options Pricing. Underlying, strike, time, volatility, dividends and interest rates affect premiums. Used for implementation explanations, not historical prices. [S10] OCC / OIC, Put/Call Parity. No-arbitrage relationships and effects of funding rates, dividends and trading frictions. Style reference: Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged, paired Excel and PDF dated 5 November 2026. The pair was retrieved and inspected for this report. Product-specific documents and the existing IFI implementation were not inspected. 29 / RESEARCH Source register (continued) Sources were reviewed on 5 November 2026. Publication dates and market observation dates are distinct. Exact source links are provided below. [S11] OCC / OIC, Black-Scholes Formula. Theoretical pricing inputs and limitations. Actual premiums are set by the market. [S12] Cboe, Hedging Downside Exposure with PPUT, CLL and CLLZ. Explains different benchmark rules, including CLLZ's monthly 2.5%-5% put spread and call sale. It is not the annual 0%-9% illustration. [S13] Cboe DataShop, Option Quote Intervals. Quote dataset documentation: interval NBBO, sizes and other fields; history advertised from January 2012. The historical quote archive was not obtained for this report. [S14] S&P DJI / Indexology, 35 years of SPX options. Documents SPX options launch on 1 July 1983. The pre-1983 portion of the price study cannot be a listed-SPX-options backtest. [S15] Robert Shiller, Online Data. Documents monthly-average stock prices and historical reconstruction. Not substituted for month-end closes in the main analysis. Style reference: Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged, paired Excel and PDF dated 5 November 2026. The pair was retrieved and inspected for this report. Product-specific documents and the existing IFI implementation were not inspected. 30 / RESEARCH Source register (continued) Sources were reviewed on 5 November 2026. Publication dates and market observation dates are distinct. Exact source links are provided below. [S16] Economic Report of the President 2020, Table B-56. Official end-of-period stock-price table. Monthly SPX levels 2017-2019 and December 2016 baseline; source attribution includes Standard & Poor's. [S17] Economic Report of the President 2023, Table B-56. Official end-of-period stock-price table. Monthly SPX levels 2020-2022. Prices are endpoints, not averages. [S18] Economic Report of the President 2026, Table B-56. Official end-of-period stock-price table. Monthly SPX levels 2023-2025. The footnote identifies the S&P composite as 500 stocks. Style reference: Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged, paired Excel and PDF dated 5 November 2026. The pair was retrieved and inspected for this report. Product-specific documents and the existing IFI implementation were not inspected. 31 / RESEARCH · PUBLIC AUDIT NOTE Audit access and data rights The complete annual endpoint and return table is not republished in this public edition. The sources remain directly accessible at NYU and Slickcharts. The published article retains the verified aggregate results, calculation definitions, boundary example and evidence limitations. Source accessibility is not a blanket redistribution licence. Open the annual-level source · Open the return-component source · Calculation methodology 32 / RESEARCH · PUBLIC AUDIT NOTE How the aggregate results were checked The 66 NYU annual levels cover year-end 1960–2025. Independent checks reproduce 65 annual returns, the 17 / 10 / 38 bucket counts, both wealth endpoints, sample standard deviations, annual-endpoint drawdown and the arithmetic floor/cap attribution. Exact rational arithmetic also reproduces the clipped terminal result from the NYU input precision. Open the annual-level source · Open the return-component source · Calculation methodology 33 / RESEARCH · PUBLIC AUDIT NOTE Source precision and reconciliation An independent comparison with an earlier Yahoo close capture found two one-hundredth-point differences, at year-end 2001 and 2003. The NYU values remain the calculation basis throughout this report; the sources are not mixed. Counts and displayed headline CAGRs are unchanged. The resulting clipped terminal values differ by about 0.035 wealth-index units from a starting value of 100. Open the annual-level source · Open the return-component source · Calculation methodology 34 / RESEARCH · PUBLIC AUDIT NOTE Monthly coverage and frozen-source discipline All 109 monthly endpoints in the government-table sample match the independent earlier close capture. The 97 one-year windows reproduce the 16 / 16 / 65 count split. This is shorter than the 65-year annual sample. Source snapshots and detailed audit files are retained for verification but are not offered as public data downloads here. No copied source HTML, publisher PDF or raw data ZIP is hosted with this reader. Open the annual-level source · Open the return-component source · Calculation methodology 35 / RESEARCH Implementation and review checklist Release the module only when its labels, data and calculation engine describe the same thing. These checks make the proposed section concrete and reviewable. 1. Resolve the actual product and tool. Inspect the existing IFI implementation and the applicable product documents. Confirm the exact reference index/version, observation and reset dates, maturity, cap/floor basis, participation, averaging, deductions, distributions, early-exit values, issuer obligations and any guarantees. Record unresolved points without inventing defaults. 2. Lock the historical data contract. Store source URLs, snapshot date, data-as-of date, year-end levels, precision and hashes. Check missing/duplicate rows, calendar alignment and data-display rights before publication. Keep the 2026 YTD card outside complete-year statistics. 3. Test the mathematical invariants. Confirm g(-10%) = 0%; g(0%) = 0%; g(6.5%) = 6.5%; g(9%) = 9%; g(12%) = 9%. Verify 2011 is classified negative from source levels. Check count totals, product compounding, identical dates, initial wealth in drawdown and the terminal price-level ratio. 4. Keep the comparators honest. Distinguish price return, gross/net total return and actual account/product return. Do not clip total returns and label them SPX option payoffs. Keep fees, taxes, funding, FX and dividends in separate documented calculations. 5. Validate the pricing panel independently. Select actual expiry/strikes and matched notionals; show bid/ask sides, sizes, timestamp and settlement convention. If zero premium is required, solve a feasible floor/cap and report any residual debit/credit. Record missing markets rather than creating executable trades from theory. 6. Review risk measures and samples. State the measurement frequency beside volatility and drawdown. Keep rolling observations labelled overlapping. Include bull, bear and poor-return windows; compare sensitivities over matched date ranges before attributing differences to start dates. 7. Check the presentation. Use the approved colours and direct labels; verify phone legibility and greyscale; ensure sources, assumptions and evidence status stay visible. Make an exact audit table downloadable only where the required data rights permit it; keep methodology tooltips accessible by tap and keyboard. 8. Verify the integration after an authorised change. Reconcile the module against the supplied audit, inspect any interactions with withdrawals or cohort allocations, and update the sitemap, tag mapping and change log. Retain the prior version. This report itself does not inspect or modify the existing tool.

A simple desk for shares, tenor and example trade dates, with independently invented numbers to explore strike, knock-out, knock-in and coupon. HYPOTHETICAL · NOT LIVE Published 5 November 2026 12 invented examples Two five-slide presentations Independently invented teaching examples. No live quotes or real trades. These summaries do not specify an investable product. Financial briefing (PowerPoint, 40 KB) Clear visual story (PowerPoint, 40 KB) Prepared 5 November 2026. These are not available products, recommendations or issuer quotes. Live pricing needs a current issuer quote and full term sheet. Capital may be at risk. 01 Start with the shares Look at every name in the basket. This is not portfolio exposure or market activity. 02 / COMPARE & REPORT Read the differences side by side Clear selection A comparison is a reading aid, not a ranking or payoff simulation. Selections last for this page session only. Tick examples in the table to build your comparison. Download comparison HTML Print comparison / save PDF 03 / READ THE TERMS The term sheet supplies the contract These examples deliberately stop short of defining an investable product. They have no issuer, actual quote, observation calendar, coupon conditions or settlement formula. Nothing here proves that a particular combination could be issued at the illustrated coupon. Shares → KI → Strike → KO → Coupon → Full terms Underlying shares The shares named in the basket. Some real contracts use the weakest-performing share; others work differently. Confirm the actual payoff design. Tenor & example date Tenor is explicitly in months here. Example trade dates are invented labels, not evidence of a transaction, quote date or observation schedule. Strike A reference level used in the contract’s settlement mechanics. Shown as a percentage of a hypothetical initial reference level. It is not a guaranteed exit price. Knock-in (KI) A barrier, expressed as a percentage of the hypothetical initial reference level, that may activate downside mechanics. Level, observation style and exact consequences must all be defined by the issuer’s contract. Knock-out (KO) A threshold, expressed as a percentage of the hypothetical initial reference level, that may trigger early termination. A level alone does not specify which shares must meet it, when it is observed or what gets paid. Coupon Shown as an assumed annual rate for this illustration. Payment conditions, frequency, accrual, fees and early termination can change the amount actually received. Rounding is a display choice, not protection For invented inputs, 72.2% strike becomes 73%, 99.2% KO becomes 100%, 57.4% KI becomes 58%, and 5.9% coupon becomes 5%. Values already at a whole percentage point stay unchanged. Rounding a barrier can change contractual outcomes; do not use rounded examples for execution. No “green means safe” score. Each heat scale uses its own fixed range across the 12 invented examples, so filters do not change its colour meaning. entries.text: Treasuries, CHF and gold: the case for a staged entry | Research Explained ← Research Explained / Market Intelligence Hub Original Hub research · 6 November 2026 The case for selectively buying US Treasuries after the election A staged approach to bonds, with separate views on CHF and gold. Research cutoff: 04:42 UTC / 12:42 Singapore time. Quote refresh checked: 05:06 UTC / 13:06 Singapore time. Each source has its own observation date. Pre-payroll research, not a live recommendation. The US employment report is scheduled for 6 November at 13:30 UTC / 21:30 Singapore time. Review this dated thesis after the release and obtain an executable quote before acting. Quote refresh · checked 6 November 2026, 05:06 UTC / 13:06 SGT The 2041 Treasury ask has moved higher again 97.006 ask · 5.046% indicated yield to maturity. Bondsupermart displayed a quote timestamp of 6 November, 1:01pm , without identifying its timezone. Bid: 96.621, yield 5.085%. Open the exact US Treasury 4.75% due 15 February 2041 . Against the 5 November chart ask of 96.897, the refreshed ask is up 0.109 per US$100 face, or 0.1125% . It is also up 0.063 (+0.0650%) from the earlier 6 November, 12:32pm ask of 96.943 used in the report below. These are indicative ask-price changes, not a traded return, and exclude coupons and costs. The two Temasek factsheets were rechecked: the displayed quotes remain 5 November, 4:28pm , with asks of 69.964 / 5.347% YTM for the 2041 and 50.514 / 5.497% for the 2070. They are not synchronous with the new Treasury quote. What changed: a slightly higher Treasury ask and slightly lower indicated yield. The staged-entry thesis is unchanged; a rise already in the price is not a promise of further gains. The original 04:42 UTC analysis, the 12:32pm bond snapshot and all model scenarios below retain their original inputs for comparison. They are not refreshed executable offers. In this report Latest quote and changes A staged approach to bonds, with separate views on CHF and gold Five takeaways What the post-election market actually shows Where the money is moving Settlement is a mechanism, not a forecast How much duration should the view carry? CHF and gold: specify the currency and the catalyst What could change the view next? Bond-specific update: the 4.75% Treasury due 2041 and Temasek A staged approach to bonds, with separate views on CHF and gold 6 November 2026 · Research update: 04:42 UTC / 12:42 Singapore time; each observation is separately timestamped There is a reasonable case for adding high-quality US Treasury duration after the election. Yields have fallen, markets are becoming more defensive, and government money-market assets have increased sharply. The more defensible approach is a measured, unlevered entry into intermediate maturities rather than an unconditional bet that settlement cash will lift bond prices over the next few days. The distinction matters. A rally has already occurred, some of the good news is already in the price, and the US employment report is due later today. CHF and gold can provide diversification, but they are separate positions with separate risks. Five takeaways Treasuries have already rallied. The official 10-year par yield fell from 4.95% on 3 November to 4.84% on 5 November. A new buyer needs a further favourable move to earn additional price gains. The clearest broad flow evidence is into government money-market funds. Their assets rose US$117.80 billion in the week ended 4 November. IEF and TLT share changes are mixed. This does not establish a delayed wave of purchases of long-dated Treasury bonds. Settlement can stagger cash availability, but does not predict returns. Most relevant US brokerage securities use T+1. Investors can trade or hedge before cash arrives, while fund redemptions can also require asset sales. CHF strength and gold strength are not interchangeable. CHF was firmer against USD in early reporting on 6 November. Spot gold was lower on the day at the latest observation used here, despite a strong weekly gain. Position size, maturity and currency exposure matter more than a broad “buy bonds” label. The 2–5-year area is a more cautious income choice; 5–10 years expresses a stronger tactical duration view. Payrolls, inflation, oil and auctions create two-way risk. What the post-election market actually shows Democrats won both the House and Senate in the 3 November US midterm election, according to Reuters. Investors interpreted divided government as a possible constraint on further fiscal expansion. The Reuters election-day follow-up also identified lower oil prices as a support for Treasuries. Treasury yields fell across selected maturities Official par yields in percent, 3, 4 and 5 November 2026. Exact values in the following table. The vertical axis begins at 4.3 percent. Treasury yields fell across selected maturities 4.3 4.5 4.7 4.9 5.1 5.3 Nov 03 Nov 04 Nov 05 2Y 5Y 10Y 30Y % Chart 1. Selected official Treasury par yields, % per year. Source: US Treasury . The solid line is 5 November. The vertical axis begins at 4.3% to make changes visible; connecting lines are a visual guide, not traded quotes. Maturity 3 Nov 4 Nov 5 Nov Change, 3–5 Nov 2 years 4.61% 4.58% 4.46% −15bp 5 years 4.74% 4.69% 4.59% −15bp 10 years 4.95% 4.90% 4.84% −11bp 30 years 5.32% 5.28% 5.25% −7bp Lower yields mean higher prices for otherwise comparable fixed-rate bonds. These observations establish repricing, not the identity of buyers or a cash-flow total. Official par yields are modelled benchmark yields, not executable prices for a specific security. An election is not automatically bullish for bonds. The 2024 presidential election produced the opposite initial response as inflation and borrowing concerns lifted yields. Policy implications and starting valuations matter. Where the money is moving Government money-market assets led the weekly increase Week ended 4 November 2026. Government plus 117.80 billion dollars; prime minus 4.03 billion; tax exempt plus 0.693 billion. Government money-market assets led the weekly increase Government +117.8 Prime -4.03 Tax exempt +0.693 Weekly change, US$ billion Chart 2. Weekly asset changes, US$ billion, week ended 4 November 2026; published 5 November. Source: Investment Company Institute . Changes are primarily driven by flows and serve as a proxy for net new cash. They are not a direct measure of Treasury purchases. ICI reported total money-market assets up US$114.46 billion to approximately US$8.02 trillion. Government funds accounted for US$117.80 billion of the increase, while prime funds declined US$4.03 billion and tax-exempt funds rose US$693 million. This supports a defensive cash-allocation interpretation. It does not prove long-duration buying. Government funds can hold cash, Treasuries, agency securities and repo. The measurement week also includes days before the election, and cash already subscribed may already be invested. The separate ICI long-term mutual-fund series showed bond-fund outflows of US$11.07 billion for the week ended 28 October. That predates the election and excludes ETFs. It cannot be combined with the money-market series to claim a single net flow into or out of Treasuries. Newly checked iShares data supply a narrower, mixed confirmation. From 4 to 5 November, IEF shares outstanding fell from 487.1 million to 485.8 million, a decrease of 1.3 million , while TLT shares rose from 597.1 million to 599.3 million, an increase of 2.2 million . On 5 November, IEF NAV was US$91.97, up 0.39% , and TLT NAV was US$81.90, up 0.20% , using the issuer's daily NAV changes. These are actual rises in dated Treasury-fund net asset values, not prices inferred from the par curve. Sources, as retrieved 6 November; linked product pages and latest-holdings files can change: IEF 4 November holdings file , IEF 5 November key facts , TLT 4 November holdings file and TLT 5 November key facts . The share-count changes are consistent with net redemptions from IEF and net creations in TLT. They do not identify the investors, source of proceeds or whether baskets were delivered in cash or securities. They are fund-level evidence, not a total for all Treasury buying. Price rises and trading volume alone do not establish cash inflows. Settlement is a mechanism, not a forecast Settlement cash does not determine its next destination Sell or redeem, then cash settles, then a separate reinvestment decision. This is an illustration, not observed money flow. Settlement cash does not determine its next destination SELL / REDEEM Trade or fund order → CASH SETTLES Timing varies → REINVEST? Destination unproven Trades, hedges and prices may move before cash arrives. Diagram 3. A possible cash sequence, not an observed flow. Source: SEC T+1 guidance , SEC settlement discussion and Fidelity settlement rules . Analytical illustration dated 6 November 2026. Illustrative sale Standard T+1 settlement What it does not establish Wednesday 4 November Thursday 5 November That proceeds remain uninvested Thursday 5 November Friday 6 November That proceeds will buy Treasuries Friday 6 November Monday 9 November That weekend delay creates new demand Actual fund cutoffs, settlement dates and cash availability vary. Money-market funds can settle the same day; other funds and cross-border transfers can take longer. Investors may move from risky funds to bonds over several sessions. But institutions can establish exposure before cash settlement using existing liquidity, repo, credit facilities or futures. Known settlement dates can also be anticipated by markets. Conversely, withdrawals can force funds to sell liquid assets. The missing evidence is the size, destination and timing of any uninvested cash. Without it, settlement alone is not enough to say a Treasury rally is likely over the next few days. How much duration should the view carry? Longer bonds react more to the same yield change Hypothetical immediate price changes in percent for a 25 basis point fall or rise in yield. Exact values follow in the table. These are scenarios, not predictions. Longer bonds react more to the same yield change 2Y +0.47% -0.47% 5Y +1.11% -1.10% 10Y +1.99% -1.94% 30Y +3.86% -3.65% Price change (%): hatched = yield +25bp; solid = yield −25bp Chart 4. Immediate model price changes for hypothetical semiannual par bonds using 5 November Treasury yields. Solid bars: yields fall 25bp. Hatched bars: yields rise 25bp. Source: calculations from the Treasury data above. These are scenarios, not forecasts; no elapsed time, fees, financing or FX. Hypothetical maturity Yield input Modified duration Price if yield −25bp Price if yield +25bp Approx. 7-day carry 2 years 4.46% 1.89 +0.47% −0.47% 0.086% 5 years 4.59% 4.42 +1.11% −1.10% 0.088% 10 years 4.84% 7.85 +1.99% −1.94% 0.093% 30 years 5.25% 15.02 +3.86% −3.65% 0.101% Over a few days, price changes dominate carry. In this illustration, yield increases of approximately 4.52bp, 1.99bp, 1.18bp and 0.67bp respectively erase seven calendar days of gross carry. Costs reduce that cushion further. This is a carry breakeven, not an inflation breakeven. Bills and money-market funds offer liquidity and income, but little upside from a duration rally. For income with lower price sensitivity, 2–5-year Treasuries can be a more cautious starting point. A 5–10-year allocation is a stronger tactical duration position, still with less sensitivity than long bonds or STRIPS. Corporate bonds introduce credit-spread and issuer risks that are not part of this Treasury thesis. The calculations assume face value 100, exact remaining maturities, semiannual coupons equal to the yield input, and an initial coupon date. Exact repricing determines the scenario returns. Actual securities require their own coupon, price, maturity, accrued interest and settlement inputs. CHF and gold: specify the currency and the catalyst Reuters on 6 November reported CHF 0.2% firmer against USD as equity risk aversion increased. It also reported December 25bp Fed-hike odds near 70%, down from more than 80% on Wednesday. Less expected tightening can help duration, but this is still a tightening-risk backdrop. Hammack and Barkin favoured gradual rate increases on 5 November. CHF strength against USD means USD/CHF falls. CHF strength for an SGD investor means CHF/SGD rises. They need not occur together: Exposure Relationship Illustration, before costs CHF in SGD CHF/SGD = USD/SGD ÷ USD/CHF USD/CHF −1% and USD/SGD −2% gives CHF/SGD about −1.01% Gold in SGD SGD gold price = XAU/USD × USD/SGD Gold +3% in USD and USD/SGD −2% gives about +0.94% in SGD Treasury in SGD (1 + USD bond return) × (1 + USD/SGD return) − 1 Bond +1% in USD and USD/SGD −2% gives −1.02% in SGD The table above contains illustrations, not quotes. A separate matched set of ECB reference fixes published by Banque de France allows a dated currency comparison: European reference date USD/CHF, CHF per USD CHF/SGD, SGD per CHF 3 November 0.819930 1.562514 4 November 0.815479 1.567044 5 November 0.817890 1.561656 These crosses are calculated from the same day's currencies-per-euro reference rates. From 3 to 5 November, CHF value rose 0.2494% against USD but fell 0.0549% against SGD . These are European reference fixes, not 6 November Asian live prices. No synchronised gold and SGD quote is used to assert a live SGD gold price. The SNB’s September assessment , summarised on 22 October, retained a 0% policy rate and flexibility to intervene in FX markets. MAS manages SGD against a basket , not a fixed bilateral USD or CHF rate. At 02:48 UTC on 6 November, Reuters reported spot gold at US$4,063.39 per troy ounce, down 0.6% on the day but up 4% over the week . Higher oil and inflation concerns were weighing on prices. The constructive gold case is lower real yields, a weaker dollar or demand for protection. The contrary case is higher real yields, tightening, cash-driven liquidation or reversal after a bounce. Falling nominal yields do not by themselves prove falling real yields. Gold also has no coupon. What could change the view next? Catalyst Date and time Focus October US employment report 6 Nov, 08:30 ET / 21:30 SGT Jobs, wages, unemployment and revisions US$58bn 3Y Treasury auction 9 Nov, 13:00 ET / 10 Nov, 02:00 SGT Demand for new supply October US CPI 10 Nov, 08:30 ET / 21:30 SGT Inflation and real-yield outlook US$42bn 10Y Treasury auction 10 Nov, 13:00 ET / 11 Nov, 02:00 SGT Intermediate-duration demand Veterans Day 11 Nov Recommended fixed-income market close US$25bn 30Y Treasury auction 12 Nov, 13:00 ET / 13 Nov, 02:00 SGT Long-end demand Sources: BLS calendar , Treasury refunding statement and SIFMA holiday recommendation . All three Treasury issues settle on 16 November. Broker and payment calendars should be checked separately. Softer jobs or inflation, continued defensive demand and orderly auctions could extend the rally. Strong wages, renewed oil inflation, hawkish policy, weak auctions or forced selling could reverse it. The view: selectively constructive on intermediate Treasuries, with a staged entry and explicit currency-risk decision. The evidence supports considering high-quality duration. It does not support a guaranteed settlement-driven rally, or an assumption that Treasuries, CHF and gold must all rise together. Before acting, check the actual security, executable yield, fees, spread, liquidity needs, duration and intended USD exposure. A USD yield is not an SGD return. Review the thesis after the employment release rather than treating an earlier market observation as current. General market research, not a personal investment recommendation or a promise of profit. Figures are timestamped and can become stale. No trade is represented as executed. Reuters observations were checked through available Reuters records and licensed syndication; primary sources support the rates, flow definitions, settlement mechanics and calendar. Bond-specific update: the 4.75% Treasury due 2041 and Temasek Checked 6 November 2026. These are indicative Bondsupermart quotes, not executable bank offers. Quote timestamps differ and the site does not identify their timezone. Prices below are per US$100 face value, before accrued interest and dealing costs. The 2041 Treasury price is already higher The exact security is the US Treasury 4.75% due 15 February 2041, ISIN US912810QN19, CUSIP 912810QN1 . Open its Bondsupermart factsheet . 6 November, 12:32pm displayed quote: ask 96.943 , ask yield to maturity 5.053% ; bid 96.574 , bid yield 5.090% . 5 November chart point: ask 96.897 , bid 96.575 . The newer ask is 0.046 price points, or 0.0475%, higher . This is a quoted-price comparison, not a completed trade or a total return. 5 October to 5 November: chart ask prices rose 92.860 → 96.897 , a 4.35% price-only gain . Coupons are excluded. Over six months, the ask fell from 99.605 on 5 May to 96.897 on 5 November, down 2.72% before coupons. The rebound is not a gain across every lookback period. The displayed headline price-change field has no clearly verified comparison period, so it is not used to calculate these returns. The dated chart points provide the baseline. Does the yield curve support buying it? It supports considering the 2041 as a deliberate longer-duration position, but does not prove it is cheap or that today is the best entry. On 5 November, official Treasury par yields were 4.46% at 2Y, 4.59% at 5Y, 4.70% at 7Y, 4.84% at 10Y, 5.27% at 20Y and 5.25% at 30Y. Treasury source . The 2041 has about 14.27 years remaining , rather than being a new 15-year benchmark. Its quoted 5.053% yield is roughly 21bp above the previous day's 10-year par yield and 22bp below the 20-year par yield. These are different instruments and timestamps , not a precise relative-value spread. There is no published 15-year point in the standard Treasury par table, and an interpolation is not an executable quote. What supports a purchase today is the combination of a roughly 5% indicated USD yield, a confirmed recent price recovery, defensive demand and the possibility of further yield declines. What weakens the case is that some of the rally is already in the price, major US data remain ahead, and roughly 10 years of modified duration means a meaningful loss if yields rise. This is more rate risk than the original report's 5–10-year core preference. The 4.75% coupon is not the 5.053% yield to maturity . Buying below par adds potential pull-to-par to the coupon stream if the bond is held and paid as promised. The simple annual coupon divided by the clean ask is about 4.90%; yield to maturity uses all scheduled cash flows and their timing. Temasek: compare maturity, not just the headline yield Indicative quote Treasury 4.75% Feb 2041 Temasek 2.375% Aug 2041 Temasek 2.5% Oct 2070 ISIN US912810QN19 US87973RBB50 US87973RAW07 Currency USD USD USD Clean bid / ask 96.574 / 96.943 69.491 / 69.964 50.125 / 50.514 Ask yield to maturity 5.053% 5.347% 5.497% Modified duration, BSM 10.081 11.550 19.042 Displayed quote timestamp 6 Nov, 12:32pm 5 Nov, 4:28pm 5 Nov, 4:28pm BSM durations are dated 5 November. Exact factsheets: Treasury 2041 , Temasek 2041 , Temasek 2070 . The Temasek 2070 offers only 15bp more indicated yield than the Temasek 2041, at the same displayed quote time, but about 65% more modified duration. That is a substantial increase in price sensitivity for a small extra yield. It is not automatically the better buy because its clean price is near 50 or because it matures much later. Both Temasek issues are obligations of Temasek Financial (I), guaranteed by Temasek Holdings. They are not Singapore government bonds and do not carry a Singapore government guarantee. The issuer describes the bonds as Aaa/AAA-rated, but ratings do not eliminate credit, liquidity or price risk. Temasek issue information and government non-guarantee . For the USD 2041, compare a maturity- and duration-aware USD Treasury benchmark plus an adequate credit/liquidity premium. For the USD 2070, the US Treasury curve has no matching 44-year benchmark. Subtracting a 30-year Treasury yield does not create a clean matched-maturity credit spread. Comparing either USD issue directly with an SGD government yield also mixes currency risk. The Temasek 2070 has a make-whole call provision and a par call from 6 April 2070; the 2041 also has call terms. Ask for yield to worst and the actual dealing spread, not just yield to maturity. A low clean price is not proof of undervaluation: low coupons and very distant principal repayment explain much of the discount. For immediate cash income, coupon divided by the clean ask is about 4.90% for the Treasury, 3.39% for Temasek 2041 and 4.95% for Temasek 2070 . These simple current yields are not yields to maturity. How much could prices move? Immediate total-yield shock Treasury 2041 Temasek 2041 Temasek 2070 Yield falls 25bp +2.56% +2.94% +4.95% Yield rises 25bp −2.48% −2.84% −4.58% Yield falls 50bp +5.21% +5.98% +10.31% Yield rises 50bp −4.88% −5.58% −8.82% These are illustrative dirty-price changes , not forecasts. Calculations use the quoted ask yields, semiannual scheduled coupons, assumed settlement on 9 November 2026, Actual/Actual for the Treasury and 30/360 for Temasek. They exclude elapsed-time carry, fees, FX, default and the value of call options. They treat the Temasek cash flows as continuing to maturity, so they are not option-adjusted effective-duration results. For Temasek, the yield change combines interest rates and credit spread. A 25bp fall in Treasury rates can be more than offset by a 50bp increase in the credit/liquidity premium, leaving the bond's overall yield 25bp higher and its price lower. At the quoted bid/ask levels, buying and immediately selling at unchanged quotes would cost approximately 0.38% of the clean ask for the Treasury, 0.68% for Temasek 2041 and 0.77% for Temasek 2070 , before bank markup, other fees or FX. This matters greatly for a trade intended to last only a few days. Practical conclusion: the Treasury 2041 is a plausible higher-duration choice if the goal is USD income plus participation in further yield declines. Temasek 2041 is the closer maturity comparison. Temasek 2070 needs a separate, much stronger willingness to accept long-horizon rate and credit risk; its small additional yield over Temasek 2041 does not by itself justify that risk. A staged purchase can spread entry timing, but cannot remove losses or make an unsuitable bond suitable. All three are USD bonds: a 3% fall in USD/SGD would turn a 2.56% USD bond-price gain into approximately a 0.52% SGD loss, before coupons and costs. Bank confirmation of the executable ask, accrued interest, settlement, minimum denomination, fees and FX exposure remains necessary. No transaction is proposed as already completed. entries.text: US Earnings | The cash-flow test | 28 Oct–6 Nov 2026 Market Intelligence Hub Research Explained All editions Full 65-page PDF Skip to report Market Intelligence Hub Independent research compilation · 6 November 2026 SGT US-listed equities / Earnings compilation Strong earnings. A tougher cash-flow test. Growth is not the same as cash returned to investors. A consolidated view of every earnings company covered in the 28 October–6 November daily editions, with repeated coverage merged and evidence checked again. Daily editions: 28 Oct–6 Nov 2026 · Underlying coverage: 27 Oct–5 Nov US dates · Reviewed 6 Nov 2026, Singapore time · Not live market data US listings Equities AI investment Research & analysis Dated research compilation 73 Company records Distinct issuers in the earnings register 66 Earnings briefs Substantive Reuters coverage; fields may be incomplete 7 Reaction-only records Market-wrap evidence, not a full results review 10 Daily editions merged One record per issuer, not repeated daily counts Five conclusions to take away A quarterly beat is only the first test. Intel, Apple and CVS illustrate how guidance, costs or structural uncertainty can dominate the reported result. [S04] [S05] [S64] The AI cycle has different business models, not one common outcome. Distinguish selling equipment, operating infrastructure and monetising software. Each has different capital and funding needs. [S07] [S17] [S06] Consumer strength is selective. Premium brands and value-led restaurants can both find demand, while other companies face affordability or volume pressure. [S34] [S29] [S67] Energy profits need a normalised-price stress test. Strong current cash generation does not remove exposure to commodity and refining-margin reversals. [S69] [S74] Credit investors need the cash-flow statement and the financing plan. A bond coupon, backlog or revenue run-rate cannot substitute for cash available after investment. [S78] [S79] [S17] Switch to dark Print / save PDF Export 73-company CSV Jump to company register 01 Earnings tone 02 Major companies 03 AI & technology 04 Consumer & industrials 05 Financials 06 Healthcare & energy 07 Outlook & scenarios 08 Credit & macro 09 Client discussion All 73 companies Methods & corrections Sources 01 / Earnings tone The story moved from revenue growth to the quality of returns. The compilation captures divergence, not a uniform collapse in demand. The evidence is strongest when a result, its forward outlook and its market reaction are read together. Analytical framework The same quarter can deliver a beat and a selloff 01 Reported quarter What was earned? 02 Forward outlook What may change? 03 Cash requirement What must be reinvested? 04 Price paid What was already expected? Analysis: share prices discount the future, not only the latest scorecard. A better-than-expected quarter can still be followed by a lower valuation when future margins, cash generation or strategic clarity weaken. Illustrative decision framework, not a numerical valuation model. Company examples appear below. [S04] [S05] [S64] Exhibit 01 / Dated market context Selected S&P 500 closes show changing sentiment 7,300 7,500 7,800 7,722.60 27 Oct 7,743.97 28 Oct 7,568.92 3 Nov 7,353.73 5 Nov US close, 2026 S&P 500 points 27 Oct 7,722.60 28 Oct 7,743.97 3 Nov 7,568.92 5 Nov 7,353.73 How to read. Each dot is a separately verified close. The scale is 7,300–7,800 points and does not start at zero. No line joins missing dates. S&P 500 price index, points, USD market context. Selected closes in 2026; excludes dividends. Not a total-return series or live chart. [S22] [S18] [S19] [S75] Exhibit 02 / Scope of this compilation Do not mistake this sample for the whole market Coverage Count Meaning Technology 21 Suppliers, platforms, software and wrap-only records Consumer 15 Retail, food, travel and services Healthcare 12 Drugmakers, health insurers and animal health Industrials 10 Transport, defence and materials Financials 8 Payments, insurers, alternatives and fintech Energy 7 Upstream, refining and LNG The selection follows the earlier editions. It is not a census of US results, a market-cap ranking or a representative beat-rate survey. Counts calculated from the deduplicated register in this report; classification is editorial, not an official sector index. In plain English A company can sell more, earn more and still disappoint shareholders. Ask what changed in the outlook, the cost of growth and the price investors were already paying. 02 / Major companies Read the earnings beat and the financing bill together. The largest names expose the distinction between accounting profit and cash after investment. Cash flow is a useful diagnostic, but a single quarter can also be distorted by payment timing and delivery schedules. Exhibit 03 / Expectations versus reaction A beat and a negative reaction are not a contradiction Company Latest EPS / consensus, USD Reaction in cited article What mattered next INTC 0.52 / 0.40 −23%, after hours Weaker next-quarter outlook AAPL 2.10 / 1.99 −4% during call; later −2% Holiday margin pressure CVS 2.09 / 1.65 −12.6%, Reuters intraday snapshot Unexpected planned separation EXPE 9.39 / 8.89 −9%, after hours Holiday revenue outlook How to read. Compare actual with consensus inside each row. These are different share-price observation times, not a synchronised ranking. EPS definitions follow the issuer-specific cards. Reuters coverage 29 Oct–4 Nov 2026. Actual results and future guidance are kept separate. [S04] [S05] [S64] [S30] Exhibit 04 / Quarterly cash generation Microsoft and Alphabet: comparable quarterly periods Free cash flow · USD billion · quarter ended September 2026 -15 0 25 Microsoft +18.6 Alphabet −9.07 Free cash flow · USD billion · quarter ended September 2026 Microsoft +18.6 Alphabet −9.07 -15 Zero-based scale 25 How to read. Bars extend from zero. Negative free cash flow means investment exceeded the operating cash measure used in the source. Company-defined free cash flow, as reported by Reuters. Alphabet’s more precise −$9.07bn observation is in the Microsoft story; its own story rounds to −$9.1bn. Comparability can still be affected by lease treatment. [S01] [S02] Exhibit 05 / Different period, separate display Amazon belongs in a different-period panel −US$42.4bn Trailing 12-month free cash flow US$77.26bn Quarterly capital expenditure US$46bn Quarterly AWS sales Analysis: a longer cash-flow window cannot be compared as though it were one quarter. entries.text: AI’s financing loop · Research · 10 Nov 2026 Research papers Dated editions and companions Sources and review notes MARKET INTEL · AI FINANCING / CREDIT RESEARCH AI’s financing loop raises the cost of disappointment Circular funding, rising debt-insurance costs and supplier guarantees warrant closer scrutiny. They do not, by themselves, establish that a crash has begun. Research cutoff: 10 November 2026, 01:53 SGT · Edition 1 · Independent educational analysis US BIS Artificial intelligence Credit Financing · Analysis Five key takeaways The overlap is measurable. In the BIS sample, circular deals represented 16.1% of AI-to-AI deal count but 46.4% of disclosed deal value during 2021–2025. These are financing statistics, not a share of AI revenue. [1] Credit markets are signalling a higher price for risk. Dated October reports document stress, especially at CoreWeave. Trading volume and wider spreads alone do not prove banks are exiting all AI exposure. [9] [12] Guarantees transfer risk back to suppliers. Read the trigger, timing, collateral recovery and legal cap before treating a headline amount as a loss. [4] [6] [7] A quoted default probability is model-dependent. Recovery assumptions and contract conventions matter; market-implied risk is not an objective forecast. The practical response is to review overlapping exposures. Assess equity, credit, funds, structured products and financing together. Avoid turning a credible vulnerability into an unsupported market-timing call. 01 Video & claim checks 02 BIS evidence 03 Financing mechanics 04 Guarantee disclosures 05 Reading CDS 06 Banks & contagion 07 Historical Yields 08 Scenarios 09 Client implications 10 Sources & checks 01 / SOURCE REVIEW The video identifies a vulnerability; its title goes further than the evidence Source video Watch alongside the evidence Open on YouTube ↗ Casual Finance · page title observed: “The AI Bubble Just Flashed Its First Sign of Popping.” The initial browser title differed. The video connects circular investment, more expensive default protection, lender hedging and supplier backstops. Its analogy to 2007 is an interpretation; this report tests the mechanisms separately. Evidence coverage is explicit. The full auto-generated transcript was reviewed. The sponsorship segment is excluded. The table audits selected financially material claims, not every historical anecdote or assertion. No video artwork is reproduced. [1] Supported within the study’s scope. It is not 55.2% of all AI spending, revenue or GDP. 02:12 · CDS activity rose from roughly US$2bn to more than US$9bn weekly A 20 October 2026 report attributes these weekly averages to Morgan Stanley, for CDS linked to seven named issuers in July and September 2026. [12] Reported, not independently reconstructed. [10] [11] Both are dated observations. [9] Stress is supported. [8] Broad AI-adjacent industries. Neither a 25% realised loss nor a current Singapore-bank statistic. 13:10–14:14 · US$72bn + US$105bn + US$48bn of support Company disclosures support distinct kinds of backstop amounts. [4] [5] [6] [7] [18] Arithmetic is US$225bn, but dates, activation and legal exposures differ. Do not label it cash disbursed or expected loss. They are not used to size exposures or justify the conclusion. Relative phrases such as “last week” are replaced by source dates. 02 / FACTS AND DENOMINATORS Large circular financing deals deserve scrutiny—but the BIS does not measure fake sales Evidence Different questions produce different percentages AI investors’ outgoing value → AI targets 28.7% AI targets’ incoming value ← AI investors 55.2% 0 100% Source: BIS Bulletin 137, printed p.3 / PDF p.5, Graph 3A. 2021–2025; disclosed deal value; %; no currency conversion. Percent of disclosed deal count or value, with distinct denominators. Evidence Circular deals are concentrated in larger rounds Circular share of AI-to-AI deal count 16.1% Circular share of AI-to-AI disclosed value 46.4% 0 100% Source: same paper, Graph 3B. Zero-based 0–100% scale. Full disclosed round value, not the investor’s own cheque. [1] Why it matters: the value-weighted exposure is larger than the deal-count share suggests. Circular deals are concentrated in larger rounds Investment observations 2021–2025; BIS publication 1 Oct 2026. Percent of disclosed deal count or value, with distinct denominators. Source / methodological basis ↗ Takeaway: Circular deals are concentrated in larger rounds Disclosed round value is not the investor’s cheque, revenue or traced cash; denominator and sample boundaries apply. Subject: Circular deals are concentrated in larger rounds How to read: compare the labelled observations and units; use the accompanying explanation and limitations. Figures describe the stated sample or illustrative assumptions, not a forecast. The study tracks relationships, not traced banknotes. Its universe contains 1,246 AI firms and 972 intra-AI investment relationships in 2021–2025. A relationship counts as circular if an investment link and a supplier–customer link coexist at any point within that five-year window. This does not establish that each investment financed a specific purchase. [1] The full financing round can enter the numerator. If one participating AI investor has a commercial link to the target, the deal is classified as circular and the full disclosed round value is counted once. The paper does not allocate that total among investors. Deal count, relationship count and disclosed value are different measures. [1] Technical detail · reproduce the headline ratios correctly Outgoing AI-to-AI share = disclosed AI-to-AI deal value ÷ disclosed value of all deals in which AI firms invest Incoming AI-to-AI share = disclosed AI-to-AI deal value ÷ disclosed value of all deals in which AI firms receive investment Circular value share = disclosed circular AI-to-AI deal value ÷ disclosed value of all AI-to-AI deals Do not manufacture missing totals. The underlying proprietary deal microdata were not obtained. Charts reproduce the paper’s published percentages; they are not an independent re-estimation. Incomplete disclosure, broad relationship timing and sample coverage limit inference. Economic reasons exist alongside the risks. Suppliers can understand customers better than outside financiers; customers can finance scarce inputs; shared ownership can support specialised investments. The concern is dependence on continuing financing and final demand—not circularity alone. The study notes parallels with vendor finance in telecoms, while distinguishing debt from equity exposure. [1] 03 / HOW IT WORKS A supplier can lose both its customer’s orders and the value of its support Teaching diagram Financing and commercial exposure can converge Banks / investors Supply financing SPV Owns equipment AI supplier Sells equipment AI customer Leases capacity Debt / capital Debt service Capacity Lease cash ↑ Equipment payment Contingent support ↑ Conceptual map, not a legal chart of a particular transaction. Arrows label cash/service directions; dashed line is contingent support, not an immediate payment. No scale or transaction amounts. [1] [3] Financing and commercial exposure can converge Analytical illustration at research cutoff 10 Nov 2026. Qualitative relationships; arrows are directions of obligations, not measured amounts. Source / methodological basis ↗ Takeaway: Financing and commercial exposure can converge Simplified analytical framework; actual contractual structures vary. Subject: Financing and commercial exposure can converge How to read: follow the labelled arrows to distinguish financing, payments and contingent support; no arrow represents a measured amount. Analysis Trace the outside customer’s cash The loop needs an economic endpoint. An AI firm receives financing, pays for computing capacity, and tries to earn revenue from users. The supplier may book genuine sales while also carrying an investment or guarantee exposure. Financing is not operating revenue for the recipient. The stress can arrive through several channels. Weak customer cash generation can cut equipment orders, reduce investment values and trigger support obligations. A fall in resale values can increase losses precisely when default risk rises. A simple reading test. Ask whether end users pay enough, at sustainable margins, to cover operations, replacement equipment and debt service without repeated new funding. Trace the outside customer’s cash Analytical illustration at research cutoff 10 Nov 2026. Qualitative relationships; arrows are directions of obligations, not measured amounts. Source / methodological basis ↗ Takeaway: Trace the outside customer’s cash Simplified analytical framework; actual contractual structures vary. Relationship Legitimate purpose Main vulnerability Supplier finances customer Support adoption and understand credit risk through usage. Revenue may depend on continuing supplier funding. Customer finances supplier Secure scarce chips, power or specialised infrastructure. Capital becomes tied to a narrow input or counterparty. Investment plus two-way trade Coordinate products and reduce contractual disputes. More links can obscure where the ultimate loss lands. Financing and commercial links Analytical illustration at research cutoff 10 Nov 2026. Qualitative relationships; arrows are directions of obligations, not measured amounts. Source / methodological basis ↗ Takeaway: A supplier can lose both its customer’s orders and the value of its support Simplified analytical framework; actual contractual structures vary. Subject: Financing and commercial links How to read: compare the labelled observations and units; use the accompanying explanation and limitations. Figures describe the stated sample or illustrative assumptions, not a forecast. Relationship types adapted in original form from BIS Bulletin 137, printed pp.1–4. [1] 04 / COMPANY FILINGS Headline backstops are conditional exposures, not an immediate cash bill Company / source date Disclosed amount and mechanism What it does—and does not—mean Broadcom · 26–27 Oct 2026 US$63bn financing through an SPV; approximately US$43bn maximum undiscounted backstop at deployment. [3] [4] Exposure rises with delivery and falls with lease payments. Default remedies and equipment proceeds reduce liability; it is not a plain guarantee of every dollar of Anthropic debt. Broadcom · earlier arrangement Earlier US$29bn maximum; 85% lease-balance formula, less asset-sale value. No payments reported under that backstop in the August-quarter filing. Customer cash receipts; capacity utilisation; cash flow after capex and leases; reduced reliance on support. Growth relies increasingly on finance provided or guaranteed by suppliers. Firm-specific spreads, funding access, cancellations and utilisation—not only sector averages. Broad borrower failures and simultaneous support calls, or much stronger cash conversion than expected. Different tickers may share the same ultimate source of demand. AI-linked corporate bonds / private credit Read borrower, guarantor, collateral, covenants, seniority and funding maturities. Separate coupon from yield and expected recovery. A high yield may compensate for a real possibility of permanent loss; illiquidity complicates exit. Structured investments / short puts Check contingent share-delivery obligations, issuer risk and correlated underlying names against available cash. Premium income does not cap equity downside; several names can weaken together. For a concentrated investor, rebalancing toward an intended risk budget is more defensible than selecting a crash date from a video. For a new purchase, require a valuation and cash-generation case that survives less generous refinancing. This report does not provide current prices or a security-specific buy/sell target. What would change the view? More revenue collected from independent end users, stronger cash generation after capital spending, less reliance on supplier support, and improving financing terms would weaken the cautious case. Rising guarantees without commensurate cash generation would strengthen it. Client-ready explanation AI suppliers increasingly help finance or guarantee their customers. That can accelerate genuine growth, but it also means one customer problem can hurt sales and create financial losses at the same time. Credit markets are charging more for some of these risks. The sensible response is to check cash generation, guarantees and portfolio concentration—not assume that every AI company is about to fail.
