Overview / 01 The price of growth. The value of income. A decision-led analysis of the JPM Guide to the Markets | U.S. 4Q 2026 The price of growth. The value of income.. The four figures are anchors for the analysis, not a combined score or an allocation model. The price of growth. The value of income. VALUATION 19.0x S&P 500 forward P/E CONCENTRATION 40.6% Top-ten index market value AI EXPOSURE 53.2% Unique AI-related index coverage BOND INCOME 5.56% U.S. Aggregate yield Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: The four figures are anchors for the analysis, not a combined score or an allocation model. This report connects the slides to portfolio decisions. It asks what the evidence says about earnings, valuation, inflation, income and the ability to remain invested through an adverse outcome. The highlighted slides form the core; selected adjacent slides explain the links between them. The central conclusion is to separate the opportunity from the amount of risk taken. Strong AI earnings and higher bond yields can both be useful. Neither removes valuation risk, concentration, credit losses or currency exposure. A resilient implementation gives each asset a defined job and tests the conditions that would make it fail. Read the numbers as a dated research snapshot. The source is the uploaded 71-page edition dated 30 September 2026. This report was prepared on 5 November 2026, Singapore time. It does not update the source to current market prices or represent J.P. Morgan's own investment recommendation. Decision: Start with the investment objective, then choose the exposure, entry valuation and risk budget. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Overview / 02 Five decisions matter more than one market forecast Executive synthesis | conclusions drawn from the supplied evidence Five decisions matter more than one market forecast. Each row links a source observation to a practical decision. The order is a research priority, not an allocation ranking. Five decisions matter more than one market forecast Decision Evidence anchor Practical implication Equity exposure 19.0x forward P/E Test earnings AND price Concentration 40.6% top-ten weight Look through all holdings Duration 30-year: -9.0% in +1pp scenario Size the downside Credit IG spread: 80 bps Separate yield from spread Resilience 74/26 drifted mix Review liquidity and rebalance Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: Each row links a source observation to a practical decision. The order is a research priority, not an allocation ranking. Stay selective within equities . The market can grow while individual stocks disappoint. The guide combines a 19.0x index forward P/E with substantial earnings expectations and a 40.6% top-ten weight. Review what is already priced in before adding another position with the same underlying exposure. Use bonds for a defined purpose. A higher starting yield supports future income, but the source's rate-shock outcomes differ sharply by maturity. Choosing a 30-year Treasury is also a decision to tolerate large price movements. Choosing corporate credit adds a separate default and spread decision. Monitor inflation and household stress together. Wage pressure has eased, yet core PCE remains 3.0% in the source. Aggregate household wealth looks strong while delinquency flows identify weaker borrower groups. Neither a single inflation release nor the aggregate balance sheet settles the macro outlook. Make diversification and rebalancing operational. Geography, issuer, industry, currency and funding are separate dimensions. Document the intended mix, set review conditions and retain liquidity so that an investment thesis can survive an inconvenient market path. Decision: Prioritise concentration, duration, credit quality, currency and liquidity in that order of review. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. The sequence is deliberately causal: evidence, transmission, portfolio choice, and monitoring. The report follows the decision chain from evidence to implementation 01 | Price and profits Inflection points, valuation, concentration, Mag 7 and sectors. 02 | Economic transmission Jobs, inflation, households, fiscal policy and sentiment. 03 | Income and risk Policy path, Treasury yields, rate shocks and credit spreads. 04 | Portfolio decisions Diversification, currency, funding, liquidity and monitoring. Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: The sequence is deliberately causal: evidence, transmission, portfolio choice, and monitoring. The equity section tests the relationship between price and profits. Slides 4 and 6 establish the limits of historical valuation signals. Slides 8, 10, 11 and 15 then separate concentration, earnings leadership, AI exposure and sector selection. The macro section tests the cash -flow backdrop. Labor, inflation, consumer finances, fiscal policy and sentiment each describe a different part of the economy. Reading them together avoids treating an optimistic or pessimistic survey as a complete investment case. The fixed-income section separates income from risk. Policy expectations, the Treasury curve, rate scenarios and credit spreads explain why two instruments labelled bonds can behave very differently. The final section translates those differences into an SGD-based investor's decision process. Sources, calculations and judgement remain distinct throughout. Printed data retain their original precision. Derived figures identify their formula. Forecasts carry an F or estimate label. Conceptual diagrams explain mechanisms without claiming to be measured historical relationships. Decision: Use the page headings as conclusions; use the source notes to inspect the evidence behind each conclusion. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Method / 04 Several plausible comparisons fail unless the definitions match Measurement discipline | the most consequential footnotes Several plausible comparisons fail unless the definitions match. Several plausible comparisons fail unless the definitions match Comparison What changes Required treatment 12% vs 12.7% Price vs total return Keep dividends explicit 36.1% earnings vs forward P/E Trailing vs forecast Do not reconcile directly 2026F vs NTM Calendar year vs next 12 months Retain each horizon 2.82% TIPS yield Real vs nominal Do not rank as like-for-like 11.1% debt service JPM estimate Carry estimate label Sentiment troughs Known with hindsight No live timing claim Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: Read each row as a guardrail against a specific analytical error. Source data are transcribed from printed values; independent validation of every underlying vendor series is outside this report. Price return and total return answer different questions. The rounded 12% S&P 500 figure on slide 10 is price performance; the 12.7% figure on slide 15 includes dividends. The difference is not evidence that one slide is wrong. Rounding also prevents deriving an exact dividend contribution from the two displays. Forward, trailing and calendar-year earnings are separate measures. Top-ten earnings weight on slide 8 uses the last 12 months; its valuation uses the next 12 months. Slide 10's 2026F growth is a calendar-year forecast. Slide 15 reports next-12-month growth. Do not combine them into an exact reconciliation. Yield is not the same as a realised return. TIPS have a real yield ; most credit sectors show yield to worst; leveraged loans use a three-year takeout convention. The historical return column and the future rate scenarios refer to different calculations. Forecast labels and source limitations travel with the number. The household debt-service estimate, AI forecasts and fiscal projections retain their labels. No unlabelled historical points are digitised, and no missing regression is reconstructed. Decision: Check the unit, date, denominator, return basis and estimate status before drawing a comparison. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Equities / 05 An all-time high is a price observation, not an investment conclusion Highlighted slide 4 | S&P 500 inflection points Public edition: the detailed numerical exhibit is not reproduced. The dated findings and analysis below refer to the source slides linked at the end of this section. The same index level can carry very different fundamentals. The source records 1,527 at the March 2000 peak and 1,565 at the October 2007 peak, but their forward P/E ratios were 25.2x and 15.1x. An index level alone tells us little about the profits being purchased or the competing yield on bonds . The latest observation combines a higher index with a lower multiple than some earlier peaks. At 30 September 2026, the source shows 7,652 and 19.0x. That P/E is below 2000's 25.2x and January 2022's 21.4x, while the 10-year Treasury yield in the comparison table is 5.3%, versus 1.6% at the 2022 peak. A lower relative multiple does not make the market cheap or safe. Earnings forecasts can fall and required returns can rise. Historical peaks were reached under different business mixes, margins and interest rates, so the comparisons provide context rather than a trading rule. The useful question is whether the portfolio can absorb another drawdown. The guide illustrates substantial falls between selected turning points. Liquidity and position size determine whether an investor can remain exposed while the long-term business case develops. Decision: Evaluate valuation and earnings together; do not exit or add solely because the index reaches a record. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 4 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. Equities / 06 Valuation is more useful for return discipline than for a one-year timing call Highlighted slide 6 | what the scatter plots can and cannot establish Valuation is more useful for return discipline than for a one-year timing call. This is a conceptual comparison of the two source charts, not a new statistical estimate. Valuation is more useful for return discipline than for a one-year timing call ONE-YEAR HORIZON Wide dispersion in outcomes. Starting valuation is a weak standalone timing tool. FIVE-YEAR HORIZON More visible negative association. Entry valuation informs return discipline. WHAT THE SOURCE SHOWS Monthly observations, overlapping future periods and a 19.0x current marker. WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE No raw points, fitted equation, confidence interval or exact forecast at 19.0x. Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: This is a conceptual comparison of the two source charts, not a new statistical estimate. Slide 6 uses monthly starting observations from 31 December 1993 and subsequent total returns. The one-year scatter is wide at almost every valuation. In the source chart, similar starting P/E ratios precede very different one-year total returns. Earnings surprises, changes in risk appetite and macro shocks can dominate a valuation signal over that horizon. The five-year chart displays a stronger downward association. Paying more for an earnings stream generally leaves less room for future return unless growth offsets the entry price. The chart supports disciplined long-term expectations; it does not provide an exact five-year return forecast for an investor buying at 19.0x. The source does not provide the underlying observations or regression equation. This report therefore explains the relationship without recreating a fabricated scatter, estimating a slope by eye, or attributing a precise expected return to the red marker. Overlapping five-year observations also reduce the independence of the plotted sample. Translate valuation into a hurdle rate and a stress test. Ask how much earnings growth is needed if the multiple stays unchanged or contracts. That question is actionable because it exposes the assumptions embedded in the purchase, even when the market's next move remains unknowable. Decision: Use valuation to set expectations, sizing and review conditions; keep near-term timing claims modest. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 6 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. Equities / 07 EPS can grow and investors can still lose money Analytical bridge | an exact earnings-and-multiple sensitivity EPS can grow and investors can still lose money. Rows are hypothetical EPS changes; columns are hypothetical P/E changes. Each cell is exact price return. EPS can grow and investors can still lose money 17.1x -10% multiple 19.0x Unchanged 20.9x +10% multiple Exact price return = (1 + EPS growth) x (ending P/E / 19.0) - 1 -10% EPS 0% EPS +10% EPS +20% EPS -19% -10% -1% -10% +0% +10% -1% +10% +21% +8% +20% +32% Swipe the original analytical exhibit to inspect its labels. How to read: Rows are hypothetical EPS changes; columns are hypothetical P/E changes. Each cell is exact price return. Illustration only. Starting P/E 19.0x; ending P/E 17.1x, 19.0x or 20.9x. No dividends included. Explore the EPS / valuation relationship Hypothetical inputs. Starting P/E is 19.0x; output excludes dividends, fees, taxes and FX. EPS change: 10% Ending P/E: 17.1x -1.00% (1.10 x 17.1 / 19.0 - 1) x 100 Display rounded to 2 decimals; the formula retains the input values. This is sensitivity analysis, not a forecast. Source data and calculation notes type Hypothetical EPS and P/E illustration starting pe 19.0 eps growth pct [-10, 0, 10, 20] ending pe [17.1, 19.0, 20.9] price return pct [[-19, -10, -1], [-10, 0, 10], [-1, 10, 21], [8, 20, 32]] formula (1 + EPS growth) * (ending P/E / starting P/E) - 1 excludes ["dividends", "costs", "taxes", "FX"] forecast False Price is the product of earnings per share ( EPS ) and the multiple paid for them. With a consistent EPS definition, the price-return identity is (1 + EPS growth) multiplied by the ending-to-starting P/E ratio, minus one. The matrix uses the source's 19.0x starting multiple and clearly stated hypothetical changes. A 10% earnings increase can be offset by a 10% multiple contraction. The exact result is 1.10 x 0.90 - 1 = -1%, not zero. Conversely, 10% earnings growth with a 10% expansion produces 21%. The interaction matters whenever two percentage changes are compounded. These are conditions, not forecasts. The matrix excludes dividends, fees, taxes, currency changes and any change in the forecast earnings definition. Its purpose is to show what must happen for a valuation thesis to work, not to estimate the probability of each cell. Separate business conviction from purchase-price discipline. An excellent company can deliver poor shareholder returns if expectations are too demanding. A research process should document both the earnings case and the multiple that can reasonably survive disappointment. Decision: Write the earnings assumption and exit-valuation assumption separately before approving a purchase. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 4 · Slide 6 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. Equities / 08 The index is concentrated, but the valuation premium is not confined to the leaders Supporting slide 8 | concentration, earnings and valuation Public edition: the detailed numerical exhibit is not reproduced. The dated findings and analysis below refer to the source slides linked at the end of this section. Ten companies account for 40.6% of index market capitalisation. They account for 36.1% of trailing earnings in the source. The 4.5 percentage-point gap signals a larger price weight than earnings weight, but it is not an exact forward-valuation decomposition because the earnings horizons differ. The remaining companies also carry an above-average valuation. Their 17.9x forward P/E compares with a 16.0x historical average. The top ten stand at 20.9x versus 20.8x. Simply removing the largest names does not automatically remove valuation risk. Holdings count can disguise economic concentration. An investor may own a broad U.S. fund, a technology fund and several individual leaders and still depend on the same earnings cycle. Review the combined company exposure and the common demand, spending and discount-rate drivers. Diversification should be tested against the investment thesis that could fail. Adding a different security label is insufficient if the new asset relies on the same AI investment budgets or growth expectations. Geographic, industry and factor exposures deserve separate checks. Decision: Look through funds and direct holdings; measure combined exposure to dominant issuers and shared drivers. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 8 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. Equities / 09 Similar 2026 returns conceal a very uneven multi-year journey Highlighted slide 10 | Magnificent 7 price performance Public edition: the detailed numerical exhibit is not reproduced. The dated findings and analysis below refer to the source slides linked at the end of this section. The source's rounded 2026 price returns converge at 12%. The S&P 500, the Magnificent 7 and the remaining 493 companies all show 12% year to date. That does not mean every company performed similarly, or that concentration stopped mattering. The S&P 493 is a weighted residual aggregate, not an equal-weight index. The preceding years show large differences in both directions. The Magnificent 7 fell 40% in 2022 while the remaining group fell 12%. In 2023 the respective gains were 76% and 11%. A portfolio concentrated in the winners needed the ability to withstand the earlier losses. Contribution share is different from group return. The guide attributes 34% of the 2026 index return to the Magnificent 7, compared with 63% in 2023. This is the group's share of the aggregate return, not its portfolio weight, and the rounded inputs should not be reverse-engineered into exact company exposures. A good allocation must survive dispersion within the theme. The source's individual-company chart reinforces that one label does not create one return path. Size the aggregate theme first, then examine the individual company's operating and valuation risks. Decision: Review both the upside thesis and the loss that the same exposure has historically required investors to bear. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 10 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. Equities / 10 The earnings story is strong, and the forecast hurdle is high Highlighted slide 10 | Magnificent 7 earnings growth Public edition: the detailed numerical exhibit is not reproduced. The dated findings and analysis below refer to the source slides linked at the end of this section. The guide forecasts a sharp 2026 earnings advantage for the Magnificent 7. Growth is shown at 57%, compared with 23% for the remaining 493 companies: a 34 percentage-point gap. Both numbers are forecasts rather than completed full-year outcomes. Broader earnings growth still matters. The remaining group moves from 4% in 2024 and 10% in 2025 to a forecast 23% in 2026. If delivered, this would support a wider set of businesses. It does not prove that a catch-up trade will outperform, because valuations and revisions also matter. Forecast strength raises the cost of disappointment. A company can report growing profits and still lose market value when growth falls below expectations. Review revisions, margins and cash conversion alongside the headline growth rate rather than treating a large forecast as a sufficient buy signal. Calendar-year and next-12-month estimates must stay separate. The 2026F comparison here cannot be substituted directly into slide 15's NTM sector table. The practical approach is to compare revisions within the same estimate series and reporting period. Decision: Monitor the change in expectations as closely as the expected growth level. Source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to the Markets - U.S. 4Q 2026. Slide 10 · Slide 15 . Data / reference period: 30 Sep 2026. Original analysis and original exhibit design. AI / 11 AI is already a large index exposure, and its buckets overlap Highlighted slide 11 | mapping the exposure before choosing securities Public edition: the detailed numerical exhibit is not reproduced. The dated findings and analysis below refer to the source slides linked at the end of this section. The guide defines the composite groups and explicitly removes double counting in its total. The source reports 53.2% unique S&P 500 exposure across its AI -related buckets. The five displayed industry weights add to 59.4%, but some hyperscalers also fall into other categories. The 6.2 percentage-point difference is the excess of the bucket sum over the deduplicated total; it is not a sixth industry. Coverage measures the index weight of companies in these industry definitions, not the share of S&P 500 revenue generated by AI . The categories describe different business models. Hyperscalers buy infrastructure and sell computing services. Semiconductor businesses supply key equipment. Eurozone equities return 11.4% locally but 7.8% in USD. Korea returns 86.3% locally and 98.3% in USD; India returns -9.1% locally and -14.7% in USD. These paired figures illustrate a second return driver. Country diversification can still contain thematic concentration. An allocation outside the U.S. may retain semiconductor, export or global growth exposure. Evaluate the underlying businesses and demand sources alongside the country label. Do not chase the strongest table entry. The guide offers a comparison point, not evidence that the best recent market will remain the best investment. For an SGD-based investor, the final assessment needs the SGD return and intended currency policy rather than stopping at the guide's USD presentation. A USD asset return is not automatically the SGD outcome. Let X be SGD per USD and R the asset's USD total return. Before costs and taxes, the SGD return is (1 + R) x (X at exit / X at entry) - 1. The exchange-rate direction and quotation must be stated explicitly. Income and currency changes should not be netted casually. The coupon is a cash flow; the exchange rate changes its SGD value; the asset price changes the portfolio's market value. Keeping these components separate makes the result auditable and prevents a yield figure from masking FX risk. Borrowing adds another obligation and potentially another currency. Financing cost, rollover risk, collateral recognition and margin calls are distinct from the asset's expected return. A low borrowing rate does not prove that the combined position has a satisfactory risk-adjusted outcome. No client-level leveraged simulation is inferred from this guide. A complete calculation would require actual holdings, prices, currencies , loan terms and cash -flow needs. The report therefore provides a decision framework and exact algebra, with no invented capital amount, exchange rate, financing spread or collateral assumption. First, reconcile the existing exposures. Look through funds and direct holdings for issuer, theme, sector, currency and maturity overlap. Record which risks are intentional and which have accumulated through performance or repeated purchases. Second, test cash needs and adverse paths. Identify when money is required and what could force an early sale. Examine an earnings disappointment, an increase in long yields, a widening of spreads and an adverse currency move as distinct mechanisms, using actual inputs when calculating losses. Third, compare alternatives on the same basis. Use consistent dates, total-return definitions, costs and risk measures. A switch should solve a specific problem or improve the expected outcome sufficiently to justify its costs; a higher coupon alone is not enough. Finally, write the reason to hold and the reason to review. This makes the next decision less dependent on market mood. The result is a repeatable process: define the purpose, assess the price, size the risk, monitor the evidence and update the decision when the evidence changes. entries.title: MAS–SNB | SGD support and CHF borrowing risk
entries.text: MAS–SNB | SGD support and CHF borrowing risk Research Explained Dashboard MAS–SNB research · Client one-pager SGD has policy support. CHF borrowing still carries risk. Singapore’s appreciating currency policy can support SGD, but low Swiss interest rates do not protect a borrower from a stronger Swiss franc. Two different policy holds: MAS retains currency appreciation; SNB retains a 0% policy rate. Inflation needs context: Swiss underlying pressure remained below headline inflation. Currency risk remains: a stronger CHF raises the SGD cost of repaying CHF debt. The evidence behind the view At the report cutoff Singapore / MAS Switzerland / SNB Policy stance Appreciation path maintained 14 Oct 2026 decision Policy rate held at 0% 24 Sep 2026 decision Headline inflation 2.2% September 2026 1.5% October 2026 Core inflation 2.0% · MAS core September 2026 0.5% · FSO core 1 October 2026 Inflation: % year-on-year; observation months differ. Core measures are not directly comparable: MAS excludes accommodation and private transport; Swiss core 1 excludes fresh/seasonal products, energy and fuel. Dated MAS/SNB policy and inflation observations; read the two country columns with their distinct months and core definitions. Source: Public abridgement and source register Two different policy holds: MAS retains currency appreciation; SNB retains a 0% policy rate. What could change the conclusion? CHF can strengthen even with low rates. A market sell-off can trigger safe-haven demand or repayment of CHF-funded investments. Broader Swiss inflation or policy surprises can also strengthen CHF. MAS does not target CHF/SGD. Its currency basket policy does not guarantee SGD gains against CHF. Before borrowing in CHF: check loan pricing, fees, repayment dates, hedges and collateral headroom. The SNB’s 0% is not your borrowing rate. Falling investments and a stronger CHF can occur together. Data cutoff: 6 November 2026, 17:00 Singapore time. Prepared 14 November 2026; data not refreshed. entries.text: NVIDIA deep dive | Research Explained ← Research Explained · within Market Intel Company research · public edition · 5 November 2026 NVIDIA: the platform and the price A full research framework for the AI platform, its cash generation, financing exposures and valuation assumptions. Dated research, not a live feed. Issuer facts, original analysis and external analyst resources are labelled separately. This public adaptation contains four original charts and exact-value tables; publisher valuation/rating data and private material are excluded. Tables and charts scroll horizontally on small screens. NVIDIA: the platform and the price How the business makes money Using Morningstar as an external research input The revenue engine Where demand sits Follow the cash, not only EPS Balance-sheet strength has layers What changed after the quarter Valuation: test the assumptions What would strengthen or weaken the thesis? Source map and methods 01 · NVIDIA: the platform and the price Independent deep-dive research | NASDAQ: NVDA | 05 Nov 2026 (Thu), 23:15 SGT / 15:15 UTC The investment question is no longer simply whether AI demand is strong. It is whether NVIDIA can turn that demand into durable cash returns while its commitments to the wider AI ecosystem expand. Snapshot Observation Last reported quarter Q2 FY2027, ended 26 Jul 2026 Revenue / GAAP gross margin $96.221bn / 75.0% Data Center revenue share 92.5% (calculated) Next results / call 17 Nov 2026; call 2pm PT / 18 Nov, 6am SGT Five takeaways 1. An integrated platform, not just a chip. Hardware, networking and software reinforce one another. The relevant competitive test is a customer’s total cost of running useful AI workloads. 2. Growth is exceptional, but cash deserves equal attention. Quarterly free cash flow was well below GAAP net income. Timing and investment gains matter; this is a reason to investigate conversion, not an allegation about accounting. 3. The balance sheet is changing. Supply commitments, investments and conditional customer-support guarantees must be evaluated separately from funded debt. 4. A valuation framework is more useful than one target. Assess a range of earnings and valuation multiples. The public edition links to external research without reproducing analyst estimates or ratings. 5. The next earnings call must validate quality as well as volume. Watch collections, gross margin, deployment timing and customer funding alongside revenue. Research stance: A differentiated AI franchise with substantial valuation sensitivity and ecosystem exposure. This report is a decision framework, not a personalised buy/sell instruction, a record of any investor’s position or an executed trade. Sources: [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [11] . All calculations are identified as analysis. 02 · How the business makes money Business facts [1] and an independent explanation of the economics NVIDIA sells an accelerated-computing system whose value depends on the entire workload. Its disclosed platform combines processors, networking, systems and the CUDA software stack. It uses outside foundries and packaging partners rather than owning a conventional leading-edge wafer-fabrication network. [1] Layer Plain-English function Why an investor cares Compute GPUs and CPUs perform the work Performance can support pricing and demand Network / systems Connect chips and coordinate large clusters A fast chip is less useful if the cluster stalls Software Libraries and tools let developers use the hardware Migration requires engineering time and validation Customer infrastructure Clouds and enterprises deploy the systems Power, buildings and financing can delay revenue The economic chain Customer demand → financed data-centre build → hardware delivery → working AI service → customer cash generation → collection and repeat orders. Each arrow is a separate test. A model becoming popular does not establish that a cloud provider can fund its next facility. A signed equipment order does not establish that the site has power. A shipment does not establish that cash has already been collected. Why the software moat matters The switching cost is often the work around the chip. Consider a hypothetical enterprise that has already tuned its model, testing process and deployment tools for one platform. A cheaper alternative must save enough to compensate for re-engineering, retraining and operational risk. This is an economic explanation, not a measured estimate of NVIDIA’s customer switching costs. An integrated platform can remain valuable even as individual components become more competitive. Conversely, custom accelerators may win a repetitive, well-defined workload without replacing NVIDIA everywhere. The practical questions are which workloads migrate, how quickly they migrate and whether NVIDIA’s pricing or mix changes. The supplier link to TSMC NVIDIA and TSMC have different exposures to the same investment cycle. NVIDIA captures architecture and platform economics; a foundry captures manufacturing economics across its customer mix. Owning both would not automatically remove shared AI-capital-spending or supply-chain risk. This comparison is conceptual, not a conclusion about either security’s suitability. Sources: [1] . Annual report filed 25 Feb 2026. Original explanatory analysis is not attributed to management or Morningstar. 03 · Using Morningstar as an external research input Analyst research and original analysis have different roles. Read the latest report at the publisher. Morningstar can provide a structured view of business quality, competitive durability, valuation assumptions and uncertainty. This public edition does not reproduce the analyst’s fair-value estimates, ratings, proprietary model or report screenshots. External links are supplied in the source map. [5,6,13] Four distinctions that prevent common mistakes Moat is about competitive durability. It does not mean a share price cannot fall or that competitors cannot win selected workloads. Fair value is conditional. Changing growth, margins, reinvestment, discount rates or the assumed life of excess profits changes an estimate. Uncertainty is about the range of plausible outcomes. A strong business can still be difficult to value when its market is young and fast-changing. A star rating depends on price and the provider’s methodology. An old rating is not a current recommendation. A practical reading workflow Record the analyst, update date, assumptions and uncertainty assessment from the current report. Compare its growth and margin path with the latest issuer release. Read the risk discussion before interpreting a headline discount, and distinguish what the analyst says from independent analysis. Coverage limit: The selected full Morningstar pages were not accessible for this review. Public indexed metadata and excerpts helped identify the research links; a current subscriber model or live rating was not verified. No access control was bypassed. [4] Three useful demand tests Training: Are frontier models and new entrants still commissioning large clusters? Inference: Are deployed applications producing enough usage and revenue to justify ongoing compute expenditure? Enterprise and sovereign deployments: Are announced programmes becoming installed, powered systems with identifiable cash-paying customers? The useful unit is economic output per dollar, not simply more chips. Improvements in efficiency can expand usage by lowering cost, or reduce hardware required for an unchanged workload. The net result depends on the response of demand. Neither outcome should be assumed automatically. Sources: [4] . Shares are independently calculated and rounded. When a seller allows customers to pay later, sales can outpace cash receipts even without any default. Track whether receivables turn into cash as scheduled, rather than treating strong revenue growth as sufficient evidence. GAAP EPS contains investment effects. It covers defined lease/power obligations after specified defaults and can reduce or terminate under contractual conditions. Treat $105bn as a maximum contingent cap, not as a forecast loss. [3] Equity investments are not cash substitutes. Private holdings may be difficult to sell and public holdings can fall precisely when AI funding conditions weaken. A downside test should not assume that every investment can be liquidated at its reported carrying value. A better stress test Ask what happens if customer payments slow, component commitments remain due, and investment values fall at the same time. Then compare available liquidity and operating cash generation with the timing of actual obligations. Keep gross guarantees separate from the cash needed under an assumed default scenario. The key modelling discipline is to avoid double counting. Procurement commitments usually lead to inventory and sales; they are not automatically incremental permanent losses. A guarantee may overlap with a customer’s lease economics. The full contracts and payment triggers matter more than a single alarming sum. Sources: [3] . This edition publishes only the public-source material and original explanatory analysis retained after removing unsuitable third-party content. It is not the complete original V2 report. No current market prices or investment returns are asserted. Three different ways to own bond risk A bond fund is not a bond held to maturity. A rolling portfolio does not promise repayment of your purchase price on a single maturity date. Income paid out is not the same as investment return. Compare the change in investment value plus distributions, after applicable costs. A currency hedge does not remove bond-price risk. Interest rates, credit spreads, fees and the terms of the hedge still matter. Temasek debt is not Singapore government debt. The issuer explicitly states that its debt is not guaranteed by the Singapore Government. [4] Compare structures before comparing headline yields Exposure What it represents What still needs checking PIMCO GIS Income An actively managed multi-sector income strategy. PIMCO describes flexibility across fixed-income markets and says distributions are not guaranteed. [1] Exact share-class ISIN, currency, hedging policy, charges, current dated factsheet and distribution notices. UST maturing in 2041 A direct US Treasury bond exposure, assuming the intended security is a conventional Treasury bond. Treasury bonds pay interest every six months. [2] The precise CUSIP, coupon and maturity date must be confirmed. No instrument-specific price, yield or duration is retained here. Temasek Financial (I), Series 21 USD notes with a 2.50% coupon, issued 6 October 2020 and due 6 October 2070. Temasek lists a US$1.0 billion issue. [3] Executable price, accrued interest, transaction costs, minimum denomination, full terms and current yield. How to read the comparison: the first column identifies the exposure, not a ranking. A fund distribution rate, a bond coupon and a yield to maturity measure different things. The coupon is not the yield you earn Contractual coupon 2.50% × US$100 face value ↓ US$2.50 annual coupon cash Purchase price and timing Price paid + future cash flows ↓ Yield to maturity calculation Original teaching diagram. The left side uses Temasek Series 21 contractual terms [3]. The right side is the pricing principle explained by TreasuryDirect [2], not a current yield estimate. Verified contractual fact Temasek Series 21 has a 2.50% annual coupon . For each US$100 face value, that corresponds to US$2.50 annual coupon cash before tax or costs, subject to the note terms and issuer performance. This is arithmetic from the official coupon, not a current yield quotation. [3] Pricing principle The purchase price changes the yield. TreasuryDirect explains the relationship between a fixed coupon, the price paid and yield to maturity. A bond bought below face value does not thereby have a larger contractual coupon. [2] Original analysis: yield to maturity is a discounted-cash-flow measure, not a promise of the realised compounded return. Early sale, reinvestment terms, default, costs and currency conversion can change the investor’s outcome. Separate income, capital and currency effects Fund cash distributions Distributions alone do not establish profit. A fall in NAV can offset cash paid out. A proper historical reconciliation needs dates, units held, distributions and the reinvestment convention. Restricted historical series have not been republished or reconstructed. Full-hedge assumption Under a perfectly matched full hedge, USD spot gains and losses on the hedged amount are offset. This is an idealised explanatory assumption, not a claim about any share class. Hedge carry, roll dates, changing portfolio values and implementation costs still affect results. No “net yield” shortcut is endorsed. Subtracting a single assumed annual hedge charge and one fee from a portfolio yield does not establish a realised SGD return. Share-class expenses, turnover, defaults, derivatives, timing and the precise yield definition must be reconciled first. What could change the outcome? Scenario Possible effect Counterargument or limit Government yields fall Fixed-rate bond prices may rise. Wider credit spreads or defaults may offset the gain for credit-sensitive assets. Yields rise Existing fixed-rate prices may fall. Reinvested cash can earn higher prevailing yields; a forced sale removes the option to wait. Credit conditions weaken Spreads, liquidity and repayment risk can deteriorate. Issuer strength and portfolio composition matter. Diversification is not a guarantee against loss. Hedge terms change SGD cash outcomes can differ even without unhedged USD spot exposure. Obtain a dated hedge quote and understand its tenor rather than assuming a constant cost. These are qualitative scenarios, not forecasts. No probabilities, price targets or instrument-specific sensitivity estimates are supplied because compatible current inputs have not been verified for this edition. The distinction helps explain CHF/SGD , but does not determine its next move. Latest verified snapshot Singapore Switzerland Policy decision 14 Oct: slope maintained 24 Sep: policy rate 0% Headline inflation, y/y 2.2% | Sep 1.5% | Oct Underlying inflation MAS core 2.0% | Sep TM15 core 0.6% | Aug Unemployment 2.0% overall SA | Sep 3.0% registered NSA | Oct Latest real GDP, q/q 1.1% | Q3 advance 1.5% | Q2, sports adjusted The central issue is the inflation process, not which country has the lower interest rate. Singapore is leaning against imported costs through the exchange rate. Switzerland can retain a low policy rate while its conditional inflation outlook remains consistent with price stability. Both economies are expanding, but neither country's labour market can be reduced to its headline GDP number. The bilateral currency conclusion is conditional. The SNB documented franc weakness and carry-trade incentives; MAS retained the currency path strengthened earlier in the year. Together these are consistent with downward pressure on CHF/SGD . The low policy rate also says nothing by itself about collateral recognition, margin requirements or currency losses. No current OCBC loan pricing has been assumed. Apply an exposure map before an interest-rate view. Identify the asset's currency, the liability's currency and the currency in which future expenses are paid. Then measure each leg. If NAV is already net of CHF debt, do not subtract the debt a second time. Treat cash income, asset-price P&L, FX translation and loan interest as separate lines. Historical perspective: policy regimes can change abruptly. The SNB ended its EUR/CHF minimum exchange rate on 15 January 2015. That is not a prediction of a repeat, but it shows why a central-bank preference cannot be treated as a permanent protection for an unhedged liability. [H1] Action: use the macro report to select stresses, then use actual facility inputs. Review the effect of simultaneous asset weakness and CHF strength, available liquidity for margin calls and the timing of cash needs. A personal loan or portfolio calculation would require the exact amounts and contract terms; this report supplies no invented principal, spread or return. Preserve the previous data vintage, record the new observation and compute the difference in the correct unit. Rate differences belong in percentage points; employment changes belong in persons. Flag revisions separately from newly observed economic changes. Decision discipline: revisit the explanation before changing the position. One monthly print should change the weight of evidence, not automatically produce a new directional trade. Look for agreement across underlying prices, wages, vacancies and the central bank's forecast. If they disagree, retain the uncertainty rather than averaging incompatible measures. MAS is countering imported inflation with an appreciating currency path. The SNB has judged low rates compatible with medium-term price stability, while the franc's weakening has itself eased financial conditions. Employment evidence in both countries argues for attention to composition and productivity rather than a mechanical reaction to strong GDP. The most important new challenge is Swiss inflation persistence. October's higher headline reading raises the value of watching underlying prices and the next conditional forecast. Singapore 's September easing is encouraging but does not remove the pipeline from energy and food costs. These developments narrow the case for extrapolating a historical CHF/SGD decline without reassessment. The practical stance is conditional and auditable. Use the policy divergence as a research hypothesis. Define the counter-evidence, maintain separate financing and FX calculations, and update the view when the relevant information changes. entries.text: SNB and MAS: policy transmission and portfolio risk | Public abridgement My Research Earlier published edition All editions PUBLIC ABRIDGED EDITION · 7 NOVEMBER 2026 SNB and MAS: policy transmission and portfolio risk Pending further information review. This article is published for general information while the underlying information is reviewed again. It retains selected official-source facts and independent analysis from the 6 November 2026 research, not a fresh verification of every release. Figures and conclusions may be revised. No live prices, dealing quotations or personalised investment advice are provided. Scope of this edition. This is a separate, shortened public edition of this study. Vendor market snapshots, forecasts and price-history extracts, undated screenshots and private design references are omitted pending source, accuracy and reuse review. Omission does not imply the omitted material was false. Key takeaways. Compare the two policy frameworks rather than headline rates alone; distinguish inflation composition and labour-market definitions; treat currency and financing outcomes as conditional. Earlier published edition · Official source register EVIDENCE 01 Analysis with dated evidence Two holds, different policy settings MAS keeps an appreciating currency path; the SNB keeps a low policy rate. The distinction helps explain CHF/SGD , but does not determine its next move. Dated source snapshot Singapore Switzerland Policy decision 14 Oct: slope maintained 24 Sep: policy rate 0% Headline inflation, y/y 2.2% | Sep 1.5% | Oct Underlying inflation MAS core 2.0% | Sep TM15 core 0.6% | Aug Unemployment 2.0% overall SA | Sep 3.0% registered NSA | Oct Latest real GDP, q/q 1.1% | Q3 advance 1.5% | Q2, sports adjusted The central issue is the inflation process, not which country has the lower interest rate. Singapore is leaning against imported costs through the exchange rate. Switzerland can retain a low policy rate while its conditional inflation outlook remains consistent with price stability. Both economies are expanding, but neither country's labour market can be reduced to its headline GDP number. Read the dates and definitions with every value. The unemployment measures and core inflation measures above are not harmonised. October Swiss CPI and September Singapore CPI were released after the respective policy decisions. How to read: Read across each row, then check the observation date. Core inflation and unemployment measures are not harmonised across the two countries. Read the reasoning and implications Singapore Switzerland MAS SNB CHF/SGD ANALYSIS Evidence: MAS5 SNB4 SG1 CH7 CH8 SG3 SG6 CH10 SNB5 EVIDENCE 02 Reported facts / source forecasts Two tools for the same objective Both seek price stability. MAS manages a currency basket; the SNB primarily sets a short-term policy rate and can also intervene in FX. Two monetary policy transmission channels MAS: S$NEER path Import costs + demand Consumer prices + activity SNB: rate + FX tools Rates + franc + credit Consumer prices + activity Two monetary policy transmission channels MAS: S$NEER path Import costs + demand Consumer prices + activity SNB: rate + FX tools Rates + franc + credit Consumer prices + activity How to read: the two branches show the principal transmission channels. These are mechanisms, not quantified estimates or promises about future market prices. Source: [ FW1 , FW2 , SNB6 , SNB10 ] . Policy feature MAS SNB Main setting S$NEER slope, centre and width SNB policy rate Operational transmission Trade-weighted currency conditions Money-market rates, wider financing conditions and CHF FX role Core monetary-policy instrument Additional instrument when needed What is not targeted A fixed CHF/SGD level A guaranteed CHF/SGD floor or ceiling MAS chooses the exchange rate because imported prices matter greatly. Its framework explains that imports account for almost 40 cents of each dollar spent domestically. A stronger trade-weighted SGD lowers local-currency import costs; effects reach consumer prices with lags. Domestic interest rates respond largely to international rates and currency expectations. SORA is therefore not an MAS -set policy rate. [ FW1 ] Read the reasoning and implications The SNB considers both rates and the franc. Its strategy defines price stability as CPI inflation below 2% a year while also rejecting sustained deflation. It looks through some temporary shocks rather than reacting mechanically to every monthly number. The constant-rate projection is a diagnostic exercise, not forward guidance promising an unchanged rate. [ SNB6 ] MAS SNB FX REPORTED Evidence: FW1 FW2 SNB6 SNB10 EVIDENCE 03 Reported facts / source forecasts MAS tightened before holding April and July increased the rate of appreciation. October preserved the resulting policy path. 2026 decision Slope decision 2026 core forecast 2026 headline forecast 29 Jan Maintain appreciation 1.0-2.0% 1.0-2.0% 14 Apr Increase slightly 1.5-2.5% 1.5-2.5% 27 Jul Increase very slightly 1.5-2.5% 1.5-2.5% 14 Oct Maintain appreciation 1.5-2.0% Around 2.0% The sequence was preventive tightening followed by observation. April responded to prospective energy and wider import-cost pass-through. July added a smaller adjustment as growth proved resilient and cost pressures spread. October allowed the existing appreciating path to continue working as the medium-term disinflation story remained plausible. [ MAS3 , MAS4 , MAS5 ] How to read: Read down the decision dates. These are changes in the basket’s appreciation path, not changes in a disclosed numerical interest-rate target. Read the reasoning and implications The forecast revision is narrower than a blanket downgrade. October reduced the upper bound of the 2026 core range by 0.5 percentage point, leaving the lower bound unchanged. Both 2027 inflation forecasts are 1.5-2.5%. These ranges are forecasts, not exchange-rate slopes. Width and centre were unchanged at all four 2026 decisions. No numerical slope has been invented. [ MAS2 - MAS5 ] MAS Singapore Policy REPORTED Evidence: MAS2 MAS3 MAS4 MAS5 EVIDENCE 04 Reported facts / source forecasts SNB holds as forecasts edge higher A higher inflation forecast can still justify an unchanged rate if the medium-term path remains compatible with price stability. SNB annual inflation forecasts by assessment; 2027 and 2028 both reach 0.8% in September 2026 average 2027 average 2028 average 0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8 1 Mar Jun Sep 0.7 0.8 SNB annual inflation forecasts by assessment; 2027 and 2028 both reach 0.8% in September 2026 average 2027 average 2028 average 0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8 1 Mar Jun Sep 0.7 0.8 How to read: each line follows the forecast for one calendar year across successive 2026 meetings. Units: annual-average CPI inflation, percent. All three vintages assume a constant 0% policy rate. Source: [ SNB2 , SNB3 , SNB4 ] . Assessment Rate 2026 CPI 2027 CPI 2028 CPI 19 Mar 0% 0.5% 0.5% 0.6% 18 Jun 0% 0.6% 0.6% 0.7% 24 Sep 0% 0.7% 0.8% 0.8% September brought a change in conditions without a rate change. Compared with June, the SNB raised its annual inflation forecasts by 0.1 percentage point for 2026, 0.2 for 2027 and 0.1 for 2028. Oil prices and the weaker franc explained the upward pressure. Its 2026 growth forecast rose from around 1% to 1.5-2%, while 2027 remained around 1.5%. [ SNB3 , SNB4 ] Read the reasoning and implications The intervention language also matters. March and June stressed heightened readiness to counter excessive CHF appreciation. By the September discussion, heightened readiness was no longer judged necessary, although intervention remained available. A currency can change monetary conditions even when the policy rate is flat. [ SNB2 , SNB3 , SNB5 ] SNB Switzerland Inflation REPORTED Evidence: SNB2 SNB3 SNB4 SNB5 EVIDENCE 05 Reported facts / source forecasts Inflation rose through the middle of 2026 Singapore cooled in September; Switzerland accelerated into October. The latest observations are one month apart. Annual CPI inflation, April to October 2026 Singapore headline MAS core Switzerland headline 0 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct 2.2 2.0 1.5 Annual CPI inflation, April to October 2026 Singapore headline MAS core Switzerland headline 0 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct 2.2 2.0 1.5 How to read: solid lines show headline CPI y/y; the dashed Singapore line shows MAS core. Units: percent, Apr-Oct 2026. Singapore October is unavailable and is left blank. Core definitions differ across countries. Source: [ SG1 , CH1 - CH7 ] . View exact observations 2026 Singapore headline y/y MAS core y/y Swiss headline y/y Apr 1.8% 1.4% 0.6% May 1.8% 1.4% 0.6% Jun 1.9% 1.6% 0.5% Jul 2.2% 2.0% 0.4% Aug 2.3% 2.2% 0.8% Sep 2.2% 2.0% 1.0% Oct Not released Not released 1.5% Change in published annual rate Calculation Change Singapore headline, Aug to Sep 2.2% - 2.3% -0.1 percentage point Singapore core, Aug to Sep 2.0% - 2.2% -0.2 percentage point Swiss headline, Sep to Oct 1.5% - 1.0% +0.5 percentage point Swiss headline, Jul to Oct 1.5% - 0.4% +1.1 percentage points Disinflation is not the same as falling prices. Singapore 's September headline and core price levels still rose by 0.2% and 0.1% month on month. Swiss October prices rose 0.2%. A lower annual rate can occur while the price level rises, because the comparison month a year earlier also matters. [ SG1 , CH7 ] Read the reasoning and implications Do not replace a quarterly series with a convenient average. Published monthly inflation rates are already rounded. This report preserves official quarterly aggregates where available and otherwise labels a month-to-month or end-quarter comparison explicitly. A simple average of rounded monthly annual rates is not presented as an exact official quarterly inflation rate. Singapore Switzerland Inflation REPORTED Evidence: SG1 CH1 CH2 CH3 CH4 CH5 CH6 CH7 EVIDENCE 06 Analysis with dated evidence Singapore faces imported cost pressure Energy and food costs push upward, while productivity, subsidies and competition restrain domestic services prices. Opposing forces in Singapore inflation Higher energy and food import costs Higher local costs and consumer prices SGD appreciation; productivity; subsidies; competition Lower import costs or weaker domestic pass-through Opposing forces in Singapore inflation Higher energy and food import costs Higher local costs and consumer prices SGD appreciation; productivity; subsidies; competition Lower import costs or weaker domestic pass-through How to read: the upper pathway raises costs; the lower pathway restrains their transmission. The diagram is qualitative. It does not assign percentage-point contributions to these forces. Source: [ SG2 , MAS1 , MAS4 ] . Energy reaches consumers with a lag. July's electricity-tariff increase reflected natural-gas prices during the first two and a half months of the previous quarter. Electricity and gas inflation moved from -2.9% in June to 8.7% in July. A temporary improvement in spot energy prices therefore need not immediately remove pressure from household bills. [ SG2 ] MAS core excludes accommodation and private transport. It does not exclude all food and energy. Treating it as a standard ex-food-and-energy index would misread Singapore 's inflation process. Read the reasoning and implications Productivity helps contain domestic costs. MAS reported resident average monthly earnings growth of 3.3% in Q1 and 4.0% in Q2. It also identified productivity, healthcare subsidies and telecom competition as restraints on persistent inflation. The two official H1 unit labour cost readings differ; the labour-cost card below preserves both. [ MAS1 , SG12 ] Policy analysis: the relevant test is persistence. A one-off energy shock changes relative prices. It becomes harder to look through when wage settlements, margins, rents and expectations propagate it. The appreciating currency path directly addresses import prices, while the labour-cost evidence helps MAS judge whether a wider inflation process is taking hold. MAS Singapore Inflation Energy ANALYSIS Evidence: SG1 SG2 MAS1 MAS4 SG12 EVIDENCE 07 Analysis with dated evidence Swiss prices rise while households stay cautious Higher October inflation and weak consumer sentiment create a mixed signal for the SNB . Swiss price measure Earlier observation Later observation Headline CPI y/y 0.8% | Aug 1.5% | Oct Headline CPI m/m 0.0% | Sep +0.2% | Oct Domestic inflation y/y 0.6% | May 0.6% | Aug Imported inflation y/y 0.7% | May 1.5% | Aug Oil-products inflation y/y 17.7% | May 25.2% | Aug Consumer sentiment, index points October 2025 comparison -45 | Oct 2026; 8 points lower y/y The earlier rise was concentrated in imports. The Bulletin's May-to-August comparison shows domestic inflation unchanged while imported prices accelerated. Its August TM15 core measure was 0.6%. October's release identifies higher oil-product, footwear and hospital outpatient prices, with declines in other medical services, travel packages and hotels. [ SNB1 , CH7 ] How to read: Annual inflation, monthly inflation and sentiment index points use different units. Their direction helps assess persistence and demand; do not add them. Read the reasoning and implications New on 6 November: household sentiment remains weak. SECO’s October index was -45, 8 points below October 2025. Households’ assessments of past finances, future finances and major purchases deteriorated; their economic outlook barely changed. This supports caution about domestic demand, but does not constitute a new monetary-policy decision. [ CH13 ; analysis] Policy analysis: 1.5% does not itself establish a need to hike. The SNB must judge the duration and breadth of the increase. A persistent oil shock plus currency weakness could lift underlying inflation; an energy reversal or renewed franc appreciation could do the opposite. The useful question is whether later data shift the medium-term forecast enough to change the policy judgment. The annual-average forecast and one month are different objects. October CPI of 1.5% y/y is not a direct contradiction of September's 0.7% forecast for the average of 2026. The annual average includes earlier months. It may nevertheless provide evidence that the next forecast needs revision; that is an assessment to make with the complete release history. SNB Switzerland Inflation ANALYSIS Evidence: SNB1 CH6 CH7 SNB4 SNB6 CH13 EVIDENCE 08 Analysis with dated evidence Why Switzerland often has low inflation Currency behaviour and price formation matter; differences in consumption weights alone do not explain the entire Swiss inflation advantage. Evidence What it supports What it cannot prove SNB March discussion: lower energy exposure An energy shock can affect Switzerland differently Immunity to a prolonged energy shock SNB research: smaller price rises drive most of the gap Actual product-price behaviour matters A permanent gap versus Singapore Safe-haven demand for CHF Investors may accept lower returns for perceived safety CHF appreciates in every crisis Currency pass-through Appreciation can restrain import prices A fixed bilateral FX outcome The structural explanation is more nuanced than a small energy basket. A September SNB research note compares Switzerland with the euro area over the preceding 15 years. Goods, especially food and energy, account for two-thirds of the inflation gap; services account for the remaining third. Smaller price increases explain more than different consumption weights. This is evidence about the euro area comparison, not a measured decomposition against Singapore . [ SNB8 ] How to read: The table separates an economic mechanism from a claim that the evidence cannot establish. Read the reasoning and implications Exchange-rate credibility can lower required nominal returns. The SNB describes investors' willingness to hold CHF for safety despite lower yields. Currency appreciation can then dampen imported inflation. Its March discussion also noted Switzerland 's lower energy exposure in consumption and manufacturing. These channels help explain why a large foreign policy-rate gap can coexist with credible Swiss price stability. [ SNB7 , SNB9 ] Analysis: distinguish a long-run property from a short-run trade. Persistent low inflation can support a currency's purchasing power over long periods, while an unfavourable interest differential weakens it during a particular carry-trade episode. These statements operate on different horizons and need not conflict. Neither is a guarantee about the next quarter. Switzerland SNB Inflation ANALYSIS Evidence: SNB7 SNB8 SNB9 EVIDENCE 09 Analysis with dated evidence Singapore adds jobs and sheds jobs Net employment expansion strengthened, while retrenchments and resident unemployment still warrant attention. Singapore net employment growth and retrenchments Net jobs added 0 9,400 Q1 11,400 Q2 27,700 Q3* Retrenchments 0 3,830 Q1 4,620 Q2 4,800 Q3* Singapore net employment and retrenchments; separate scales; Q3 advance Net jobs added · persons 0 9,400 Q1 11,400 Q2 27,700 Q3* Retrenchments · persons 0 3,830 Q1 4,620 Q2 4,800 Q3* How to read: separate panels show net employment change and retrenchments, persons per quarter. They are not components to subtract from each other. Employment already measures a net change and excludes migrant domestic workers. Q3 is advance. Source: [ SG3 , SG4 ] . Quarter-end / quarter Q1 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 2026 advance Overall unemployment, SA 2.0% 1.9% 2.0% Resident unemployment, SA 2.9% 2.9% 3.0% Citizen unemployment, SA 3.1% 3.0% 3.1% Net employment change +9,400 +11,400 +27,700 Retrenchments 3,830 4,620 4,800 More jobs do not mean every worker is better matched. Q3 employment expansion was predominantly nonresident, especially in construction and manufacturing. Resident gains concentrated in essential and public services. The resident/nonresident numerical split was not yet published in the advance release. [ SG3 ] Read the reasoning and implications Two Q2 indicators reveal adjustment costs. Vacancies fell from 73,300 to 68,600, and the six-month re-entry rate for retrenched residents fell from 60.7% to 54.9%. The twelve-month re-entry rate was broadly stable. The pattern points to longer job searches rather than a simple collapse in labour demand. [ SG4 ] Policy analysis: aggregate demand is only part of the problem. Skills mismatches, sectoral restructuring and ageing can coexist with strong GDP. A broad monetary easing may not solve these frictions and could worsen imported inflation. The policy response therefore depends on whether weakness is broad and cyclical or concentrated and structural. Singapore MAS Employment ANALYSIS Evidence: SG3 SG4 SG5 EVIDENCE 10 Analysis with dated evidence Swiss labour data tell several stories Raw unemployment rose in October, but the seasonally adjusted headcount fell. Quarterly survey measures add a different perspective. Measure Earlier Latest Correct reading Registered unemployed, NSA 140,480 | Sep 141,015 | Oct +535 people m/m Registered rate, NSA 3.0% | Sep 3.0% | Oct Unchanged at published precision Registered rate, SA 3.1% | Sep 3.1% | Oct SA headcount fell 1,328 ILO unemployment, NSA 5.2% | Q1 4.9% | Q2 -0.3 pp; Q2 is +0.3 pp y/y ILO unemployment, SA 5.0% | Q1 5.1% | Q2 +0.1 pp q/q Seasonality changes the October diagnosis. SECO reported 141,015 registered unemployed, 535 more than September, but its seasonally adjusted count fell by 1,328 to 145,949. Both published rates were unchanged. The raw rise alone is not evidence of an unambiguous monthly deterioration. [ CH8 ] Swiss registered rates and Singapore survey rates are not an apples-to-apples ranking. The Swiss ILO series is conceptually closer, but population coverage, adjustments and observation periods still need alignment. How to read: SA removes estimated regular seasonal effects; NSA retains them. Registered unemployment and the ILO survey measure also cover different populations. Read the reasoning and implications Survey unemployment has wider coverage than registration. The FSO's Q2 ILO rate was 4.9% NSA, versus 4.6% a year earlier. Employed persons increased 0.8% y/y. Employment and unemployment can rise together when labour supply grows faster than employment or when matching worsens. The Bulletin's SA ILO rate increased from 5.0% to 5.1% between Q1 and Q2. [ CH9 , SNB1 ] Policy analysis: the labour market leaves room for a patient SNB . Hiring recovery does not establish a nationwide wage-price spiral. Equally, pockets of slack do not justify ignoring a persistent import-price shock. Evaluate the breadth of hiring, unemployment duration, pay settlements and price-setting behaviour alongside the headline rate. Switzerland SNB Employment ANALYSIS Evidence: CH8 CH9 CH12 SNB1 EVIDENCE 11 Analysis with dated evidence Productivity matters; the labour-cost readings differ Both official releases point to contained costs, but their H1 unit labour cost figures remain unreconciled. Compensation divided by productivity determines unit labour cost Compensation per worker Output per worker Unit labour cost Compensation divided by productivity determines unit labour cost Compensation per worker Output per worker Unit labour cost How to read: compensation and productivity jointly determine unit labour cost. This is a conceptual identity with consistent definitions, not a calculation using mismatched published wage and output series. Source: [ MAS1 ; analytical framework] . Observation Source / date How to interpret it Resident average monthly earnings: 3.3% to 4.0% y/y, Q1 to Q2 MAS October Review Realised earnings; not a Swiss-comparable wage measure H1 overall unit labour cost: +0.3% MAS October Review, printed p. 37 Published reading; numerical difference unresolved H1 overall unit labour cost: -0.8% y/y; productivity: +3.8% y/y MOM / NWC, 19 Oct Productivity is real value added per actual hour worked Interview pay rises: 1.5% in 2026; 1.3% expected in 2027 SNB Bulletin 3/2026 Business indications; 2027 is a forecast Unresolved official-source difference. Both ULC figures concern H1 2026. The retrieved sources do not reconcile them. Do not interpret their difference as a change between periods, an established revision or a value to average. The qualitative cost-pressure conclusion is better supported than one supposedly definitive H1 figure. A higher wage can reflect higher productive capacity. If output per worker rises alongside pay, an employer need not increase selling prices by the wage-growth rate to maintain its cost position. Conversely, weak productivity makes even moderate wage gains harder to absorb. Margins and competitive pressure affect how much cost is passed to customers. Read the reasoning and implications The country comparison must preserve measurement differences. Singapore 's AME is not the Swiss interview measure. The first reflects earnings, including variable components; the second reports businesses' wage indications. They provide separate evidence about persistence. Subtracting one from the other would create a spurious international wage gap. Analysis: this is why employment belongs in an inflation report. Jobs, hours, vacancies and turnover help reveal bargaining pressure. Productivity, utilisation and margins show whether that pressure becomes consumer-price inflation. The useful dashboard joins these mechanisms rather than treating unemployment as a single trigger for rate changes. Employment Inflation MAS SNB ANALYSIS Evidence: MAS1 SNB1 SG12 EVIDENCE 12 Reported facts / source forecasts Growth is strong, but uneven Singapore slowed from a strong Q2; Switzerland had a large pharmaceutical contribution. Use ordinary q/q growth for this comparison. Swiss data also adjust for sporting events. Singapore Q3 is advance; Swiss Q3 is not yet available. Latest respective vintages: 14 Oct / 3 Sep 2026. Source: [ SG6 , CH10 ] . Period Singapore y/y Singapore q/q SA Swiss q/q SA, sports adjusted Q1 2026 6.4% 1.4% 0.5% Q2 2026 6.2% 1.5% 1.5% Q3 2026 5.4% advance 1.1% advance Not released Sector concentration changes the policy interpretation. Singapore 's Q3 growth remained firm even as manufacturing slowed. Switzerland 's Q2 chemicals and pharmaceuticals output rose 10.5% q/q, compared with 0.7% for the rest of manufacturing. Strong output in a high-value sector does not imply that all employers face labour shortages or all households experience the same expansion. [ SG6 , CH10 ] Read the reasoning and implications Revision discipline is essential. Singapore 's current table includes revised earlier quarters. The Swiss Bulletin's 6.3% Q2 growth number is annualised; it is not comparable with Singapore 's 1.5% ordinary q/q number. This chart uses the latest official non-annualised series and preserves the Swiss sports adjustment rather than silently mixing definitions. Singapore Switzerland GDP REPORTED Evidence: SG6 CH10 SNB1 EVIDENCE 15 Analysis with dated evidence The SNB ’s September account of franc weakness Its September discussion links CHF depreciation to interest differentials, low volatility and limited safe-haven demand. Carry trade mechanism and reversal risk Low CHF rates and low perceived FX volatility Borrow CHF; buy a higher- yielding foreign asset Initial CHF selling can weaken the franc Risk reversal: closing trades can require buying CHF Direction depends on market conditions Carry trade mechanism and reversal risk Low CHF rates and low perceived FX volatility Borrow CHF; buy a higher-yielding foreign asset Initial CHF selling can weaken the franc Risk reversal: closing trades can require buying CHF Direction depends on market conditions How to read: the arrows describe a conditional funding mechanism. Risk sentiment can reverse the sequence. This is not a forecast or an estimate of the share of the CHF/SGD return caused by carry. Source: [ SNB5 ; analysis] . Read the reasoning and implications Analysis: carry demand is strongest when the funding currency looks stable. An investor who borrows CHF and buys a higher-yielding foreign asset sells CHF initially. A wider rate gap improves the interest differential before fees and hedging. Lower perceived currency risk can encourage the position. This describes a mechanism, not evidence of the size of any individual investor's trade. The reversal mechanism is equally important. If volatility rises or the financed asset loses value, closing the position may require buying CHF. A funding currency can therefore strengthen precisely when risk assets weaken. A calm historical chart is not proof that the liability is safe. The balance between carry demand and demand for safety changes over time. SNB CHF/SGD FX ANALYSIS Evidence: SNB5 SNB9 EVIDENCE 16 Analysis with dated evidence A basket is not a bilateral promise CHF/SGD moves with both currencies. MAS can retain an appreciating basket path while SGD weakens against CHF. Identity or condition Meaning CHF/SGD = (USD/SGD) / (USD/CHF) SGD per USD divided by CHF per USD gives SGD per CHF CHF strengthens faster than SGD CHF/SGD can rise even if both appreciate against USD SGD strengthens faster than CHF CHF/SGD can fall even if both appreciate against USD MAS holds an appreciating S$NEER path The basket path remains positive; no bilateral guarantee The economic comparison is relative. A view on USD/SGD alone is not a complete CHF/SGD view. Use matching timestamps, price conventions and sources for both legs of a cross-rate calculation. Dividing observations from different times can produce a number that never represented an executable cross rate. How to read: The units cancel in the cross-rate identity. Both USD legs must use matching timestamps and price conventions. Read the reasoning and implications Interest differentials also affect forward pricing. A hedged foreign-currency return includes forward points and transaction costs. It cannot generally be assessed by subtracting only the visible cash borrowing rate from the foreign asset yield. An unhedged position retains currency risk; a hedged position changes the economics. No current forward-price quote is assumed here. Analysis: evaluate the whole set of possible paths. The most helpful decomposition is SGD policy support, CHF monetary conditions, global risk appetite and the two currencies' responses to external rates. Assigning the entire cross-rate move to one central bank obscures the other currency and encourages overconfident forecasts. CHF/SGD S$NEER FX ANALYSIS Evidence: FW1 FW2 SNB5 EVIDENCE 18 Reported facts / source forecasts Keep the forecast vintages separate Official forecasts differ by institution, definition and date. The differences are informative when labelled. It raised 2026 sports-adjusted growth from 0.9% to 1.7%, keeping 2027 at 1.6%. It expected some correction after unusually strong pharmaceutical activity. Its inflation forecasts stayed at 0.6% for both years; the later SNB projections were higher. These are separate judgments, not data errors to average away. [ CH11 ] How to read: Read each row as a separate dated forecast. Swiss growth is sports adjusted; annual inflation forecasts are annual averages. Read the reasoning and implications Singapore 's latest available annual forecast predates its latest GDP estimate. The August ministry upgrade from 2.0-4.0% to 4.5-5.5% remains the identified annual forecast. October's policy statement said revised 2026 and 2027 growth forecasts would be announced in November. This report does not invent an unreleased update. [ SG7 , MAS5 ] Analysis: forecast revisions often matter more than levels for markets. An expected weak outcome can have little price effect; a better-than-expected outcome can move prices even if its level remains modest. A proper market assessment needs the prevailing expectations and a dated market window as well as the economic release. This report does not claim to have measured those surprises. Forecasts MAS SNB Macro REPORTED Evidence: SNB4 CH11 SG7 MAS5 EVIDENCE 19 Analysis with dated evidence Scenarios for the next policy phase Use conditional triggers rather than a single unsupported CHF/SGD target. Scenario Policy interpretation Possible CHF/SGD pressure Evidence that would change the view Imported inflation fades; growth stays resilient MAS path can continue; SNB may stay patient Existing SGD support / CHF carry can persist Core prices or wages broaden unexpectedly Global risk aversion and carry unwind Both assess growth and financial conditions Upward if CHF safety demand dominates Limited CHF demand or forceful policy response Swiss inflation becomes persistent SNB tightening or firmer CHF becomes more plausible Upward if repricing exceeds Singapore 's Energy reversal; stable core and expectations Singapore growth and resident jobs weaken broadly MAS easing becomes more plausible if inflation allows Upward if SGD support falls relative to CHF Strong services demand or sticky imported inflation Renewed energy supply disruption Inflation rises while growth is hurt Ambiguous: relative exposure and policy matter Resolution of disruption or offsetting currency moves How to read: These are analytical scenarios with qualitative direction, not sourced numerical targets or probability estimates. Read the reasoning and implications Strategy: specify what would falsify the thesis. A weak-franc view is vulnerable to a narrowing international rate gap, renewed safety demand and stronger Swiss underlying inflation. A strong-SGD view is vulnerable to a broader domestic slowdown or a shift in MAS 's assessment. Record those conditions before taking a position so that new evidence has an explicit consequence. CHF/SGD MAS SNB Risk ANALYSIS Evidence: MAS5 SNB4 SNB5 SNB6 FW2 EVIDENCE 20 Analysis with dated evidence Implications for CHF-funded portfolios Keep currency translation, financing cost and asset performance separate when applying the macro view. Exposure When CHF/SGD falls When CHF/SGD rises Fixed CHF cash asset, valued in SGD SGD value falls SGD value rises Fixed CHF principal liability, valued in SGD SGD equivalent falls SGD equivalent rises Foreign asset financed in CHF Depends on asset currency, price, income and costs Same components need separate measurement Hedged currency position Hedge value and forward terms affect the result Hedge value and forward terms affect the result The financing rate is contractual. A 0% SNB policy rate is not a 0% client loan. A facility depends on its benchmark, spread, tenor, reset date and other terms. The low policy rate also says nothing by itself about collateral recognition, margin requirements or currency losses. No current OCBC loan pricing has been assumed. How to read: Each row isolates one exposure. Asset gains, liability translation, cash income and financing costs must be measured separately. Read the reasoning and implications Apply an exposure map before an interest-rate view. Identify the asset's currency, the liability's currency and the currency in which future expenses are paid. Then measure each leg. If NAV is already net of CHF debt, do not subtract the debt a second time. Treat cash income, asset-price P&L, FX translation and loan interest as separate lines. Historical perspective: policy regimes can change abruptly. The SNB ended its EUR/CHF minimum exchange rate on 15 January 2015. That is not a prediction of a repeat, but it shows why a central-bank preference cannot be treated as a permanent protection for an unhedged liability. [ H1 ] Action: use the macro report to select stresses, then use actual facility inputs. Review the effect of simultaneous asset weakness and CHF strength, available liquidity for margin calls and the timing of cash needs. A personal loan or portfolio calculation would require the exact amounts and contract terms; this report supplies no invented principal, spread or return.
