entries.text: Protection has a price: less upside Skip to brief Research Explained Dashboard One-page-style public companion · Prepared 14 November 2026 Protection has a price: less upside SPX put-and-call collars · Educational companion Hold equity exposure, buy a put and sell a call. A 0% floor and 9% cap are a hypothetical expiry rule, not a verified zero-premium quote. A maturity floor is not a guarantee of your daily account value. The trade-off, in plain English The put provides downside protection at expiry; the sold call gives away gains above its strike. Its premium can help fund the put. The actual net premium depends on market prices, chosen strikes, expiry and execution costs. With a reference starting at 100, the illustration ends between 100 and 109. A reference ending at 70 gives a combined price payoff of 100; at 105 it gives 105; at 120 it gives 109. This is matched-notional, same-expiry payoff arithmetic before premiums, dividends and costs, not an available product offer. What the historical illustration found Across 65 complete calendar years, the floor affected 17 years and the cap affected 38. Ten years lay between 0% and 9%, inclusive. These are historical sample counts, not future probabilities. Less annual downside did not mean more ending wealth. A starting 100 became 11,780.24 for the price-index path versus 3,871.85 for the hypothetical annually reset 0%–9% rule. Both exclude dividends and costs; the clipped path is not a historically priced options strategy. Before treating it as an investment Require real contract quotes and matching terms. Check the underlying vehicle, strikes, expiry, settlement, premium, spreads, fees and early-exit value. Each annual reset would need fresh market terms. The research does not validate an IFI product, guarantee a 0% net return, or establish zero-cost protection. This independently written educational brief uses the published report’s aggregate original analysis only, not the separate private one-pager or its source images. Historical returns are USD price-index returns, with no dividend reinvestment. Sample frequencies are descriptive; annual endpoints conceal intra-year risk. No raw third-party historical series is republished, no product payoff is verified, and no live trade recommendation is made. All three earned less than in the previous quarter. How much of a recovery is already in their share prices? the project maintainer · Personal research view · 6 November 2026, Singapore Singapore Equities Banking Quarterly earnings Interpretation 56.90% STI concentration Three bank weights at the 5 Nov close −9.93% Combined earnings 3Q26 profit versus the previous quarter 2.91× DBS price to book 5 Nov close ÷ 30 Sep book value Investment view I would trim a bank overweight into strength. An STI holding already places about 57 cents of every dollar in these three names. Direct bank shares can double up that exposure. The sector’s 13.58% year-on-year profit growth flatters the underlying quarter. UOB’s prior-year provisions explain much of the rebound. Combined operating profit before allowances fell 2.41% year on year. The reasons for caution differ by bank. DBS commands the highest price for its book. OCBC has the strongest operational rebuttal. UOB trades closest to book, but earns the lowest return on equity. 01 Index exposure 02 Earnings 03 The banks 04 Valuation 05 What to track Sources 01 / Index exposure Three banks set the pace for thirty stocks DBS alone represents 29.31% of the Straits Times Index. NII is the dollar interest spread earned across the balance sheet. Net interest margin (NIM) expresses it relative to average interest-earning assets. ROE measures earnings against equity. CET1 is the bank’s core equity capital ratio. One basis point (bp) is 0.01 percentage point. ¹Rounded from (1,250 ÷ 443 − 1). ²DBS reports net fees in the commercial book. DBS · 3Q26 trading update OCBC · 3Q26 results release UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights UOB · CFO presentation In plain English A bank can earn more interest dollars even as it earns less on each dollar lent. A larger loan book helps. A smaller provision charge can also lift profit without a stronger lending business. 03 / The three franchises Each bank has a different earnings test The same interest-rate move reaches the three banks through different businesses. DBS has a wealth and markets franchise, OCBC consolidates an insurer, and UOB’s comparison is especially sensitive to the credit provisions it booked last year. SGX · D05 DBS The strongest return on equity comes with the highest price for book. Morningstar · D05 S$2.813bn 3Q26 net profit 16.0% Annualised ROE 2.91× Price to book Markets trading income fell from S$469m to S$152m in one quarter. That S$317m revenue decline exceeded the S$266m drop in group net profit. Other lines absorbed part of the hit. The commercial book produced a record S$5.693bn of income. The deposit and wealth franchises strengthened. Group NII rose 4% both sequentially and year on year. Wealth fees rose 9% year on year to S$864m, and wealth assets reached S$544bn. Those figures explain why investors pay more for DBS than its peers. The premium leaves little room for a second disappointment. Group NIM averaged 1.87% but exited the quarter at 1.90%. Management’s mid-single-digit 2027 total income growth view assumes average SORA near 1.6%, two further Fed hikes by end-2027 and a stronger Singapore dollar. Follow the realised margin and the trading result separately. DBS · 3Q26 trading update DBS · CFO presentation DBS · CEO presentation SGX · O39 OCBC A record banking quarter was partly hidden by Great Eastern. Morningstar · O39 S$2.042bn 3Q26 group profit 13.1% Annualised ROE 2.06× Price to book Banking profit rose S$145m while Great Eastern’s contribution fell S$324m. Bond valuation losses and the absence of the prior quarter’s equity gains weighed on the insurer. Customer-flow trading reached S$480m, and loan growth helped banking NII rise 4% year on year even as group NIM fell 18bp. 2Q group 2,221 Banking change +145 GEH change −324 3Q group 2,042 Reading the bridge. S$ million, 2Q to 3Q26. Banking profit rose from 1,750 to 1,895. Great Eastern’s after-tax contribution fell from 471 to 147. Add the two changes to the opening balance. OCBC Results Highlights, slide 5, 6 Nov. The banking result is the clearest challenge to a cautious sector view. Banking wealth AUM reached S$358bn, NPLs were 0.8% of loans, and insurance new business embedded value rose 14% year on year to S$208m. The investment marks and new insurance business tell different stories. At twice book, some of that strength is already reflected in the price. FY26 management guidance calls for low-double-digit loan growth, at least mid-single-digit total income growth and flat to slightly lower NII. Loan credit costs of 6bp in 3Q were favourable against full-year guidance of 15–20bp. OCBC · 3Q26 results release OCBC · results highlights and CEO slides SGX · U11 UOB A lower multiple buys a lower return and greater credit sensitivity. Morningstar · U11 S$1.250bn 3Q26 net profit 10.1% Annualised ROE 1.30× Price to book A S$1.103bn fall in allowances outweighed the S$807m rise in year-on-year net profit. UOB booked S$1.361bn of allowances in 3Q25, including pre-emptive provisions, versus S$258m this quarter. Operating profit fell 3% over the same period. The allowances are pre-tax and the profit is after tax. Fees reached S$733m, up 19% year on year, but that did not offset weaker quarterly trading and the absence of prior divestment gains. NIM fell from 1.74% to 1.68% sequentially. At 46.4%, UOB also had the highest cost-to-income ratio of the three. The case for a recovery depends on earning more from the existing franchise. Management expects 2027 NII above 2026 and mid-to-high-single-digit growth in both fees and operating costs. Its 25–30bp total credit-cost guidance compares with 24bp in 3Q26. Watch the gap between income growth and expense growth. UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights UOB · CFO presentation In plain English DBS’s swing came from trading, OCBC’s from insurance investments, and UOB’s annual rebound from last year’s credit charges. A single sector headline hides all three. 04 / Valuation & distributions Share prices rose faster than book values OCBC had the largest price increase, while DBS still trades at the highest multiple. Price to book (P/B) is the share price divided by ordinary book value per share. A high multiple can be earned by sustaining a high return on that equity. The question is how much improvement the price already requires. Willie Keng’s October 2025 essay asked whether earnings could keep up with the price paid for Singapore banks. His concern about interest margins holds up year on year across all three. His rate-cycle explanation needs updating. DBS and OCBC grew quarterly NII in dollars, and DBS reported an improving exit margin. The case for caution now rests more on what investors pay for those earnings than on a blanket prediction that falling rates will squeeze every bank. The dividend offsets only part of that price move. 05 / Earnings history & what to track What would change the portfolio view? I would start by trimming the overlap between direct bank holdings and STI exposure. I would revisit that stance if returns on equity rise enough to support the premium, or if share prices offer the same earnings at a more attractive valuation. entries.text: SGS, T-bills and bank net interest margins · Research addendum · 6 Nov 2026 STI banks · Part 2 · NIM and SGS Part 1 · original report All report editions Research Papers ← Research Explained · Market Intelligence Hub Skip to report Market Intelligence Hub Research addendum / Singapore rates & banks SGS · T-bills · Bank earnings The banks’ interest-margin engine About two-thirds of the three banks’ latest quarterly income came from net interest. Eleven years of reported margins show why the yield cycle matters, and why funding costs, loan resets and hedges decide how much reaches earnings. Market Intelligence Hub · Research addendum · 6 November 2026, Singapore Bank accounts through 3Q26 · Official yield snapshot at 5 Nov close Singapore Banking SGS Quarterly earnings Interpretation Companion to Part 1 · The STI’s bank premium 64.06% NII / total income DBS + OCBC + UOB, 3Q26 86.59% Rates in the 2023 uplift Share of the banks’ combined NII increase −S$2.327bn 2025 rate effect Before volume and calendar offsets Four takeaways Banks remain heavily dependent on the interest margin. In 3Q26, net interest income contributed S$8.302bn of S$12.959bn combined group income. Costs, credit losses and tax determine how much becomes profit. The banks’ own attribution shows how large the rate effect can be. Rates explained S$5.190bn of the S$5.994bn rise in 2023 NII. In 2025, rate effects cut NII by S$2.327bn before offsets. T-bills affect competition for deposits as well as returns on bank assets. DBS reported funds returning from maturing retail T-bills into deposits as rates fell in 2025. The direction of SGS yields is only the beginning of the earnings analysis. The outcome depends on which assets and funding reprice first, their currencies, and the bank’s hedges. 01 NIM dependence 02 Yield charts 03 Eleven-year history 04 Bank attribution 05 How rates transmit 06 Latest quarter 07 Hedges & risk 08 What to track Sources 01 / The earnings engine Most income still comes from the interest spread Net interest income (NII) is interest earned on loans, securities and other earning assets, less interest paid on deposits and other funding. Net interest margin (NIM) divides that annualised income by average interest-earning assets. It measures the spread earned across the balance sheet. Exhibit 01 · 3Q26 group income composition NII supplied 62%–67% of each group’s income DBS 63.49% OCBC 61.96% UOB 67.38% 3Q26, S$m NII Other income Total DBS 3,711 2,134 5,845 OCBC 2,313 1,420 3,733 UOB 2,278 1,103 3,381 How to read. The filled portion is NII as a share of total group income. Other income is the remainder. This is revenue composition. OCBC includes Great Eastern. Its Banking Operations share is 2,268 ÷ 3,506 = 64.69%. DBS · 3Q26 trading update OCBC · 3Q26 results release OCBC · 3Q26 results highlights UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights The identity behind the results A small change in margin acts on a very large asset base NII = NIM × average earning assets Full-year basis. Apply the reporting-period fraction for an interim period. DBS’s FY2025 numbers make the scale tangible. S$14,500m of NII divided by S$721,393m of average interest-bearing assets gives the reported 2.01% margin after rounding. NIM can decline while NII rises. Expanding the asset base or adding lower-margin, profitable liquid assets can increase interest dollars despite reducing the average percentage earned. Why loan rate minus deposit rate does not reproduce NIM The numerator and denominator cover the full earning balance sheet. Banks hold securities and interbank placements as well as loans, and use wholesale funding, equity and deposits with different costs. The average asset and liability balances differ. Simple subtraction of two quoted customer rates omits these effects. DBS · FY2025 performance summary In plain English Think of NIM as the margin on each dollar of earning assets. NII also depends on how many dollars the bank puts to work. 02 / Embedded Hub history The Singapore yield cycle in context The chart below embeds the SGS and T-bill observations already used by the Market Intelligence Hub. Its snapshot runs through August 2026. The separate MAS panel provides an official 5 November observation for the current rate environment. Exhibit 02 · preserved Hub series · % p.a. Compare the short end with the 10-year yield First series 1Y T-bill · Hub “SGD 1Y” 6M T-bill · Hub “SGD 6M” 10Y SGS bond Second series 10Y SGS bond 1Y T-bill 6M T-bill Historical window Oct 2006–Aug 2026 2015 onward 2019 onward 2020 onward 2022 onward 1Y · Aug 2026 1.65% 10Y · Aug 2026 2.35% 6M · Aug 2026 1.57% Snapshot ends Aug 2026 Read the embedded monthly observations How to read. Both lines are annualised yields, observed monthly. The original Hub labels “SGD 1Y” and “SGD 6M” denote T-bill tenors. Broken series remain gaps. MAS records a 6M issuance gap between late 2013 and July 2019. The Hub source is a supplied MAS-labelled workbook. Its monthly sampling method and original retrieval date are unverified, so this is a preserved history snapshot. Market Intelligence Hub · Yield history Hub · preserved SGS history data MAS · historical benchmark definitions Exhibit 03 · official closing curve · 5 Nov 2026 The 10-year SGS yielded 2.15% Tenor 6M 1Y 2Y 5Y 10Y Yield, % p.a. 1.86 1.88 1.82 1.96 2.15 How to read. Points are MAS closing benchmark bid yields on 5 Nov 2026. Maturity is measured in years. The 10Y–6M gap is 29bp. A bank’s actual funding and assets have different rates and maturities. MAS · daily SGS benchmark yields Auction and secondary-market measures A 6-month T-bill puts a visible price on household cash The latest MAS-listed 6M auction cut-off was 1.86% for BS26122V, due to be issued on 10 November. The prior issue’s cut-off was 1.95%, a decline of 9bp. On 5 November, the benchmark’s secondary-market closing bid yield was also 1.86%. Customers compare that return with deposits. Higher T-bill yields can encourage funds to leave a low-paying account or push a bank to improve deposit offers. When the relative appeal fades and bills mature, some cash can return. The loan reset follows its contractual benchmark. A floating SGD mortgage linked to compounded SORA responds to its own reset convention. MAS defines SORA from actual unsecured overnight SGD interbank borrowing, with compounded tenors published separately. MAS · latest T-bill cut-off yield MAS · daily SGS benchmark yields MAS · SORA benchmark In plain English The short end tells you what cash can earn. The longer end shows pricing for longer commitments. A bank’s margin depends on the rates and reset dates of its own assets and funding. 03 / Eleven years of reported margins The low-rate years and the 2023 peak are visible in all three banks Full-year group NIM rose sharply from 2021 to 2023, then softened through 2025. DBS gained 70bp over that upswing, OCBC 74bp and UOB 53bp. These are realised group margins after the banks’ funding costs and balance-sheet mix. Exhibit 04 · annual group NIM · % Margins peaked in 2023 across this sample DBS OCBC UOB How to read. One point per full financial year, 2015–2025. All three lines use group NIM and the same scale. Their reported averaging convention covers the full year. Company colours follow the shared Singapore Jade assignment, with solid, dashed and dotted lines. DBS · FY2023 performance summary DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2023 financial highlights OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2023 financial statements UOB · FY2025 financial statements Exhibit 05 · annual group NII · S$bn Growing assets can keep interest dollars high DBS OCBC UOB How to read. The same years and banks, now showing NII in Singapore dollars. DBS’s FY2025 NII rose while its margin narrowed. Comparisons span changes in the size and geographic mix of the franchises. DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2025 financial statements Exact annual NIM · issuer figures Financial year DBS OCBC UOB 2015 1.77% 1.67% 1.77% 2016 1.80% 1.67% 1.71% 2017 1.75% 1.65% 1.77% 2018 1.85% 1.70% 1.82% 2019 1.89% 1.77% 1.78% 2020 1.62% 1.61% 1.57% 2021 1.45% 1.54% 1.56% 2022 1.75% 1.91% 1.86% 2023 2.15% 2.28% 2.09% 2024 2.13% 2.20% 2.03% 2025 2.01% 1.91% 1.89% Read exact annual NII and historical source coverage NII, S$m DBS OCBC UOB 2015 7,100 5,189 4,926 2016 7,305 5,052 4,991 2017 7,791 5,423 5,528 2018 8,955 5,890 6,220 2019 9,625 6,331 6,563 2020 9,076 5,966 6,035 2021 8,440 5,855 6,388 2022 10,941 7,688 8,343 2023 13,642 9,645 9,679 2024 14,424 9,755 9,674 2025 14,500 9,150 9,355 Historical source documents are listed in the source register. Annual and quarterly data use their own series. Rounding in individual reports can create S$1m differences between summed quarters and reported annual totals. 2015–2019 Margins varied within a relatively narrow range. By 2019, DBS reported 1.89%, OCBC 1.77% and UOB 1.78%. Each bank entered the pandemic with a different asset and funding mix. 2020–2021 Lower rates compressed the spread. By 2021, NIM was 1.45% at DBS, 1.54% at OCBC and 1.56% at UOB. Falling deposit costs could only offset part of the decline in asset yields. 2022–2025 The higher-rate cycle lifted margins before the benefits receded. OCBC’s NIM reached 2.28% in 2023 and fell to 1.91% by 2025. DBS and UOB also declined from their 2023 highs. In plain English The banks kept their franchises throughout the cycle. The spread earned on those franchises changed substantially, which changed the earnings available to shareholders. 04 / What the banks themselves attributed to rates The 2023 NII uplift was mostly rate-driven In the banks’ own decompositions, rate effects contributed S$5.190bn, or 86.59%, of the combined FY2023 NII increase. Volume effects contributed S$804m. These calculations sum each bank’s published group attribution across its assets, funding and currencies. Exhibit 06 · FY2023 versus FY2022 · S$m Rates supplied most of the S$5,994m uplift How to read. Each floating bar contributes to the change in annual NII. Rates add 5,190 and volume adds 804, producing a total increase of 5,994. These are reported accounting decompositions. DBS · FY2023 performance summary OCBC · FY2023 financial highlights UOB · FY2023 financial statements Exhibit 07 · FY2025 versus FY2024 · S$m Volume softened a S$2,327m rate headwind How to read. The rate effect is −2,327, volume adds 1,572 and calendar effects subtract 93, leaving an 848 decline. Calendar effects reflect the comparison with leap-year 2024. DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2025 financial statements The underlying bank-by-bank calculations FY2023 change, S$m Rates Volume Net change DBS +2,482 +219 +2,701 OCBC +1,553 +404 +1,957 UOB +1,155 +181 +1,336 Total +5,190 +804 +5,994 FY2025 change, S$m Rates Volume Calendar Net DBS −579 +695 −40 +76 OCBC −1,236 +658 −27 −605 UOB −512 +219 −26 −319 Total −2,327 +1,572 −93 −848 Scope and arithmetic. Combined NII rose from S$26,972m to S$32,966m in 2023. It fell from S$33,853m to S$33,005m in 2025. Rate and volume allocation conventions can differ between banks. The sum retains each issuer’s own attribution and cannot isolate the effect of SGS yields or quantify the share of total profit caused by rates. DBS · FY2023 performance summary DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2023 financial highlights OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2023 financial statements UOB · FY2025 financial statements The dependence is visible even after allowing for balance-sheet growth. The margin cycle added billions of dollars of annual income on the upswing. In the later phase, growing balance sheets absorbed much of the rate pressure. In plain English The banks tell us that changing rates did most of the work in the 2023 increase in net interest income. When the rate effect reversed, they had to put more assets to work to defend those earnings. 05 / How the yield move reaches NIM Follow both the money lent and the money borrowed SGS and T-bill yields influence bank economics through several channels. The asset side can earn a higher rate while the funding side becomes more expensive. Reset dates, customer behaviour and hedges determine the net effect. Exhibit 08 · rate transmission map One market move reaches several parts of the balance sheet Floating-rate loans Compounded SORA or another contractual benchmark resets → asset yield changes after the loan’s reset lag. Deposits and wholesale funding T-bills and competing offers change the return customers demand → funding cost and the deposit mix change. Fixed-rate loans and securities New lending and reinvestment occur at new yields → the asset yield adjusts as old positions mature or reset. Hedges and currencies Swaps alter effective fixed/floating exposure → SGD, USD and other rate moves can have different effects. Asset interest − funding interest = NII Divide by average earning assets to calculate NIM. Mechanism schematic. SORA and sovereign yields affect different contracts and investments. Timing is bank-specific. MAS · SORA benchmark DBS · FY2025 CFO statement UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights (public filing mirror) OCBC · 3Q26 results highlights Deposit beta and funding mix The cost of deposits catches up with market rates Deposit beta describes how much of a benchmark-rate change passes into the deposit rate. Customers can also shift from current and savings accounts into higher-paying fixed deposits. That mix shift raises the average cost even if each product’s own rate is unchanged. Low-cost deposits create an advantage until their price or mix changes. CASA means current-account and savings-account deposits. Their stability depends on transaction needs, competing offers and customer behaviour. On the way down, a deposit already paying little interest has limited room to fall. What to inspect. Average deposit cost, CASA share, fixed-deposit maturities, and funding growth alongside average loan and securities yields. DBS · FY2025 CFO statement DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2025 financial statements Exhibit 09 · average rates · FY2024 → FY2025 Asset yields fell faster than deposit costs Reported rate DBS OCBC UOB Asset yield 4.56 → 3.92% 5.06 → 4.19% 4.88 → 4.18% Asset-yield change −64bp −87bp −70bp Deposit cost 2.25 → 1.67% 2.84 → 2.27% 2.81 → 2.23% Deposit-cost change −58bp −57bp −58bp Group NIM 2.13 → 2.01% 2.20 → 1.91% 2.03 → 1.89% How to read. Each cell compares full-year reported averages. Asset yields and deposit costs have different balance denominators. Their difference does not mechanically equal NIM. The table shows why the speed of repricing matters. DBS · FY2025 performance summary OCBC · FY2025 financial highlights UOB · FY2025 financial statements A direct T-bill example · DBS FY2025 Maturing T-bills helped bring deposits back DBS reported retail funds returning from maturing T-bills as rates fell. Deposits increased S$64bn, or 12% on a constant-currency basis, to S$610bn. More than two-thirds of the increase came from CASA. T-bills mature Cash returns → Deposits grow Funding expands → HQLA added NII rises Deploying surplus deposits into high-quality liquid assets lowered the average margin while increasing income. DBS said HQLA grew S$42bn to S$208bn. These assets earned a thinner spread than some loans but still added NII and ROE. This explains why the margin percentage alone can miss an improvement in earnings. DBS · FY2025 CFO statement Singapore rates also reflect the currency framework MAS conducts monetary policy through the Singapore dollar exchange-rate path. With open capital markets, domestic rates are strongly influenced by global rates and expectations for the SGD. A US rate change can therefore transmit to Singapore without matching it point for point. Local liquidity and funding demand add another layer. MAS · monetary-policy framework In plain English For a bank, the timing gap matters. Loan income may rise before deposit costs, or funding may become expensive before the loan book catches up. The same yield direction can produce different quarterly margins. 06 / The latest quarter Funding costs weighed on UOB’s margin UOB’s group NIM fell 6bp between 2Q26 and 3Q26, from 1.74% to 1.68%. Its public performance highlights attribute the decline to higher funding costs. Loan growth helped offset the effect on net interest income. Exhibit 10 · UOB quarterly margin · % Margin narrowed while NII remained broadly stable Reported group measure 2Q26 3Q26 NIM 1.74% 1.68% NII, S$m 2,297 2,278 How to read. NIM fell by 6 basis points. UOB reported that 3% loan growth offset pressure from higher funding costs, leaving NII broadly stable. This panel uses the public performance release rather than a component-by-component presentation bridge. UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights (public filing mirror) Peer checks · 3Q26 Each group absorbed a different mix of rate effects OCBC benefited from higher SORA in its SGD business. It said SGD asset yields rose faster than funding costs. In USD, funding repriced ahead of assets. Group NIM fell from 1.70% to 1.66%, yet NII rose from S$2,264m to S$2,313m as average earning assets expanded. DBS’s group margin stabilised while its commercial-book margin declined. Group NIM stayed at 1.87%, while the commercial-book measure fell from 2.21% to 2.16%. Group NII increased from S$3,581m to S$3,711m. Management reported a 1.90% exit margin. That difference in scope matters when reading a chart. Comparing DBS’s commercial-book NIM with the other banks’ group NIM would overstate the margin gap. The historical charts in this report use group figures throughout. OCBC · 3Q26 results highlights DBS · 3Q26 CFO slides DBS · 3Q26 CEO slides Exhibit 11 · seven-quarter group margin history The recent squeeze is visible across the three banks DBS OCBC UOB Quarterly NIM and NII at source precision NIM, annualised DBS OCBC UOB 1Q25 2.12% 2.04% 2.00% 2Q25 2.05% 1.92% 1.91% 3Q25 1.96% 1.84% 1.82% 4Q25 1.93% 1.86% 1.84% 1Q26 1.89% 1.76% 1.82% 2Q26 1.87% 1.70% 1.74% 3Q26 1.87% 1.66% 1.68% NII, S$m DBS OCBC UOB 1Q25 3,681 2,345 2,409 2Q25 3,648 2,283 2,336 3Q25 3,578 2,226 2,265 4Q25 3,593 2,296 2,346 1Q26 3,494 2,222 2,324 2Q26 3,581 2,264 2,297 3Q26 3,711 2,313 2,278 How to read. All values are quarterly group NIM, annualised. DBS’s 1.90% exit margin is a point-in-time observation and is discussed separately from the 1.87% full-quarter average. The chart shows realised outcomes through 30 September 2026. DBS · 3Q26 CFO slides OCBC · 3Q26 results highlights UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights (public filing mirror) In plain English A higher yield today can improve future loan returns while hurting this quarter through faster funding repricing. Read the reported asset and funding outcomes before assuming an earnings benefit. 07 / Hedges & interest-rate risk The sign of the rate exposure can change Banks manage their exposure using asset mix, deposit behaviour and derivatives. A bank can remain highly dependent on NII even after reducing, delaying or reversing its sensitivity to a particular market rate. DBS management sensitivity · reported 5 Nov 2026 Singapore and US rates had opposite reported sensitivities +S$10m/bp Singapore interest rates −S$2m/bp US interest rates DBS’s 3Q26 CEO slide reports positive NII sensitivity to Singapore rates and negative sensitivity to US rates. Those coefficients apply to its prevailing positioning. The slide states S$m per basis point without specifying a separate shock horizon. Hedging has changed the exposure over time. At end-2025, DBS reported S$210bn of fixed-rate assets, including fixed mortgages, swaps and securities. Its reported USD sensitivity then was −S$4m/bp. The 2026 coefficient belongs to a different date and balance sheet. DBS · 3Q26 CEO slides DBS · FY2025 CFO statement Exhibit 12 · regulatory scenarios · 31 Dec 2025 A downward shock affects OCBC and UOB differently One-year NII effect, S$m OCBC UOB Supervisory parallel down −1,951 +1,457 Supervisory parallel up —¹ −923 These are currency-specific prescribed shock scenarios on each bank’s modelled balance sheet. They incorporate different exposures, hedges and customer-behaviour assumptions. UOB’s disclosure demonstrates that a higher rate can reduce modelled NII for some balance sheets. How to read. Read each number as a one-year NII change under that bank’s published supervisory scenario. They are not uniform 100bp shocks or management earnings forecasts. ¹OCBC’s cited table presents the disclosed adverse NII scenario. Different model conventions and business mixes limit direct ranking. OCBC · Annual Report 2025 UOB · Annual Report 2025 A bond valuation loss and NII pressure measure different things Higher long-term yields can lower the market value of existing fixed-rate assets while improving the rate available on reinvestment. Fair-value classifications determine whether marks appear in profit or other comprehensive income. Interest on amortised-cost assets follows effective-interest accounting. OCBC separately reported a S$1,062m adverse economic-value-of-equity effect under its FY2025 parallel-up scenario. It associated higher EVE sensitivity with increased fixed-rate bond holdings. Its NII downside test ran in the opposite direction. Combining these two amounts would mix different scenarios and economic measures. OCBC · Annual Report 2025 In plain English NIM dependence describes how the bank earns. Rate sensitivity describes what a particular rate move does to that earning engine after its funding and hedges are considered. 08 / Valuation & monitoring Treat the interest margin as a cyclical earnings input The earnings case for a bank share should state what margin it assumes and why that margin is sustainable. A premium valuation needs more support when the past improvement in return on equity depended heavily on a favourable rate cycle. Exhibit 13 · the earnings-to-valuation link NIM changes Spread earned → NII changes Interest dollars → Earnings / ROE Valuation input Costs, provisions, fee income and capital determine the final outcome. Wealth-management growth can provide a valuable offset. Asset growth can stabilise NII. Credit losses can erase the gain from a wider margin. Sustainable earnings therefore require more than a yield-chart direction. Interpretive mechanism. The first report covers the price-to-book comparison and bank concentration in the STI. Part 1 · The STI’s bank premium DBS · 3Q26 trading update OCBC · 3Q26 results release UOB · 3Q26 performance highlights The six checks I would use before relying on a margin recovery Check Evidence to look for Meaning Short rates SORA and 6M/1Y T-bill yields, with dates Loan-reset environment and competition for cash Asset repricing Loan and securities yields, average earning assets How quickly new rates enter income Funding repricing Deposit cost, CASA, term-deposit renewals How much of the rate move is paid away Hedges and currency Current sensitivity, fixed-rate assets, SGD/USD split Whether the group benefits from that move Core earnings NII alongside fees, expenses and provisions Whether the margin benefit reaches profit Valuation Expected ROE and payout against price paid How much recovery is already assumed My preference remains to use strength to reduce an oversized bank allocation when valuation assumes an easy earnings recovery. A durable improvement in the reported margin, supported by funding costs and credit quality, would weaken that cautious view. Part 1 · The STI’s bank premium In plain English Bank dividends come from an earnings engine exposed to the rate cycle. Follow the spread the bank actually earns, the size of its asset base and the price paid for that profit. 09 / Sources, definitions & reproducibility Every chart carries its data period and source This addendum uses the three banks’ reported group financial data. Full-year NIM covers 2015–2025, and quarterly NIM runs through 3Q26. Historical and current market observations retain their separate dates and frequency definitions. Reading the source boundaries Embedded Hub history. The chart reuses the supplied workbook series through Aug 2026. It retains gaps. Monthly averaging and the original download date remain unverified. The latest official MAS daily observation is shown in its own panel. Annual versus quarterly data. Full-year NIM and annualised quarterly NIM use separate charts. A published quarter-end or exit margin is a different observation again. Rates and volume. Aggregates sum issuer decompositions in S$m. Cross-effect allocation conventions can differ, and the rate component includes multiple currencies, asset pricing and funding pricing. Changing business scope. Acquisitions, geography and asset mix evolve over the sample. OCBC includes insurance. Long-run total-income accounting presentations also changed, so historical charts focus on group NIM and NII. Rounding. Calculations retain reported source precision. Displays use two decimals for rates and percentages. Individual rounded quarters can differ from reported annual or year-to-date sums by S$1m. entries.text: Singapore local banks V2 · MAS, NIM and 2027 outlook · 9 Nov 2026 ← Research Explained · Market Intelligence Hub Skip to report Market Intelligence Hub V2 updated / Singapore local banks SGX banks · V2 updated 9 November 2026 Singapore banks: earnings held, valuations cracked The Q3 results were not a collapse in net interest income. They were a test of deposit costs, margin durability and the premium investors will pay for cyclical bank earnings. The sell-off and the balance sheet have to be read together. Research checked through 2026-11-09T18:53:00+08:00 (SGT), with MAS latest independently confirmed close 6 Nov 2026. Independent research · updated 9 November 2026 (Singapore time) Bank results through 3Q26 · Share prices 6 Nov 2026 close · last verified MAS SGS closing data 6 Nov · Commentary 7–8 Nov Singapore · region DBS / D05 · company OCBC / O39 · company UOB / U11 · company Financials / banking · sector Equities · asset SGS · instrument MAS · institution SORA / interest rates Valuation risk · analysis Versioning rule. V2 is a new standalone report. The original STI banks study (6 Nov) and the SGS, T-bills & NIM addendum (6 Nov) remain separate and unchanged. Its full historical charts, 2015–2025 NIM, rate/volume attribution and technical explanations are also retained below, after the new V2 chapters. Bank filing means directly reported; Market interpretation means reasoned analysis or a columnist’s hypothesis; Derived means a shown calculation. The opinion and actual issuer financial results are not interchangeable. S$8.302bn Combined 3Q26 NII 16th consecutive quarter above S$8bn, per SGX 64.06% Interest income share 3Q26 NII ÷ combined total income −15.7% Largest one-month bank decline UOB · BT's 7 Oct–6 Nov comparison window The four findings to carry forward Bank earnings are highly spread-dependent, but NIM is not the same as net interest income. Every bank's 3Q26 NIM fell YoY; higher asset volumes still lifted their NII YoY. The wider share-price decline cannot be explained by one quarter's NIM. All three fell sharply before or around reporting; weaker global risk appetite and higher discount rates are plausible contributing explanations, not proved causes. UOB is cheapest on price-to-book, but earns the lowest contemporaneous ROE. A smaller multiple is not automatically a bargain; sustainable ROE, asset quality and funding structure decide whether it deserves a discount. The rate cycle cuts both ways. Short rates change lending and deposit margins; longer SGS yields reprice investment securities and insurer portfolios. Previous 11-year NIM and SGS charts remain below for context. V2 · Share sell-off V2 · Q3 scorecard V2 · Four takeaways V2 · Valuation V2 · MAS verified V2 · Hub yield history V2 · Strategy & scenario Original · NIM Original · 11-year NIM Original · Rate attribution Original · Transmission Original · 3Q bridge Original · Hedges Original · Watchlist Original sources V2 sources V2 · 01 / What the market actually repriced Two sell-offs, one question: earnings or valuation? Market pricing turned before the full Q3 scorecards arrived. The Business Times' 8 November column highlights an October repricing after a bearish Citi call and a second sell-off around 3Q26 results. That sequence is consistent with both company-specific disappointment and a broader sector de-rating. Exhibit V2.01 · Equity drawdown · BT-reported window 7 October to 6 November 2026 DBS −11.3% OCBC −13.9% UOB −15.7% Window: The Business Times comparison beginning 7 Oct. Negative percentages are share-price declines, not dividend-adjusted returns. BT, 8 Nov 2026 · supplied PDF Exhibit V2.02 · Earnings-report week Week ended 6 November DBS −4.7% OCBC −5.3% UOB −10.9% Benchmark: STI fell 3.7% over the same week; the bank declines differ markedly. BT, 8 Nov 2026 Company Report week Since 7 Oct (BT) YTD to 6 Nov (BT) Headline 3Q26 profit What matters DBS · D05 −4.7% −11.3% +23.7% −5% YoY Markets trading weak; NII up OCBC · O39 −5.3% −13.9% +40.3% +3% YoY Banking record; GEH mark-to-market drag UOB · U11 −10.9% −15.7% +5.2% +182% YoY* Margin guidance disappointment; easy prior-year base Evidence What the filings can verify DBS, OCBC and UOB reported different underlying drivers of profit. Across the three, combined 3Q26 NII was S$8.302bn , yet overall non-interest income weakened quarter on quarter. The banks' Q3 filings and SGX's 6 November study document the split. Crucially, all three bank NIMs were lower year on year. The headline profit figures alone hide the effect of trading, insurance and provisions. Interpretation, not measured attribution Why the broader de-rating thesis is plausible BT cited the Nasdaq 100 falling 13.6% from 7 October and 4.9% during the report week. It discussed bond yields, funding costs and wider technology weakness as contemporaneous risk-off forces. Correlation does not establish causation. These cross-market movements do not measure how much of the SG bank fall came from rates versus earnings, flows or valuation multiples. Investor distinction. A market-wide decline can create an entry point, but a sector-wide higher required return can also make the previous P/B premium permanently less defensible. Buying merely because prices fell is not a valuation method. Reference period: 6 November 2026 data cutoff; historic points as noted Units: Share-price changes in %; NIM and profit in reported units Coverage: DBS, OCBC and UOB / STI Read: start with the dated values and legend, then compare direction and the stated units. Limit: Company moves cannot be assigned solely to earnings or yields. Source / verification V2 · 02 / Reported bank financials All three margins narrowed YoY. None suffered an NII collapse. The numerator and denominator matter. NIM is a percentage spread over earning assets. NII is the number of dollars earned from that spread across the whole earning-asset base. Asset growth and hedging allowed NII to keep rising despite lower average margins. DBS SGX:D05 1.87% 3Q26 group NIM · -9bp YoY · +0bp QoQ S$3,711m NII · +4% YoY 16.0% ROE (quarter annualised) · 0.9% NPL NII rose 4% YoY, while markets trading fell 65% YoY. Management reported a 1.90% exit NIM, higher than its 1.87% quarterly average. OCBC SGX:O39 1.66% 3Q26 group NIM · -18bp YoY · -4bp QoQ S$2,313m NII · +4% YoY 13.1% ROE (quarter annualised) · 0.8% NPL NII rose 4% YoY despite an 18bp NIM reduction. Banking operations earned record quarterly profit; Great Eastern investment valuation losses weighed on group results. UOB SGX:U11 1.68% 3Q26 group NIM · -14bp YoY · -6bp QoQ S$2,278m NII · +1% YoY 10.1% ROE (quarter annualised) · 1.5% NPL Funding costs and asset repricing squeezed margin. The +182% reported profit growth comes against 3Q25 net profit of just S$443m, when allowances were elevated. Exhibit V2.03 · Q3 2026 earnings and rate dependence Annualised NIM, net interest dollars and reported profit Group NIM 3Q25 NIM 3Q26 YoY Δ QoQ Δ 3Q26 NII NII YoY Net profit Net profit YoY DBS 1.96% 1.87% -9bp +0bp S$3,711m +4% S$2,813m −5% OCBC 1.84% 1.66% -18bp -4bp S$2,313m +4% S$2,042m +3% UOB 1.82% 1.68% -14bp -6bp S$2,278m +1% S$1,250m +182%* Reported issuer data. Δ in basis points (bp), not percentage change. *UOB profit comparison reflects a depressed 3Q25 base: Q3 2025 net profit S$443m and S$1,361m allowances; Q3 2026 profit S$1,250m and allowances S$258m. Net profit movement must not be interpreted as a 182% underlying NIM increase. Exhibit V2.04 · Q3 yoy margin comparison Source NIM: 3Q25 → 3Q26 3Q25 3Q26 DBS 1.96% DBS 1.87% OCBC 1.84% OCBC 1.66% UOB 1.82% UOB 1.68% Scroll sideways for the full chart. Keyboard: focus the chart, then use Left and Right arrows. DBS, solid OCBC, dashed UOB, dotted All bank entities share the Singapore Jade colour, as prescribed by the current master tag standard. Direct labels and line patterns distinguish them. Vertical geometry illustrates ordering and change; exact values are labelled. Exhibit V2.05 · Reported quarter-on-quarter NIM bridge Deposit funding can absorb higher asset yields Component, bp OCBC UOB 2Q26 NIM 1.70% 1.74% Asset/loan repricing +3 −1 Treasury yield +3 Not separately disclosed Funding cost −11 −7 Volume / mix +2 +2 3Q26 NIM, reported 1.66% 1.68% Bank CFO presentations: OCBC 6 Nov, p.8; UOB 4 Nov, p.8. OCBC published bridge amounts are rounded individually and sum to 1.67%, versus a reported 1.66% closing NIM. Do not force a false exact reconciliation. DBS · Management outlook Hedging and volume cushion the spread 3Q26 group NIM was 1.87% (flat QoQ), while NII rose 4% QoQ . The reported quarter-end exit NIM was 1.90% . Management described the 2027 NII path as supported by loan/deposit growth and hedging opportunities. Check: The 1.90% exit margin is not the same statistic as a quarterly average of 1.87%. OCBC and UOB · Different transmission Rising rates do not guarantee a wider NIM OCBC said higher Singapore-dollar SORA supported 3Q income, but rising US rates initially hurt its US dollar funding spread. UOB's funding cost effect was −7bp QoQ while the average 3-month SORA increased in the quarter. Check: Currency, deposit mix, loans resets and asset duration are more informative than the direction of an SGS yield alone. Reference period: 6 November 2026 data cutoff; historic points as noted Units: NIM %; NII S$m; ROE %; bridge basis points Coverage: DBS, OCBC and UOB quarterly results Read: start with the dated values and legend, then compare direction and the stated units. Limit: Bank NIM and NII are not interchangeable. Source / verification V2 update · 07 / 9 Nov reading of 7 Nov Business Times coverage The next question is not just NIM. It is where the growth comes from. The four new themes are 2027 earnings, selective AI-related financing, Indonesia exposure, and wealth fees. All remain relevant to how much of today’s bank earnings deserves a long-term premium. This section interprets the Business Times article dated 7 November 2026 , and separates commentary-reported management figures from directly verified Q3 filings. 01 · 2027 outlook NII ≠ NIM DBS: management targets mid-single-digit total income growth in 2027, with loans and deposit growth contributing; its 2027 sensitivities are +S$10m per bp of Singapore rates and −S$2m per bp of US rates. UOB: expects 2027 NII above 2026, supported by balance-sheet growth. OCBC: published upgraded 2026 guidance, not a quantitative 2027 target. Source: DBS CEO slide 3; UOB CFO slide 17; OCBC CEO slide 3. NII and total income are different measures. 02 · AI financing discipline Selective Business Times reports DBS S$14.6bn of data-centre exposure and S$8.98bn outstanding, or around 2% of loans. OCBC reports AI-related financing below 1% of its loan book and data-centre exposure around 3%. UOB reports AI-related financing below 5% of loans. Exposure definitions vary: commitment, outstanding loan and AI-related financing are not interchangeable. Figures are management remarks as reported by BT, not separately audited exposure tables here. 03 · Indonesia exposure FX matters BT reports DBS Indonesia franchise down about 9% in 2026, largely reflecting the rupiah’s depreciation against SGD. OCBC’s Indonesia loan growth was about 10% in local terms but around 5% in SGD terms; Indonesia represented around 5% of OCBC operating income. UOB attributed below 3% of group loans and profit to Indonesia. BT-reported management commentary. Country contribution, FX translation and credit quality are distinct tests. 04 · Wealth management is the earnings counterweight DBS: S$864m 3Q wealth fees OCBC: S$442m 3Q wealth fees UOB: S$733m total net fees Wealth fees are real, but they are not immune to volatility. DBS reported S$864m wealth fees (around +9% YoY at issuer rounding). OCBC reported S$442m net wealth fees and S$480m of customer-flow trading income. UOB reported S$733m total net fees, up 19% YoY. The business can offset some interest-margin drag, not erase it. Definition alert: BT cited S$258m for UOB wealth-management fees. UOB’s CFO presentation shows S$299m of gross wealth fees on a waterfall explicitly gross of expenses. The S$258m figure has not been reconciled to the issuer’s gross-fee figure; do not assume that expenses explain the difference or compare them as identical measures. Source reconciliation before using the numbers OCBC profit correction: the 7 Nov BT article describes OCBC 3Q profit as S$2.22bn . OCBC’s 6 Nov official financial release reports S$2,042m . That is the figure used throughout this report. DBS wealth growth: BT states 8%; the issuer shows +9% YoY (S$864m versus S$796m) on rounded presentation. The ratio calculated from the published S$864m and S$796m figures is 8.54%, which rounds to 9%. BT’s 8% figure is not reconciled here. Source hierarchy: financial statements and issuer slide decks govern reported numbers; Business Times is separately attributed for management comments and market interpretation; analytical scenarios are labelled as calculations. Investment implication. The expansion narrative matters only if stronger wealth fees, careful AI underwriting and regional growth can sustain ROE after rates, deposit costs and credit losses normalise. Paying an aggressive P/B for a cyclical spread is still a valuation risk. OCBC · Annual Report 2025 UOB · Annual Report 2025 A bond valuation loss and NII pressure measure different things Higher long-term yields can lower the market value of existing fixed-rate assets while improving the rate available on reinvestment. Fair-value classifications determine whether marks appear in profit or other comprehensive income. Interest on amortised-cost assets follows effective-interest accounting. OCBC separately reported a S$1,062m adverse economic-value-of-equity effect under its FY2025 parallel-up scenario. It associated higher EVE sensitivity with increased fixed-rate bond holdings. Its NII downside test ran in the opposite direction. Combining these two amounts would mix different scenarios and economic measures. OCBC · Annual Report 2025 In plain English NIM dependence describes how the bank earns. Rate sensitivity describes what a particular rate move does to that earning engine after its funding and hedges are considered. A premium valuation needs more support when the past improvement in return on equity depended heavily on a favourable rate cycle. Exhibit 13 · the earnings-to-valuation link NIM changes Spread earned → NII changes Interest dollars → Earnings / ROE Valuation input Costs, provisions, fee income and capital determine the final outcome. Wealth-management growth can provide a valuable offset. Asset growth can stabilise NII. Credit losses can erase the gain from a wider margin. Sustainable earnings therefore require more than a yield-chart direction. Interpretive mechanism. The first report covers the price-to-book comparison and bank concentration in the STI. A durable improvement in the reported margin, supported by funding costs and credit quality, would weaken that cautious view. entries.text: TSM deep dive | Market Intel Research Explained Skip to research ← Research Explained • Market Intel • NVIDIA deep dive Company research · public edition · 5 November 2026 Issuer facts, dated analyst views and independent assumptions are separated throughout. Price reference: 4 November 2026 US close, not a live quote. 01 Overview 02 Business model 03 Financial history 04 Latest quarter 05 Cash and capital 06 Morningstar lens 07 Valuation scenarios 08 Risks 09 Review plan 10 Sources TSM | US LISTED ADR | 5 NOVEMBER 2026 Taiwan Semiconductor deep dive A strong manufacturing franchise with rising AI concentration. TSMC gives exposure to advanced chip production across competing designers. The case is attractive if leading-edge demand and pricing continue to offset factory spending, start-up costs and geopolitical risk. This report separates company facts, Morningstar views and independent scenario analysis. Overview data Reference price Evidence foundation Research conclusion US$395.75 4 Nov 2026 close [13,14] Company filings and dated publisher links Worth further consideration Price and cash returns matter Five takeaways 1. TSMC benefits from several AI chip architectures. Manufacturing leadership can capture spending even when the winning designer changes. It does not eliminate the risk that total AI investment disappoints. 2. Diversification is narrower than the customer count suggests. HPC reached 68% of Q3 revenue; the ten largest customers generated 78% of FY2025 revenue. [3,7] 3. Cash generation is strong, but reinvestment is substantial. Nine-month operating cash flow of NT$2,402.1bn less NT$1,290.0bn cash capex leaves NT$1,112.1bn FCF. [2; calculation] 4. Analyst research is a comparison tool, not a guarantee. Read dated publisher research alongside issuer filings and visible scenario assumptions. This public edition links to Morningstar instead of republishing its valuation estimates or ratings. [10,11] 5. A lower share price does not remove business risk. N2 execution, overseas-fab margins and customer spending must support the earnings assumed in any valuation. TSM fell 10.0% from 28 Oct to 4 Nov. How to read: consecutive trading-session closes; USD/ADR; line axis is 380-455, not zero. Sources [13,14], retrieved 5 Nov 2026. Price changes exclude dividends; no cause is assigned to this move. Educational company research. This is not personalised investment advice or a trade recommendation. Past closing prices are not executable quotes. Exact values: historical closing prices Exact values: historical closing prices US trading date, 2026 USD per ADR 28 Oct 439.51 29 Oct 431.81 30 Oct 406.13 2 Nov 398.63 3 Nov 404.80 4 Nov 395.75 01 BUSINESS AND REVENUE EXPOSURE How TSMC makes money Customers design chips; TSMC manufactures them. The pure-play foundry model earns revenue by turning customers' designs into physical semiconductors rather than marketing a competing branded chip. Process know-how, yield, scale and trusted execution are central to the proposition. [6] Business model data Layer Role in plain language Economic question Chip design Decide what the chip does Will the customer's product win? Wafer fabrication Build transistors and circuits on wafers Can TSMC deliver high yield at scale? Advanced packaging Connect chips and memory into a working system Can capacity and performance meet demand? Customer systems Install chips in phones, servers and other products Will end users justify further spending? Takeaway: HPC dominates revenue while leading-edge nodes dominate wafer sales. How to read: separate denominators; Q3 2026 percentages. Older nodes = 100% - 79%. Source [3], 15 Oct 2026. HPC includes more than AI; it must not be relabelled as pure AI revenue. Winning across designers is different from diversified end demand. A shift from GPUs toward custom accelerators can still support foundry demand, but only if those designs use TSMC and total silicon spending holds up. Different customers can depend on the same hyperscaler budgets. This is an analytical inference, not disclosed customer-level revenue. The latest mix raises the importance of AI-related returns. Smartphones remain material at 21%; IoT and automotive are 4% each. Those businesses are useful breadth, but together they are not large enough to offset every plausible HPC downturn. [3; analysis] Concentration check: FY2025 top ten customers 78%, largest 19%, second largest 17%. The filing does not identify them in this table. Do not assign those percentages to named customers without separate evidence. [7] Exact values: Q3 revenue exposure Exact values: Q3 revenue exposure Platform / node Revenue basis Share HPC Net revenue 68% Smartphone Net revenue 21% IoT Net revenue 4% Automotive Net revenue 4% DCE Net revenue 1% Other Net revenue 2% 2nm Wafer revenue 8% 3nm Wafer revenue 33% 5nm Wafer revenue 28% 7nm Wafer revenue 10% Older nodes Wafer revenue 21% 02 FINANCIAL HISTORY The AI upturn followed a real downcycle Takeaway: revenue recovered from the 2023 contraction and accelerated through 2025. How to read: annual revenue and net income attributable to parent, US$bn; all bars start at zero. Sources [6,8]. 2026 is excluded because the full year is not yet reported. Financial history data Metric 2022 2023 2024 2025 Revenue US$bn 75.88 69.30 90.08 122.42 Net income US$bn 34.07 26.88 36.52 55.21 Gross margin 59.6% 54.4% 56.1% 59.9% Operating margin 49.5% 42.6% 45.7% 50.8% Diluted EPS NT$/ordinary 39.20 32.34 45.25 66.26 Sources [6,8,9]. FY2025 EPS uses the later annual report, not the preliminary presentation's NT$66.25. US$ income translations use the company's annual conventions and should not be recomputed with one current exchange rate. Revenue growth alone is an incomplete test of quality. From 2022 to 2025, US-dollar revenue rose about 61%, but 2023 revenue fell 8.7% and net income fell about 21%. The history shows both structural growth and cyclicality. [6,8; calculations] The recovery improved profitability as well as scale. Annual operating margin rose from 42.6% in 2023 to 50.8% in 2025. Maintaining that improvement requires utilization, yield and price to absorb depreciation and overseas costs. The next cycle may not resemble the last one. [6,8; analysis] An investor should distinguish three kinds of growth More wafers: higher physical volume. Better mix: more advanced, higher-value products. Pricing: more revenue per comparable service. A blended revenue-per-wafer figure mixes these effects; it is not a clean price index. This report does not label that ratio as pricing power. 03 LATEST QUARTER Strong growth with a sequential margin decline Latest quarter data Metric Q3 2025 Q2 2026 Q3 2026 Revenue US$bn 33.10 40.20 46.72 Revenue NT$bn 989.92 1,270.38 1,494.24 Gross margin 59.5% 67.7% 66.4% Operating margin 50.6% 60.3% 58.7% Net income to parent NT$bn 452.30 706.56 763.06 Diluted EPS US$/ADR 2.92 4.31 4.60 Diluted EPS NT$/ordinary 17.44 27.25 29.43 Sources [1-4]; unaudited; quarter ended 30 Sep 2026. US-dollar revenue grew 41.2% year over year, versus 50.9% in NT dollars. The exchange-rate basis changes the growth figure. Takeaway: margins are far above Q3 2025 but below Q2 2026. How to read: percentage of revenue, line axis 45%-72%; dots and squares distinguish series. Sources [3,4], 15 Oct 2026. A percentage-point change is not the same as a percentage growth rate. Q2 had benefits that should not be assumed to recur. The management report attributes the fall in non-operating gains mainly to absent disposal and mark-to-market gains on Vanguard shares. Q2 also benefited from earthquake insurance claims in other operating income. Net income and operating margin therefore need context beyond revenue growth. [3] What management expects next Q4 revenue guidance is US$52.3bn-US$54.3bn , with gross margin 65%-67% and operating margin 56.5%-58.5%, assuming NT$31.8/US$. The revenue midpoint is 14.1% above Q3. Guidance is an expectation, not a reported result. [1,4; calculation] Management's full-year US-dollar revenue growth outlook is around 44%. Separately, adding the Q4 midpoint to reported nine-month US-dollar revenue gives roughly US$176.1bn. Translation and rounding mean these are not identical calculations. [2,4] 04 CASH AND CAPITAL Factories are profitable but expensive to expand Takeaway: quarterly FCF remained positive and rose in Q3. How to read: operating cash flow less cash capex, NT$bn; zero-based bars. Source [3], 15 Oct 2026. This measure excludes acquisitions and does not treat all investing inflows as operating cash. Cash and capital data Nine months ended 30 Sep 2026 NT$bn Interpretation Operating cash flow 2,402.117 Cash generated by operations Cash purchases of property and equipment 1,289.971 Cash capex deducted here Calculated free cash flow 1,112.146 28.5% of revenue Common cash dividends paid 440.853 39.6% of calculated FCF Source [2]; calculations. FCF is not net income and excludes other investing/financing flows. Nine-month FCF/net income to parent is about 54.5%. Compare matching periods and definitions. Liquidity provides resilience, not free money. At 30 September, company-reported cash and marketable securities were NT$4,016.98bn against NT$1,031.58bn interest-bearing debt, leaving NT$2,985.40bn company-defined net cash. Committed expansion and working capital still consume resources. [3] The spending ramp is a core valuation assumption. Management kept 2026 capex at US$60bn-US$64bn and expects 2026-2028 investment to exceed the prior three years significantly. It expects overseas fabs to dilute gross margin by about two percentage points in 2026 and three to four points over the next few years. These are management forecasts. [5] Watch the cash after the build, not just the size of the build. A new fab can depress near-term cash and margins before earning returns. The crucial test is whether later output, pricing and utilization repay the investment at an attractive rate. Large capex is neither automatically good nor automatically bad. Exact values: quarterly free cash flow Exact values: quarterly free cash flow Quarter NT$ billions Q4 2025 368.60 Q1 2026 348.21 Q2 2026 287.36 Q3 2026 476.56 05 MORNINGSTAR READING FRAMEWORK How to use Morningstar alongside the filings Independent analyst research can test a thesis, but it does not replace the underlying evidence. The linked Morningstar public articles are useful reading alongside TSMC’s company results. This public edition does not republish Morningstar’s fair-value figures, rating values, proprietary forecasts or charts derived from those estimates. [10-12] Morningstar lens data Research concept Question to ask How to avoid misreading it Fair value What future cash generation and discount rate support the estimate? An intrinsic-value estimate is not an executable price or guaranteed target. Economic moat Why might the business sustain competitive returns? A strong franchise can still be bought at an unattractive price. Uncertainty How wide is the range of plausible business outcomes? A model label is not a promise of low daily share-price volatility. Capital allocation Will reinvestment, financing and distributions create value? Higher spending does not automatically imply higher shareholder returns. Star rating How do price, estimated value and uncertainty interact on the stated date? Do not infer a current rating from an older article or a separate valuation model. A practical reading sequence Start with the issuer, then challenge the assumptions. Establish reported revenue, profit, cash flow and capital expenditure first. Next ask which elements of the analyst thesis depend on future demand, capacity utilisation, pricing or new manufacturing processes. Finally compare those assumptions with the explicit independent scenarios in this report. Keep dates and methods separate. The Morningstar technology article was published on 8 September 2026 with data dated 3 September. The linked earnings article is dated 16 October 2026. The historical capital-allocation discussion is dated 5 March 2025. These are different observations, not a single current research snapshot. [10-12] The independent scenarios below are not Morningstar forecasts. Their revenue, net-margin and multiple assumptions are shown so a reader can change them. They do not reproduce the publisher’s complete valuation model or claim a current rating. Publisher access Read the original pages through the dated links in the source register. Access may depend on location or subscription. No subscriber report, publisher screenshot, rating table or analyst-derived valuation chart is reproduced in this public edition. 06 TRANSPARENT VALUATION Three scenarios show what the price requires These are independent illustrations for calendar 2027, not Morningstar forecasts. EPS = assumed revenue x assumed net margin / 5.1864bn ADR-equivalent shares. Value = EPS x assumed P/E. The share base equals 25.932bn ordinary shares divided by five, held constant for the model. [2; assumptions] Valuation scenarios data Scenario Revenue Net margin EPS / ADR P/E Value Price return Bear $190bn 42% $15.39 20x $308 -22.2% Base $220bn 49% $20.79 24x $499 +26.1% Bull $250bn 52% $25.07 28x $702 +77.3% Takeaway: a broad outcome range remains despite the same manufacturing franchise. How to read: zero-based bars, US$/ADR; dashed line = 4 November close. All bars are independent calendar-2027 scenarios, not analyst forecasts. No probabilities assigned. Sources [2,13] plus stated assumptions. Bear: US$190bn revenue and 42% net margin allow some growth versus the approximate 2026 midpoint but assume material profitability normalization and a lower 20x multiple. This is not a catastrophe case; war, prolonged shutdown or severe demand destruction could be far worse. Base: US$220bn revenue, 49% margin and 24x earnings assume continuing growth with profitability below Q3's 51.1%. Bull: US$250bn revenue, 52% margin and 28x require strong demand, good capacity execution and a premium valuation. These assumptions are deliberately visible so they can be challenged. The margin of safety depends on the model. A 20% discount to the illustrative base value is about US$399.1. That is near the US$395.75 historical reference, but it is not a floor, an order or a recommended entry. The base case still assumes substantial future growth. Returns are model price/reference price - 1, excluding dividends, fees, FX costs and taxes. No separate net-cash value is added because the EPS/P/E method is an equity valuation; adding it mechanically can double count financial income. 07 VALUATION CHECKS AND RISKS The assumptions deserve as much attention as the target Risks data 2027 EPS / P/E 20x 24x 28x US$16 $320 $384 $448 US$20 $400 $480 $560 US$24 $480 $576 $672 Independent sensitivity, US$/ADR; no probabilities or consensus status. Each cell is EPS x multiple. At US$395.75, a 24x multiple requires about US$16.49 annual EPS; a 20x multiple requires US$19.79. Annualizing the latest quarter makes the stock look less demanding than using history. Q3's US$4.60 ADR EPS x four is US$18.40, implying 21.5x at the reference price. This is a run-rate illustration, not trailing or forward P/E: it ignores seasonality, future ramp costs and non-operating items. [1,13; calculation] Risks data Risk Why it matters Evidence to watch Taiwan disruption Production, utilities and supply chains can be interrupted; losses need not resemble an ordinary cycle. Location exposure; contingency capacity; official developments AI demand and concentration Different chip customers can depend on common cloud spending budgets. Customer capex, order timing, utilization and HPC mix Capacity and yield execution Start-up costs can arrive before profitable output. N2 ramp, leading-node yield, capex and gross margin Overseas economics Resilience may cost more and dilute returns. Fab milestones and disclosed margin dilution Export rules and competition Demand can be restricted or move to alternatives. Official rules, customer mix, competing-node execution Valuation and ADR exposure Multiple compression or FX can offset earnings growth. Consistent currency/share basis; fees and tax treatment Risk framework: issuer disclosures [7], management outlook [5], and independent analysis. The 20-F identifies customer concentration, capacity forecasting, export restrictions, disasters, utility interruptions and cyber threats; no probability of geopolitical disruption is estimated here. Multiple end markets do not make TSM a diversified conglomerate. It remains a focused manufacturing franchise. Combining it with AI hardware companies or hyperscaler exposures may offer less diversification than the different tickers suggest. This is a general risk observation, not an assessment of any individual portfolio. 08 REVIEW PLAN AND SECURITY DETAILS What would strengthen or weaken the case Review plan data Checkpoint Stronger evidence Weaker evidence Demand Sales meet guidance with sustainable orders Repeated delays or unexplained inventory build Profit quality Operating earnings grow without one-off dependence Net income supported chiefly by gains or subsidies Investment returns FCF stays healthy as new capacity fills Capex rises while utilization and cash conversion fall Technology N2 ramps with manageable margin cost Yield or schedule setbacks spread across products Shareholder return Per-ADR earnings grow with disciplined reinvestment Share-count, FX or reinvestment drag overwhelms growth Confirmed upcoming information The next scheduled operating update is October monthly sales on 10 November 2026. The calendar then lists November sales on 10 December and December sales on 8 January 2027. Dates are subject to change. Monthly sales show revenue pace, not quarterly profit or free cash flow. [15] September revenue was NT$511.86bn, down 0.6% from August and up 54.6% year over year. Nine-month cumulative revenue rose 41.1% in NT dollars. The next release can be compared with Q4 guidance, but one month is not the entire quarter. [16] ADR and currency discipline One TSM ADR represents five ordinary shares. NYSE TSM trades in US dollars; Taiwan-listed 2330 is an ordinary share in New Taiwan dollars. Do not multiply the ADR price by the full ordinary share count, or compare NT-dollar ordinary EPS directly with a US-dollar ADR price. [2] At the reference ADR price, 5.1864bn ADR-equivalent shares imply approximately US$2.052tn equity value. This is an illustrative ADR-equivalent calculation, not an official consolidated market cap: it mixes the September share count with November pricing and may differ from local-share valuation through ADR premiums and FX. [2,13; calculation] Dividend cash received is not the declared NT-dollar dividend. Currency conversion, depositary fees, withholding and personal taxes can change the net USD payment. Investor-specific taxes and broker fees are not modeled, so no individual net yield or total-return forecast is presented. Research conclusion TSMC merits consideration as a long-term advanced manufacturing investment, subject to price and risk tolerance. Its financial strength and technology position support the case. The harder question is whether future capacity earns enough to justify the valuation while preserving cash returns. Independent scenario downside and Taiwan exposure prevent treating the business as a certain bargain. 09 SOURCES AND METHODS Source register Research cutoff: 5 November 2026. THE CENTRAL JUDGMENT | REPORT ANALYSIS Office distress is material. A system-wide banking crisis is a conditional risk, not an established outcome. The critical test is whether refinancing gaps turn into losses that exceed individual lenders' earnings and capital while funding confidence weakens. Source/context: Federal Reserve: H.8 bank assets and liabilities Five takeaways that matter Refinancing is the immediate test. A borrower can pay today's interest yet lack the cash to repay the balloon balance at maturity. CMBS distress is not a bank loss rate. Loan populations, reporting dates, delinquency rules and loss allocation differ. [2] [3] [4] Concentration magnifies the effect on capital. A smaller loan book can pose a larger bank-level threat if it is large relative to capital and exposed to the same local economy. An extension must be judged by its terms. Fresh equity, paydowns and credible cash flow can repair a loan; repeated relief without those changes can defer the problem. [11] [12] Systemic risk needs transmission. Watch simultaneous credit deterioration, funding outflows and shrinking lending capacity. Aggregate profitability is a buffer, not proof that every bank is safe. FILL THE GAP Existing debt plus transaction costs, less new borrowing and available cash, leaves an equity or paydown requirement. RESOLVE The owner contributes capital, sells, negotiates a workout, or defaults if a viable solution cannot be agreed. Follow the numbered stages from new debt capacity to the equity gap and a resolution decision. The tighter collateral or income constraint can leave an equity/paydown gap. Appraisal and sale liquidity Sparse transactions can make valuation uncertain; a forced sale may produce a different recovery from an orderly workout. The interagency screen includes CRE at least 300% of total capital and CRE growth of at least 50% over the prior 36 months. A separate construction/land screen starts at 100% of capital. Broad reported CRE balances need not match the supervisory definition. [10] H.8: 28 Oct 2026; research concentration: 30 Sep 2025, as identified. Source/context: Interagency CRE concentration guidance CAPITAL TRANSLATION | REPORT ANALYSIS Gross portfolio loss relative to capital = CRE loans / capital × portfolio loss rate. This is an accounting identity, not a forecast. Earnings, existing allowances, tax effects, risk weights and capital actions affect the actual regulatory outcome. Concentration makes the bank sensitive; it does not determine the loss rate. H.8: 28 Oct 2026; research concentration: 30 Sep 2025, as identified. Units/scope: USD billions, loan share percent or CRE/capital percent; distinct denominators. H.8 small banks, research regional banks and supervisory screening are different populations and concepts. Source/context: Interagency CRE concentration guidance THE REFINANCING TEST · 8 NOV 2026 06 / 16 06 / EXTENSIONS AND RECOGNITION Buying time can help, or hide a deterioration The evidence is contested. A loan extension is a contract change; its economic value depends on what changes with it. Evidence of delayed recognition Crosignani & Prazad find that weakly capitalised banks extended distressed CRE loans and granted payment relief to preserve capital. Their analysis links this behaviour to less new lending and more maturities clustered ahead. [11] New York Fed staff working paper • October 2024, revised June 2026 • post-pandemic supervisory evidence. NY Fed revised Jun 2026; FEDS May 2026; original cutoff 8 Nov 2026. Units/scope: Qualitative findings and conceptual workout criteria; not pooled loss estimates. Different research samples support different findings; an extension alone proves neither fraud nor soundness. Source/context: Crosignani & Prazad: Extend-and-Pretend Evidence of effective workouts Glancy finds that extensions mainly addressed temporary payment frictions. Banks increased income and principal-paydown requirements after the 2023 stress episode, supporting strong performance relative to comparable unextended loans. The finding that about half of 2023-25 maturities were extended does not itself prove concealment. [12] Federal Reserve FEDS paper • May 2026 • large-bank supervisory data; not a census of smaller regional lenders. NY Fed revised Jun 2026; FEDS May 2026; original cutoff 8 Nov 2026. Units/scope: Qualitative findings and conceptual workout criteria; not pooled loss estimates. Different research samples support different findings; an extension alone proves neither fraud nor soundness. Source/context: Glancy: Pretend or Amend? On Evergreening in CRE Loan extensions: repair versus deferral Assess the extension Evidence of repair Evidence of deferral Owner commitment New equity, cash paydown, enforceable support No new capital despite a widening shortfall Operating cash Credible rent, expenses and leasing budget Interest funded through further borrowing Exit plan Repayment supported by realistic valuation and terms Reliance on untested rent or sale assumptions Bank reporting Updated grades, allowances and valuation evidence Repeat extensions with little explanation of risk Compare the evidence of repair against the evidence of continuing deferral. Fresh capital, sustainable operations and a credible exit distinguish a workout from delay. NY Fed revised Jun 2026; FEDS May 2026; original cutoff 8 Nov 2026. Units/scope: Qualitative findings and conceptual workout criteria; not pooled loss estimates. Different research samples support different findings; an extension alone proves neither fraud nor soundness. Source/context: Interagency policy: prudent CRE accommodations and workouts Assess, recognise, resolve ASSESS Re-underwrite repayment capacity and collateral. RECOGNISE Review risk grade, nonaccrual status and expected credit-loss allowance. RESOLVE Recover cash or charge off amounts judged uncollectible. Follow the numbered assessment, accounting-recognition and cash-resolution steps. Prudent workouts require repayment assessment and recognition, not only contractual current payments. NY Fed revised Jun 2026; FEDS May 2026; original cutoff 8 Nov 2026. Units/scope: Qualitative findings and conceptual workout criteria; not pooled loss estimates. Different research samples support different findings; an extension alone proves neither fraud nor soundness. Source/context: Interagency policy: prudent CRE accommodations and workouts Current payments are not the whole test. Guidance allows prudent workouts and says collateral decline alone need not trigger adverse classification when repayment remains credible. It also warns that contractual currency can obscure credit weakness. A provision reduces earnings; a charge-off uses the allowance already established. Counting both as fresh losses can double-count the impact. [13] REPORT ANALYSIS Read the terms and outcomes, not just the number of extensions. Different samples and research methods can support different conclusions. Neither paper justifies declaring every extension fraudulent or every extended loan sound. NY Fed revised Jun 2026; FEDS May 2026; original cutoff 8 Nov 2026. Units/scope: Qualitative findings and conceptual workout criteria; not pooled loss estimates. Different research samples support different findings; an extension alone proves neither fraud nor soundness. Source/context: Interagency policy: prudent CRE accommodations and workouts THE REFINANCING TEST · 8 NOV 2026 07 / 16 07 / SYSTEMIC TRANSMISSION Credit losses and a funding run are different Property stress becomes systemic when the effects spread across institutions and constrain the wider supply of credit. From property pressure to wider credit contraction PROPERTY Lower sustainable cash flow or collateral value weakens repayment and refinancing capacity. CREDIT More provisions, nonaccrual loans and realised losses reduce earnings and can erode capital. CONFIDENCE Concern about loss absorption can raise funding costs or encourage deposit withdrawals. LIQUIDITY The bank needs cash now; it may borrow against eligible collateral or sell assets. FEEDBACK Forced sales and tighter lending can weaken property prices, borrowers and other lenders. Follow the numbered stages from property cash flow and credit recognition to capital, funding and lending. These are conditional links, not a claim that every stage is occurring. Systemic risk requires transmission across institutions and funding or credit supply. Conditional transmission analysis at the 8 Nov 2026 cutoff. Units/scope: Qualitative mechanisms; no probabilities or numerical loss forecast. Credit losses and funding stress are distinct; transmission is a conditional risk, not an established system-wide crisis. Source/context: Federal Reserve: October 2026 SLOOS Liquidity: can cash leave faster than it arrives? A timing problem can destabilise a viable bank. Read deposit concentration, uninsured funding, liquid assets, collateral availability and contingent borrowing capacity. Assets that are valuable over time may be difficult to sell quickly at that value. Conditional transmission analysis at the 8 Nov 2026 cutoff. Monitoring questions and warning evidence Question Evidence to request A warning that matters Can the building support its debt? NOI, cash debt-service coverage, lease expiries, concessions and capital needs. Income cannot cover sustainable financing after reserves and leasing costs. Is maturity risk actually shrinking? Cash payoffs and paydowns, new equity, extensions by original maturity year. Repeated maturity shifts without more repayment capacity. Are credit problems being recognised? Criticized/classified loans, nonaccruals, charge-offs and allowance changes. Weak loans grow faster than credible reserves or resolution progress. Can the bank absorb the losses? CRE and office relative to capital, earnings before provisions, stress assumptions. Concentrations and losses overwhelm earnings and the usable capital buffer. Is funding confidence holding? Deposit flows, uninsured concentrations, funding cost and collateral capacity. Outflows coincide with costly borrowing and asset disposals. Is stress becoming widespread? Loan-officer surveys, multiple bank disclosures, CRE financing and sale volumes. Several institutions tighten together while credit and funding measures deteriorate. Read the diligence question with the evidence requested and the warning condition. Monitor cash resolution, capital and funding together rather than one headline.
