entries.text: Who is buying gold? | Market Intelligence Hub Skip to research Market Intelligence Hub Research · 06 Nov 2026 Global reserves / Precious metals Who is buying gold? Central-bank buyers, sellers and what drives a Singapore investor’s return. Market Intelligence Hub · Research edition · 6 November 2026 The quarter in focus / Q3 2026 Only part of the buying is visible 321.2 t Estimated official net buying 120 t Publicly reported net buying Solid = disclosed. Hatched = estimated remainder. Metric tonnes, rounded for the split. WGC / Metals Focus Full report · PDF · 24 pages Executive briefing · PowerPoint · 5 slides Visual story · PowerPoint · 5 slides China and Poland led disclosed Q3 buying. Roughly 63% of total estimated demand cannot be attributed to named buyers. A central bank may sell gold to raise currency, rebalance a portfolio or meet a policy obligation. The reason changes how to read the sale. For Singapore investors, both the gold price and USD/SGD determine the unhedged return. Bank forecasts also have different dates and horizons. Market snapshot Spot gold traded at US$4,044.09/oz on 6 November at 13:01 Singapore time. Reuters Current section Overview 01 · Official demand 02 · How to read the data 03 · Disclosed buyers 04 · Disclosed sellers 05 · Reading the global register 06 · Historical reversals 07 · Case study · Ghana 08 · Reserve management 09 · Gold and US Treasuries 10 · The price of gold 11 · Bank and agency outlooks 12 · Reading the bank papers 13 · Singapore reserves 14 · The Singapore investor 15 · Portfolio decisions 16 · Reading guide Sources A+ Dark Grey 01 Official demand Central banks bought more gold as the price weakened Official buyers stepped up sharply after a weak first quarter. The November data show a net 57.7 tonnes in Q1, 296.3 in Q2 and 321.2 in Q3. The last figure was 42% above a year earlier. Yet the World Bank reports that gold prices fell 5% from Q2 to Q3. A reserve manager can add to a holding while other investors sell enough to push the price down. The estimate changed enough to alter the story of the year. The first Q1 release put buying at 244 tonnes. The Q2 release revised that sharply downward, and the November table puts it at 57.7. Combining April’s Q1 estimate with November’s Q2 and Q3 figures would exaggerate the level of demand and hide the rebound. XAU/USD World Bank Exhibit 01.1 Official net purchases accelerated through 2026 Net metric tonnes by quarter · 3 November data release Q1 2026 57.7 t Q2 2026 296.3 t Q3 2026 321.2 t Exact figures in a table Measure Value Q1 2026 57.7 t Q2 2026 296.3 t Q3 2026 321.2 t Each bar starts at zero. Purchases less sales across central banks and other official institutions include estimated activity. Sources · WGC [G1] · WGC / Metals Focus [G2] Exhibit 01.2 Price and purchasing moved in opposite directions Q3 versus Q2 2026 · changes as published Measure Quarter-on-quarter change Official gold demand +8% Gold price, World Bank review −5% The observations describe the same quarter. They do not measure the price effect of an individual purchase. Sources · WGC [G1] · World Bank [W1] Evidence · G1 G2 G6 G7 W1 Next ↓ 02 How to read the data Who bought the remaining gold? Public filings identify only part of Q3 buying. The World Gold Council puts disclosed net purchases at 120 tonnes, compared with roughly 321 tonnes after Metals Focus incorporates estimates. The gap covers late reporting and trades that never appear in time for publication. It cannot be reliably assigned to China , a Gulf state or another named buyer. The answer to “is buying up this year?” depends on the series. For January to September, reported purchases fell 7% year on year to 228 tonnes. Estimated demand rose 6% to 675 tonnes. Both comparisons can be right because their coverage differs. A monthly change in disclosed reserves is evidence about that balance sheet, while imports can also reflect households, jewellers, banks and funds. XAU/USD Reported series Exhibit 02.1 About 63% of Q3 net demand was unreported Approximate decomposition · net metric tonnes · July–September 2026 Disclosed · 120 t Estimated remainder · about 201 t Exact figures in a table Measure Value Disclosed 120 t Estimated remainder about 201 t The remainder uses source-rounded figures, 321 less 120. It has no reliable country-by-country breakdown. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus [G2] Exhibit 02.2 The reporting perimeter changes the year-on-year conclusion January–September 2026 · net metric tonnes Coverage 2026 Year on year Publicly reported 228 t −7% Reported plus estimated 675 t +6% The two rows overlap. Adding them would count publicly reported activity twice. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus [G2] · WGC [G3] Evidence · G1 G2 G3 Next ↓ 03 Disclosed buyers China picked up the pace as Poland approached its target China added 63 tonnes in Q3, more than half its purchases for the first nine months. Its September statement gives a direct check on the quantity. Holdings rose by 740,000 ounces to 77.47 million ounces, the 23rd consecutive monthly increase. The announcement gives no price target or motive for that month’s purchase. Poland’s governor confirmed on 5 November that reserves had reached the 700-tonne goal. Quarterly additions slowed from 51 tonnes in Q2 to 40 tonnes in Q3. He left open further purchases as overall reserves grow. The next indication of demand will come from the board’s decision on how much gold to hold. Uzbekistan illustrates how purchases can coexist with a willingness to sell. The central bank added 14 tonnes in Q3. Its governor had discussed selling at favourable prices as part of reserve management. A willingness to sell gives the bank flexibility and leaves the timing open. China Poland Exhibit 03.1 Six disclosed changes show how concentrated buying was Net tonnes, Q3 2026 China +63 t Poland +40 t Kazakhstan +14 t Uzbekistan +14 t Czechia +5 t Russia −19 t Exact figures in a table Measure Value China +63 t Poland +40 t Kazakhstan +14 t Uzbekistan +14 t Czechia +5 t Russia −19 t Right of zero means a net addition. WGC’s rounded figures put China and Poland together at 104 t on unrounded data, about 86% of reported net demand. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus [G2] Exhibit 03.2 Two approaches to reserve accumulation Policy evidence available by 5 November 2026 Institution What is confirmed What to watch Poland 700-tonne target reached, governor said on 5 Nov. A new allocation decision or evidence of continued purchases. Czechia 87.4 tonnes held at end-Sep. CNB aims for 100 tonnes by 2028. Progress toward a stated target and any change in the mandate. A public target provides a reference point. Actual purchases and their timing still depend on the institution. Sources · Reuters [C4] · Czech National Bank [C5] Evidence · G2 C3 C4 C15 C5 Next ↓ 04 Disclosed sellers Gold supplied cash when some official holders needed it Russia’s governor linked recent reductions mainly to the finance ministry’s transactions under its fiscal rule. The National Wealth Fund holds assets that the ministry can use under that rule. The governor also cited metal used for coin production. The published explanation does not allocate the quarter’s 19-tonne decline across those uses. Türkiye used gold to obtain foreign currency when demand for cash rose. In March, the central bank both disposed of metal and arranged gold-for-currency swaps. Under a swap, the bank agrees to reverse the exchange at maturity. Adding the swap amount to outright sales would overstate the gold permanently sold. Azerbaijan’s sovereign wealth fund reported the same gold stock in March and September. Its year-end to September holdings fell by 21.9 tonnes. The fund states its diversification policy and allocation limits. Its holdings disclosures leave the specific reason for the reduction open. Russia Türkiye Exhibit 04.1 Three different kinds of reduction Metric tonnes and observation windows shown Institution Observed change Evidence for the explanation Bank of Russia −19 t in Q3 Governor identified fiscal-rule operations and minting in September. Türkiye −81 t Jan–Sep; +1 t in Sep March swaps provided FX liquidity. A monthly addition can coexist with a year-to-date reduction. Azerbaijan · SOFAZ 200.0 t at Dec 2025; 178.1 t in Mar and Sep 2026 Sovereign fund. Changes are calculated from its own period-end stocks. Qatar, Kyrgyz Republic, UAE Small Q3 reductions WGC identified the declines. Individual motives were undisclosed. Observation windows differ. SOFAZ reports quarterly and is excluded from WGC monthly totals. A period-end stock cannot reveal every intervening transaction. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus [G2] · WGC [G3] · Bank of Russia [C8] · WGC [C9] · State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan [C11] · State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan [C12] · State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan [C10] Evidence · G2 G3 C8 C9 C11 C12 C10 Next ↓ 05 Reading the global register The largest vaults tell a different story from the largest buyers A ranking by tonnes held answers who owns the stock today. The World Gold Council’s register covers the top 100 disclosed holders and provides a separate file of changes. Most November entries refer to September, while some refer to June or earlier. The prior Hub report screened that roster. This update verifies selected moves and the cases below against their own disclosures. Five legacy holders still account for about 52% of world gold reserves. Federal Reserve staff identify the United States, Germany, Italy, France and the IMF . Together they have added little since the 1970s. Their existing stock can rise by billions of dollars in value without producing a new purchase. Gold can arrive in a country’s vault without the country buying it. The New York Fed stores metal for official account holders. South Korea illustrates a different issue: owning units in a gold fund gives the central bank exposure to the price, while the central bank reports a separate monetary-gold stock. Official reserves Physical holdings Exhibit 05.1 Ownership, custody, exposure and a reported zero Reference dates and instrument types shown Case What the source measures How to read it United States Treasury owns US official gold. The New York Fed holds metal for multiple owners. A change in foreign client custody does not establish a US purchase. Canada Finance Canada showed US$0m for gold on 30 Oct 2026. The source reports a zero position at its published precision. South Korea 679,765 SPDR Gold Trust shares at end-Jun. Separately, 104.4 t of physical reserves. Count ETF shares as securities. A planned December domestic buying channel was still prospective. The WGC top-100 register is linked in the sources. No entry or an old reporting date cannot establish zero activity. Sources · WGC / IMF IFS [C16] · Federal Reserve Board [C17] · Department of Finance Canada [C18] · Reuters [C20] · Reuters [C21] Evidence · C16 C17 C18 F1 C20 C21 H1 Next ↓ 06 Historical reversals Czechia rebuilt its stock while Switzerland held steady Czechia reversed an earlier decision to sell most of its gold. The Czech National Bank resumed more active buying in 2023. Its own analysis found that a holding near 100 tonnes would make its financial results less sensitive to market swings. That explains the target from the perspective of this particular institution. The Swiss National Bank still holds the same 1,040 tonnes it held at the end of 2008. Its gold is stored in Switzerland, London and Canada to preserve access in a crisis. All three locations belong to the same Swiss stock. Counting the location of bars as a purchase would create a trade that never took place. Europe’s coordinated sales wound down before the agreement expired in 2019. The ECB said signatories had sold little for nearly a decade. A world in which legacy holders sell less and other reserve managers buy more can show net purchases even when few institutions reverse their own policy. Swiss National Bank Czechia Exhibit 06.1 Read the verb before reading the tonnes Historical reported stocks and stated goals Case Starting position Later position Meaning Czechia 8 t at end-2019; about 12 t at end-2022 87.4 t in Sep 2026; target 100 t by 2028 A deliberate rebuild Switzerland 1,040 t at end-2008 1,040 t in the SNB’s current disclosure Long-running hold European agreement Official sales coordinated from 1999 Agreement expired in Sep 2019 End of a sales framework The Czech target is a future policy objective. The other stock figures refer to holdings that the institutions reported. Sources · Czech National Bank [C5] · Swiss National Bank [C6] · European Central Bank [C7] Evidence · C5 C6 C7 Next ↓ 07 Case study · Ghana A gold export programme can earn dollars and lose money Ghana turned locally mined gold into foreign currency during a debt crisis. When access to external borrowing tightened, the Bank of Ghana could buy gold from local producers in cedis and export it for dollars. In 2025 it purchased and exported about 104 tonnes of artisanal and small-scale gold worth US$10.9 billion. Most of that metal passed through the programme. The same programme generated losses of over US$1.7 billion in 2025, equivalent to 1.5% of GDP. The IMF identifies the biggest contributor as the gap between the exchange rate used to buy the gold and the reference rate used in the bank’s accounts. Assay fees, service charges and discounts to buyers added to losses. Part of the figure reflects accounting valuation; it cannot all be read as a cash loss. GoldBod took over the programme’s operations and costs in July 2026. The central bank retained a role as fiscal agent and as recipient of monetary gold for reserves. A change in who buys raw metal can therefore occur alongside continued changes in central-bank bullion holdings. IMF Ghana Exhibit 07.1 Follow the gold and the cash Ghana · 2025 mechanism and July 2026 transition 1 Local miners Supply partially refined gold. Purchases require cedis and quality checks. 2 Export channel Assaying, services and sale to buyers produce costs and foreign-currency proceeds. 3 Bank balance sheet Dollars can replenish reserves or finance FX sales. The exchange-rate spread affects the accounts. The US$10.9bn measures gross artisanal exports. The US$1.7bn figure measures programme losses and uses a different accounting basis. Sources · IMF Selected Issues Paper 2026/084 · Guillaume Nolin [C13] · IMF Notes 2026/007 [I1] Evidence · C13 I1 Next ↓ 08 Reserve management Why hold an asset that pays no interest? A gold bar has no issuing government that must repay it. For a reserve manager, that feature can matter when access to foreign assets becomes uncertain. A bar held at home reduces exposure to a foreign custodian. It may still have to be moved, sold or pledged before the central bank can supply dollars to local banks. The IMF authors separate long-term reserves from the cash needed at short notice. In an illustrative two-day liquidation under stress, the IMF staff note suggests discounting the headline value by 6–12% to estimate usable liquidity. More respondents expected global gold holdings to grow than expected their own bank to buy. Among respondents to the 2026 World Gold Council survey, 89% expected global official holdings to rise in the next year and 45% expected their own holdings to rise. Diversification, performance in crises and inflation protection featured in their answers. The survey records intentions. It cannot give the date or size of a trade. IMF Reserve policy Exhibit 08.1 Two uses of reserves lead to different choices Reserve-management framework · IMF staff analysis, July 2026 Need What the reserve manager considers Pay USD obligations soon Cash and readily saleable foreign assets can meet a known currency need. Diversify a long-term portfolio Physical gold removes issuer credit exposure but adds price volatility, custody costs and forgone interest. Retain control under sanctions Domestic custody can improve control. Converting those bars into usable FX can become harder under stress. The same asset can protect against one risk and make a different risk harder to manage. Sources · IMF Notes 2026/007 [I1] Exhibit 08.2 Expectations differ when managers speak about their own bank Share of respondents to each question · survey published 16 June 2026 Global official gold holdings will grow 89% Own bank’s gold holdings will grow 45% Exact figures in a table Measure Value Global official gold holdings will grow 89% Own bank’s gold holdings will grow 45% The answers concern the following 12 months. The questions have different subjects and do not add to 100%. Sources · WGC [G5] Evidence · I1 G5 Next ↓ 09 Gold and US Treasuries A higher reserve share can come from the same bars Gold’s share of reserves can rise before a central bank buys another ounce. The IMF authors found that between 2018 and 2025 the market value of official gold rose 268%, while the physical quantity rose about 8.5%. A reserve portfolio is like a household balance sheet. If a home appreciates, property becomes a larger share of wealth even when the family buys no property. The ranking also changes when the investor group changes. A September Federal Reserve staff note points out that world gold includes US government gold, while foreign official Treasury holdings exclude the US. At end-2025, gold outside the US was worth US$4 trillion against US$3.9 trillion in foreign official Treasuries. By June 2026 Treasuries were ahead on that comparison even though gold ounces had increased. European Central Bank US Treasuries Exhibit 09.1 Repricing the same end-2025 holdings changes their ranking Share of total official reserves including gold · ECB estimates Asset At end-2025 prices At end-2023 gold price Gold 27% 16% US Treasuries 22% 26% Euro-denominated reserves 15% 16% Read across each row. The ECB changed the price assigned to gold. Changing the total also changes the percentage share of the other assets. Selected assets only. Sources · European Central Bank [E1] Evidence · I1 E1 F1 Next ↓ 10 The price of gold Funds bought gold in October and still lost value Investors added US$2.7 billion to gold funds in October, yet the funds finished the month worth less. The World Gold Council’s specialised ETF report shows that physical holdings rose by 19 tonnes to 4,275 tonnes, while total assets fell 6% to US$542 billion. The lower price of the metal already in the vault outweighed the value of new subscriptions. The next trade can come from a buyer with a very different deadline. OCBC’s 26 October tracker found investment managers had reduced their futures exposure and that protection against a fall had grown dearer relative to upside protection. It also observed a Shanghai physical premium of about 0.9%. A wholesaler paying extra for metal and a fund selling futures to raise cash can act on the same day. Households responded differently again. The World Gold Council’s Q3 table showed bar-and-coin demand fell 19% year on year and jewellery consumption fell 17%. A higher price can discourage a wedding purchase even while an official buyer pursues a multi-year policy. The amount one group buys gives no mechanical price target for the next trade. XAU/USD ETF flows Exhibit 10.1 October’s three readings count different things October 2026 · specialised ETF and derivatives report, 5 November Observation Change What moved Physical ETF holdings +19 t Metal held for investors ETF assets under management −6% Market value of all holdings COMEX managed-money net longs −53 t equivalent Futures positioning of this trader group A fall in futures exposure does not mean 53 tonnes of bars left ETF vaults. The series use different markets and investor groups. Sources · WGC [G4] Evidence · G1 G4 O1 Next ↓ 11 Bank and agency outlooks The World Bank and the Reuters poll disagree on 2027 Two October forecasts give opposite answers to the same question. For the average gold price in 2027, the World Bank estimates US$4,250 an ounce, US$350 below its 2026 figure. The Reuters poll puts 2027 at US$4,650, US$155 above its 2026 median. The gap between their 2027 forecasts is US$400. It reflects disagreement among forecasters, rather than a trading range. An annual average can fall even if gold ends the year above today’s price. An average includes all the observations across the year. A high starting point or a few strong early months can lift it. Standard Chartered’s targets instead describe where the bank expects gold to trade at particular horizons. Combining all these figures into a single target would answer no clear question. World Bank Forecasts Exhibit 11.1 Annual-average forecasts can be compared directly Nominal US dollars per troy ounce · October 2026 publications Forecast owner 2026 average 2027 average Change World Bank 4,600 4,250 −350 Reuters poll, median 4,495 4,650 +155 Read across a row for one forecast path. Read down the 2027 column to see the US$400 disagreement. These are forecasts, not realised returns. Sources · World Bank [W1] · Reuters commodities poll [R2] Exhibit 11.2 Point targets answer a different question US dollars per troy ounce · dated targets Publisher and date Horizon Target Standard Chartered · 30 Oct Three months 4,350 Standard Chartered · 30 Oct Twelve months 4,700 Goldman Sachs · 5 Nov, via Reuters End-2026 4,150 The Goldman Sachs year-end target was cut from 4,650. Even a positive longer-term view can coincide with a lower near-term target. Sources · Standard Chartered Global CIO Office [B1] · Reuters [R1] Evidence · W1 R2 B1 R1 Next ↓ 12 Reading the bank papers What happened to J.P. Morgan’s US$6,000 call? The US$6,000 forecast in the supplied paper was published on 9 June. The detailed table defined it as a Q4 2026 average. On 3 July Reuters reported a new J.P. Morgan forecast of US$4,500 for the same quarter. Comparing the same horizon gives a US$1,500 reduction, or 25%. The November date on the saved copy records when the web page was printed. The bank’s change of mind had a stated economic reason. By July it saw softer demand from key buyers and greater sensitivity to real yields. Real yield is the return a bond offers after allowing for inflation. When that return rises, investors give up more income by holding a bar that pays no coupon. Central banks can keep accumulating gold while private investors change what they are willing to pay for it. J.P. Morgan real yields Exhibit 12.1 One bank, two forecasts for the same quarter Q4 2026 average · US dollars per troy ounce · issue dates below 9 June forecast US$6,000 2 July note, reported 3 July US$4,500 Exact figures in a table Measure Value 9 June forecast US$6,000 2 July note, reported 3 July US$4,500 Bars are dated forecasts, not market prices. The revision was (4,500 − 6,000) ÷ 6,000 = −25%. Sources · J.P. Morgan Global Research [J1] · Reuters reporting on J.P. Morgan research [J2] Evidence · J1 J2 O1 Next ↓ 13 Singapore reserves MAS rebuilt some of the gold it had trimmed Singapore ’s reported gold rose by 323,268 fine troy ounces in the first nine months of 2026. That reverses the direction of the two preceding year-end changes. The September balance remained below December 2024. Describing this as a partial rebuild fits the series. It also avoids guessing at MAS ’s preferred entry price or the reason for each adjustment. MAS gives readers both an accounting value and a physical volume. Its September return shows US$6,223.50 million for gold on its published book-value basis and separately lists 6,546,481 fine troy ounces. Using the ounce line avoids turning accounting changes into assumed purchases. The category includes gold deposits and, where appropriate, swapped gold. MAS Singapore Exhibit 13.1 Gold on Singapore’s official reserve return Fine troy ounces · I.A(4), period end Observation Reported volume Change from prior row Dec 2023 7,395,505 — Dec 2024 7,072,034 −323,471 Dec 2025 6,223,213 −848,821 Sep 2026, preliminary 6,546,481 +323,268 The last step covers nine months. These are changes between reported balances. They do not show individual trade dates or sale proceeds. Sources · Monetary Authority of Singapore [M4] · Monetary Authority of Singapore [M3] · Monetary Authority of Singapore [M2] · Monetary Authority of Singapore [M1] Evidence · M4 M3 M2 M1 Next ↓ 14 The Singapore investor Translate the gold return into the currency you spend A Singapore investor who owns unhedged gold has two prices to watch. XAU/USD quotes the US dollars needed to buy one troy ounce. USD/SGD quotes the Singapore dollars needed to buy one US dollar. Multiply the two at the same time to get Singapore dollars per ounce. A stronger Singapore dollar means each US dollar of gold proceeds converts into fewer Singapore dollars. Use the actual instrument and matching timestamps at both ends. A physical bar has a dealer spread and may carry storage costs. An ETF has a fee and its trading price can differ from the value of its gold. A derivatives contract can add collateral, leverage or rolling costs. The earlier Hub study traced XAU39344-USD to a derivatives listing. Joining that series to a spot quote would give a misleading return. XAU/USD USD/SGD Exhibit 14.1 From two market quotes to a Singapore-dollar return Unhedged exposure · same quantity · before dealing costs 1 Entry value per ounce Entry XAU/USD × entry USD/SGD. 2 Exit value per ounce Exit XAU/USD × exit USD/SGD. 3 Gross SGD return (Exit SGD value ÷ entry SGD value − 1) × 100%. For an actual cash return, compare SGD paid including fees with SGD received net of sale costs. A currency-hedged share class follows a different calculation. Sources · Market Intelligence Hub [H1] Exhibit 14.2 How the currency leg changes the outcome Unhedged holding · direction only Gold in USD USD/SGD What it means in SGD Rises Rises Both price moves help. Rises Falls FX can reduce, erase or reverse the gold gain. Flat Falls SGD gold loses value before costs. USD/SGD falls when the Singapore dollar strengthens against the US dollar. The HTML calculator accepts your own two dated gold and FX quotes. Evidence · H1 M1 Next ↓ 15 Portfolio decisions What would change the investment case? Choose the reason for holding gold before choosing an entry. If the objective is long-term diversification, ask whether the position still helps when it loses value at the same time as shares. If the objective is a short trade, the price of money, the US dollar and leveraged positioning can matter sooner than the next quarterly reserve release. A cash need in SGD requires a separate currency and liquidity decision. A useful test is to specify what would change your mind. A stronger dollar and rising real yields can pressure gold even as official demand holds up. Conversely, easier real yields and persistent investment inflows can support a recovery. These are conditional paths. Data observed together can support a narrative without proving which trade moved the price. real yields USD/SGD Exhibit 15.1 Three possible paths and the evidence to watch Conditional scenarios as at 6 November 2026 · no assigned probabilities Scenario What to look for Decision to revisit Support broadens Real yields ease, the dollar softens and physical ETF holdings keep rising. Check whether the price recovery also reaches the SGD investor. Gold trades sideways Official demand persists while private investors disagree and yields stay high. Revisit the holding horizon and the income forgone on cash or bonds. A cash squeeze Futures longs shrink, ETF holdings roll over or a stronger dollar tightens liquidity. Check funding needs, available cash and tolerance for an interim loss. Read each row as a combination of signals. A single data point, including a central-bank release, cannot confirm an entry price. Monthly ETF holdings and national reserve volumes Distinguish physical additions from valuation and currency effects. A target being reached, or a forecast being cut, is a reason to revisit its contribution. The most useful papers look at different parts of the gold market. The IMF authors study what a reserve manager can do with bullion in a crisis. The ECB and Federal Reserve papers test how much of the rise in gold’s reported importance comes from prices and existing holdings. Bank outlooks focus more closely on the marginal buyer and the next few quarters. The silver and renminbi papers help define the limits of the gold argument. J.P. Morgan’s silver research discusses solar manufacturers reducing silver use. That industrial channel is much less central to the official gold story. OCBC’s November renminbi note concerns its currency outlook, and its sustainability weekly covers other policy developments. Neither establishes the identity of an undisclosed gold buyer. Earlier PDF editions remain available above. Slides were rendered in LibreOffice; native PowerPoint compatibility was not tested. Some dated forecasts could not be independently rechecked during publication review. Skip to research Market Intelligence Hub Edition 2 · 06 Nov 2026 Global reserves / Precious metals Who is buying gold? Central-bank buyers, sellers and what drives a Singapore investor’s return. Market Intelligence Hub · Edition 2 · Checked 6 November, 16:40 SGT The quarter in focus / Q3 2026 Only part of the buying is visible 321.2 t Estimated official net buying 120 t Publicly reported net buying Solid = disclosed. Hatched = estimated remainder. Metric tonnes, rounded for the split. WGC / Metals Focus China and Poland led disclosed Q3 buying. Roughly 63% of total estimated demand cannot be attributed to named buyers. A central bank may sell gold to raise currency, rebalance a portfolio or meet a policy obligation. The reason changes how to read the sale. For Singapore investors, both the gold price and USD/SGD determine the unhedged return. Bank forecasts also have different dates and horizons. Market snapshot Spot gold traded at US$4,047.19/oz on 6 November at 15:18 Singapore time. Reuters Current section Overview 01 · Official demand 02 · How to read the data 03 · Disclosed buyers 04 · Disclosed sellers 05 · Reading the global register 06 · Historical reversals 07 · Case study · Ghana 08 · Reserve management 09 · Gold and US Treasuries 10 · The price of gold 11 · Market context 12 · Bank and agency outlooks 13 · Dated targets 14 · Reading the bank papers 15 · Singapore reserves 16 · Gold in Singapore dollars 17 · The currency translation 18 · The Singapore investor 19 · Portfolio decisions 20 · Reading guide Sources → A+ Dark Grey 01 Official demand Central banks bought more gold as the price weakened Reported facts Official buyers stepped up sharply after a weak first quarter. The November data show a net 57.7 tonnes in Q1, 296.3 in Q2 and 321.2 in Q3. The last figure was 42% above a year earlier. Yet the World Bank reports that gold prices fell 5% from Q2 to Q3. Data revision The estimate changed enough to alter the story of the year. The first Q1 release put buying at 244 tonnes. The Q2 release revised that sharply downward, and the November table puts it at 57.7. Combining April’s Q1 estimate with November’s Q2 and Q3 figures would exaggerate the level of demand and hide the rebound. Research interpretation Official demand is one influence on the market price. A reserve manager can add to a holding while other investors sell enough to push the price down. In plain English A large buyer can support demand while other investors sell enough to push the price down. Both sides of the market matter. XAU/USD World Bank Exhibit 01.1 · Reported and estimated data Official net purchases accelerated through 2026 Net metric tonnes by quarter · 3 November data release Q1 2026 57.7 t Q2 2026 296.3 t Q3 2026 321.2 t Exact figures in a table Measure Value Q1 2026 57.7 t Q2 2026 296.3 t Q3 2026 321.2 t Each bar starts at zero. Purchases less sales across central banks and other official institutions include estimated activity. Sources · WGC · 3 Nov 2026 [G1] · WGC / Metals Focus · 3 Nov 2026 [G2] Exhibit 01.2 · Reported and estimated data Price and purchasing moved in opposite directions Q3 versus Q2 2026 · changes as published Measure Quarter-on-quarter change Official gold demand +8% Gold price, World Bank review −5% The observations describe the same quarter. They do not measure the price effect of an individual purchase. Sources · WGC · 3 Nov 2026 [G1] · World Bank · Oct 2026 [W1] Evidence · G1 G2 G6 G7 W1 Next ↓ 02 How to read the data Who bought the remaining gold? Source estimate Public filings identify only part of Q3 buying. The World Gold Council puts disclosed net purchases at 120 tonnes, compared with roughly 321 tonnes after Metals Focus incorporates estimates. The gap covers late reporting and trades that never appear in time for publication. It cannot be reliably assigned to China , a Gulf state or another named buyer. Coverage comparison The answer to “is buying up this year?” depends on the series. For January to September, reported purchases fell 7% year on year to 228 tonnes. Estimated demand rose 6% to 675 tonnes. Both comparisons can be right because their coverage differs. A monthly change in disclosed reserves is evidence about that balance sheet, while imports can also reflect households, jewellers, banks and funds. In plain English The total estimate is larger than the list of named buyers. Keep that unknown portion visible when explaining who bought gold. XAU/USD Reported series Exhibit 02.1 · Reported and estimated data About 63% of Q3 net demand was unreported Approximate decomposition · net metric tonnes · July–September 2026 Disclosed · 120 t Estimated remainder · about 201 t Exact figures in a table Measure Value Disclosed 120 t Estimated remainder about 201 t The remainder uses source-rounded figures, 321 less 120. It has no reliable country-by-country breakdown. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus · 3 Nov 2026 [G2] Exhibit 02.2 · Reported and estimated data The reporting perimeter changes the year-on-year conclusion January–September 2026 · net metric tonnes Coverage 2026 Year on year Publicly reported 228 t −7% Reported plus estimated 675 t +6% The two rows overlap. Adding them would count publicly reported activity twice. Sources · WGC / Metals Focus · 3 Nov 2026 [G2] · WGC · 4 Nov 2026 [G3] Evidence · G1 G2 G3 Next ↓ 03 Disclosed buyers China picked up the pace as Poland approached its target Reported fact China added 63 tonnes in Q3, more than half its purchases for the first nine months. Its September statement gives a direct check on the quantity. Holdings rose by 740,000 ounces to 77.47 million ounces, the 23rd consecutive monthly increase. The announcement gives no price target or motive for that month’s purchase. Reported fact Poland’s governor confirmed on 5 November that reserves had reached the 700-tonne goal. Quarterly additions slowed from 51 tonnes in Q2 to 40 tonnes in Q3. He left open further purchases as overall reserves grow. Source commentary Uzbekistan illustrates how purchases can coexist with a willingness to sell. The central bank added 14 tonnes in Q3. Its governor had discussed selling at favourable prices as part of reserve management. A willingness to sell gives the bank flexibility and leaves the timing open. In plain English China accelerated its buying, while Poland reached a stated goal. The next purchase depends on each institution’s policy. Reading guide The most useful papers look at different parts of the gold market. The IMF authors study what a reserve manager can do with bullion in a crisis. The ECB and Federal Reserve papers test how much of the rise in gold’s reported importance comes from prices and existing holdings. Bank outlooks focus more closely on the marginal buyer and the next few quarters. Source scope The silver and renminbi papers help define the limits of the gold argument. J.P. OCBC’s November renminbi note concerns its currency outlook, and its sustainability weekly covers other policy developments. Neither establishes the identity of an undisclosed gold buyer. entries.text: CPF LIFE & RA Modelling Lab | Market Intel MARKET INTEL / TOOLS CPF · Singapore Jade Retirement maths · Standalone modelling tool Build the balance. Understand the income. Explore CPF Retirement Account growth, the effect of a top-up, and what different CPF LIFE income patterns mean over a long retirement. Public educational tool · Rules checked 6 November 2026 · All amounts in SGD Three numbers. Three different meanings. RA interest grows savings before payouts. CPF LIFE pays income for life. The remaining premium is a separate inheritance component. This independent model does not generate a CPF quotation. Its starting payouts are assumptions that you can replace with current CPF estimates. 01 · RA growth 02 · Lifetime income 03 · How it works Sources & limits Current RA base rate · Oct–Dec 2026 4.00% p.a. Current floor extended to end-2027. A constant future rate remains a model assumption. Extra interest · Age 55 and above Up to S$900/year 2% on the first S$30,000, then 1% on the next S$30,000 of eligible combined balances. 2026 Enhanced Retirement Sum S$440,800 Top-up eligibility is account-specific. This tool does not calculate your available headroom. 01 / BEFORE PAYOUTS What does an extra top-up add? Compare the same RA with and without a one-off top-up. Nothing here assumes how much extra CPF LIFE payout that top-up would buy. Age at model start Whole years; this is a pre-payout model. Age at payout start 65 to 70, no earlier than model start. Starting RA balance (S$) Hypothetical balance, before this top-up. One-off initial top-up (S$) Illustrative; confirm eligibility with CPF. Assumed annual base rate (%) Held constant in this scenario, not a forecast. Include RA-only extra interest A modelling switch, not an opt-out from actual CPF interest. Other accounts are excluded. Update RA model Reset RA example Annual, simplified periods: the top-up earns a full first model year's interest. Actual CPF uses monthly balances and calendar-year crediting; contributions start earning interest the following month. Two balances, the same assumptions With top-up Without top-up How to read: the gap is the top-up plus its additional modelled interest. Both lines are hypothetical, not your CPF statement. Balance by model age Before CPF LIFE premium deduction. Display rounded to dollars; full precision is retained in the calculation. RA formula and exclusions Next balance = balance × (1 + base rate) + extra interest RA-only extra = 2% × min(balance, 30,000) + 1% × min(max(balance − 30,000, 0), 30,000) The formula is recalculated each complete year. Extra interest is capped at S$900/year here. Actual extra interest uses combined balances, prioritising RA (including CPF LIFE premium), with OA eligibility capped at S$20,000. This pre-payout model excludes OA/MA balances and extra OA interest that could flow into RA. No monthly contributions, later top-ups, withdrawals, tax relief, matching grants, transfers, rate changes or CPF LIFE membership before the chosen start age. A projected balance exceeding the ERS does not itself mean a top-up is allowed or prohibited; logged-in CPF headroom is authoritative. Sources: interest timing · extra-interest allocation . Scenario data generated from the inputs above; model edition 6 Nov 2026. 02 / AFTER PAYOUTS BEGIN Income for a long life Compare a level starting payout with a separate payout rising 2% each year. Enter both starting amounts from matching CPF estimates, or keep the visibly hypothetical examples. Separate from the RA model. Changing RA inputs does not generate or update a payout quote. These starting payouts and premium are independent assumptions, not matched CPF quotations or a recommendation between plans. Payout start age Compare through age A scenario horizon, not a life-expectancy forecast. Illustrative LIFE premium (S$) For the remaining-premium diagram only. Level starting payout (S$/month) Hypothetical Standard-pattern example. Escalating starting payout (S$/month) Hypothetical example; increases 2% annually. Assumed inflation (% p.a.) Purchasing power is measured at payout-start prices. Update income model Reset income example Monthly income in payout-start dollars Level pattern 2% escalating pattern How to read: this is purchasing power, not the amount paid into your bank. The same nominal payment buys less as prices rise. Cumulative nominal income received Level pattern 2% escalating pattern These are amounts paid out over time, not money still held in an account. They are not an investment yield or a cash balance. Remaining premium is a different number Level pattern 2% escalating pattern Lifelong payouts continue even when this illustration reaches zero. Simplified unspent premium = max(0, initial premium − cumulative nominal payouts). This is not total bequest, accessible cash or surrender value. It excludes other CPF balances, adjustments and later premiums. Read the numbers together Each row is at the birthday, before the next payment. “Real” is monthly payout purchasing power. “Paid” is cumulative nominal payouts. “Remaining” is simplified unspent premium. Income formulas and valuation timing Level monthly amount at year n = starting level payout Escalating monthly amount at year n = starting escalating payout × 1.02ⁿ Real monthly amount = nominal amount ÷ (1 + inflation)ⁿ Year 0 is the payout-start birthday, before any payment. Each completed year has 12 equal monthly payments; escalation happens on each anniversary. At age 85 with payouts from 65, the cumulative total includes exactly 240 payments, and the displayed monthly amount is the next year's rate. Real amounts are measured in payout-start purchasing power, not today's prices. CPF LIFE payout amounts depend on member-specific actuarial factors and can be adjusted for long-term changes in interest rates or life expectancy. This arithmetic holds the supplied level amount fixed and the supplied escalating amount on a 2% path; it cannot replicate CPF's actuarial engine. It does not calculate an IRR or a “best” death age. Sources: CPF Standard Plan , Escalating Plan and premium mechanics . All chart values are calculated scenarios, not official benefit estimates. 03 / THE MONEY FLOW Why 4% interest is not a 4% payout yield 1. Retirement Account Savings and eligible top-ups earn RA interest before CPF LIFE starts. 2. LIFE premium For Standard and Escalating, RA savings are used as the annuity premium when payouts start. 3. Monthly income Payouts include use of premium and support from the lifelong risk pool. Income continues for life. 4. On death Any remaining premium plus remaining CPF account savings is distributed to beneficiaries. The pooled interest supports longevity Interest earned on CPF LIFE premiums is pooled to support lifelong payouts. It does not appear as a separately compounding pot that can simply be added to your individual bequest. CPF LIFE is backed by the Singapore Government. This independent page and its figures are not official CPF projections. Basic Plan is deliberately not simulated Basic uses only part of RA savings as premium, with different account drawdown and payout mechanics. Applying the same simple remaining-premium curve would mislead. See the official Basic Plan explanation . This page makes no numerical comparison with private insurance products. 04 / SOURCE DISCIPLINE Know what is assumed before using the result Use this page to understand the maths. Use CPF for a personalised estimate. No login, identity information or account connection is needed here. Inputs are calculated in this page and are not sent to an analytics or calculation service; reloading resets them. Open official CPF LIFE guidance ↗ Read the related research ↗ Download model CSV Print / save PDF CSV and PDF are user-initiated downloads on your device. Exported values may contain any hypothetical or personal amounts you enter; decide who to share them with. Current CPF interest rates · Oct–Dec 2026 RA rate floor through 31 December 2027 Monthly interest calculation and annual crediting Extra-interest tiers and account order Enhanced Retirement Sum · S$440,800 in 2026 Top-up limits and eligibility Payout start ages: 65–70 Factors behind CPF LIFE payouts Model and design notes Edition: 6 November 2026. All defaults are teaching scenarios, not client records. No current financial product prices, insurer projections, tax optimisation or eligibility determinations are embedded. Colour & Tagging Standard V1.2 Merged workbook checked 6 Nov 2026: CPF and RA retain Singapore Jade (#047857); comparisons use written labels and solid/dashed lines rather than new semantic colours. Independent educational model. Not personalised financial, insurance or tax advice, and not affiliated with CPF Board. Rules and personal estimates can change. Verify current official figures before making an irreversible top-up. Back to Market Intel Tools .
